title: Deputy Editor in Chief, Chalkbeat
description:
Location: Remote

Reports to: Editor in Chief, Chalkbeat

Type: Full-time

Salary Range: $130,000 - $145,000 per year, depending on location and experience


Civic News Company is leading a civic revival.


We were founded to address one of the most consequential market failures of our time: the collapse of local news. Since 2008, nearly two-thirds of U.S. newsroom jobs have disappeared, leaving communities without trusted reporting on education, elections, and public health. Our mission is simple and urgent: to help people understand how America works so they can make it work better.


Through Chalkbeat (education), Votebeat (elections), and Healthbeat (public health), we operate a national network of local news bureaus that combine deep local expertise with centralized national infrastructure.


THE OPPORTUNITY

Civic News is seeking a Deputy Editor in Chief to support our journalists and boost our newsroom leadership capacity. In this newly created role, Chalkbeat’s Deputy will partner with the Editor in Chief to set and execute the editorial vision for the newsroom. In addition, they will oversee several reporting teams and collaborate with the Managing Editors and Bureau Chiefs to extend a clear vision forward. The role will blend day-to-day journalism guidance with big-picture strategic thinking for key newsroom projects.


As Chalkbeat enters its next phase of growth, our most important metric will remain impact — so a successful candidate will have experience in developing must-read stories that reach wide audiences and drive discussion and change. They will also be an experienced and inspiring newsroom leader with a strong track record of project planning, change management, and experimentation.


The key responsibilities for this role include:

  • Working with the Editor in Chief to set the vision as Chalkbeat enters a new phase of growth and ensure it’s being carried out.

  • Overseeing several of our current local bureaus and reporting teams, with a focus on ensuring that Chalkbeat coverage drives impact in the form of informed decision-making and debate.

  • Coaching leaders on setting and achieving goals, monitoring progress, and supporting their team members’ professional growth.

  • Supporting the implementation of Civic News Academy.

  • Working on high-priority initiatives, including but not limited to impact tracking improvements, further development of a newsroom AI strategy, and future geographic expansion.

  • Collaborating closely with our growth and community team to expand our loyal audience.

  • Ensuring enterprise projects are deeply compelling and well executed.

  • Serving as a newsroom leader, representing organizational priorities to local teams and vice versa.


What background and skills do you have? (We know not all strong candidates will have all the skills we list. That’s OK. What else do you bring to the table? Please tell us!): The person we seek:

  • 10+ years of work experience, including leadership experience.

  • Experience reporting and editing breaking news, daily, and enterprise stories.

  • A track record of leading effective teams with inspiration, high standards, and accountability, including experience coaching employees at different experience levels.

  • A track record of managing complex projects, from initial vision to developing the processes that make them sustainable.

  • Experience developing editorial strategy and building an audience.

  • A deep knowledge of America’s education story paired with curiosity about its future.


Here are our Civic News Values and how they show up in our work together:

  • We work as one team.
    Rebuilding local news requires collaboration. We actively nurture a harmonious environment of dignity, respect, and professionalism. We assume good intent, support one another’s growth, and have a team-oriented approach to solving problems together.

  • We pursue truth with intellectual honesty.
    Our work demands rigor. We seek facts, challenge assumptions, and engage thoughtfully with perspectives different from our own. We follow the evidence wherever it leads.

  • We practice inclusive journalism.
    Strong civic life depends on representation and trust. We commit to antiracism, equity, and inclusive practices. We build meaningful relationships with the communities we serve and reflect their realities in our reporting.

  • We earn trust every day.
    We develop subject-matter expertise. We operate transparently. We take responsibility for our work and keep learning so our journalism remains credible, relevant, and strong.

This full-time, remote-eligible position may be based anywhere in the continental United States. Civic News Company already has a presence in Chicago, Colorado, Indianapolis, Newark, Pennsylvania, Arizona, Texas, Michigan, Tennessee, New York City, and Washington, D.C.


The salary range is $130,000 to 145,000; final salary will be determined based on level of experience and geographic location, with a generous benefits package, including:

  • Medical, vision, and dental insurance

  • Time off that truly supports rest, including 20 days of PTO, a paid one-week recess, 5 sick days, 3 floating holidays, and 12 paid holidays in 2026

  • Retirement support through a 401(k) with a 4% employer match that is immediately vested

  • 100% paid parental leave: 18 weeks fully paid, plus a 2-week part-time return-to-work ramp-up

  • Flexible Spending Plan for eligible medical or childcare expenses

  • Annual professional development stipend

  • Employer-provided life insurance and short- and long-term disability coverage

  • Monthly reimbursement for cell phone and internet expenses


Civic News Company recognizes a staff bargaining unit, Civic News Company, affiliated with the Writers Guild of America, East, a labor union representing thousands of members who write content for news and online media, motion pictures, and television. This position is not included in the Civic News Company bargaining unit.


Physical Requirements of the Job

This role is primarily sedentary and involves extended periods of sitting and regular use of standard office equipment, including computers and phones, for up to 8 hours per day. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position.

Civic News Company Commitment

Civic News Company is committed to building a diverse, equitable, and inclusive organization. We believe restoring civic trust requires a plurality of voices, backgrounds, and experiences. Civic News Company is committed to equal employment opportunities and welcomes applicants and employees from diverse backgrounds, including but not limited to races, colors, national origins, ancestries, creeds, religions, genders, ages, disabilities, veteran status, sexual orientations, and marital statuses. We encourage individuals of all backgrounds to apply and contribute to our shared vision.


Civic News Company participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S. If E-Verify cannot confirm that you are authorized to work, Civic News Company is required to give you written instructions and an opportunity to contact Department of Homeland Security (DHS) or Social Security Administration (SSA) so you can begin to resolve the issue before Civic News Company can take any action against you, including terminating your employment. Civic News Company can only use E-Verify once you have accepted a job offer and completed the Form I-9.

title: Technical Project Manager III
description:
ABOUT

Firefly Aerospace is a space and defense technology company on a mission to reliably and repeatedly launch, land, and operate space systems from Earth to the Moon and beyond. As the partner of choice for critical space missions, Firefly is the first commercial company to launch a satellite to orbit with 24-hour notice and the first company to achieve a successful Moon landing. Headquartered in north Austin, Texas, Firefly is looking for passionate, hardworking innovators to join our team and help fuel our successful trajectory into space.

SUMMARY

As a Technical Project Manager in Firefly’s Aerospace Software Engineering department, you will own the planning, scheduling, and execution rhythm for software development across all of Firefly’s Launch Vehicles programs. You will report to the Director of Aerospace Software Engineering and serve as the programmatic arm of the department, covering Flight Software, Ground Software, and Guidance, Navigation and Control (GNC) for launch vehicles programs.

This is a hands-on role. You will build and maintain integrated schedules that span software and hardware milestones, keep department development programs and IRAD efforts visible, and make sure software commitments to vehicle programs are real, tracked, and closed. You will work directly with software engineering leads and subject matter experts to translate technical input into executable plans and maintain the documentation and risk posture needed for program success. Cross-functional communication and coordination with hardware teams, test engineering, and vehicle programs is essential to this role.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Build and maintain integrated schedules for software development, spanning all vehicle-level programs and internal IRAD.
  • Coordinate across software and hardware teams to ensure integrated schedules reflect critical dependencies, hardware delivery dates, and test bench availability.
  • Manage schedules, backlogs, and risks for software teams across Flight Software, Ground Software, and Guidance, Navigation and Control (GNC).
  • Support the Director in staffing and resource planning by maintaining a clear, data-driven picture of department capacity against program demand.
  • Maintain schedules covering System Requirements Reviews (SRR), Preliminary Design Reviews (PDR), Critical Design Reviews (CDR), qualification and acceptance test campaigns, and flight readiness milestones.
  • Support documentation preparation for design reviews and program gates, aggregating inputs from engineers and functional leads.
  • Tie software delivery dates to team capacity, dependencies, hardware availability, and integration and test bench readiness so plans reflect real constraints and hardware-software integration points.
  • Interface with vehicle Program Management to surface programmatic and technical issues early and drive them to resolution.
  • Track and manage department risks, mitigation plans, and action items to closure.
  • Maintain and automate program metrics dashboards.
  • Facilitate sprint planning, stand-ups, and retrospectives for software teams using Agile or hybrid workflows.
  • Maintain project information and visibility using the Atlassian Suite (Jira, Confluence).

QUALIFICATIONS

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree in a technical field such as engineering, computer science, or similar.
  • 5+ years of experience in technical project management or program integration for complex engineering systems.
  • Demonstrated success building and maintaining integrated schedules for software development in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail in maintaining schedules, risks, and review materials.
  • Basic proficiency in Python and SQL for data analysis, automation, or reporting.
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills, capable of distilling technical details into clear, actionable plans.
  • Proven ability to collaborate across multiple engineering disciplines and with internal customers including Program Management.

Desired

  • Aerospace or space systems experience, particularly in Flight Software, Ground Software, Guidance, Navigation and Control (GNC) systems, or spacecraft operations.
  • Strong cross-functional communication skills with demonstrated ability to coordinate between software, hardware, and test engineering teams.
  • Proficiency with Atlassian tools: Jira (issue tracking, dashboards, reports) and Confluence (documentation, templates, macros).
  • Experience managing schedules through qualification and acceptance test campaigns.
  • Experience managing development in a hardware-constrained environment where delivery depends on board, bench, or vehicle availability.
  • Familiarity with system-level design reviews and program lifecycle processes.
  • Experience integrating Agile practices within a systems engineering or hardware-centric organization.
  • Understanding of configuration management, documentation control, and technical baseline maintenance.
  • Exposure to proposal writing, cost estimating, or budget tracking.
  • Working knowledge of embedded software, real-time operating systems, or hardware-in-the-loop test environments.

Firefly offers outstanding benefits for our employees, including generous health, dental and vision plans with low plan deductibles, parental leave, educational reimbursement, short term disability, and flexible PTO options.

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

Firefly Aerospace, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with Firefly is governed based on merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status

title: Head of Clinic
description:
Introduction

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

Applications are welcome from internal and external candidates. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process. For the purpose of this vacancy, internal and internal-equivalent candidates as well as external women candidates are considered as first-tier candidates.

Organizational Context and Scope

Under the overall supervision of the Regional Health Assessment Programme Coordinator (RHAPC) and the direct supervision of the Chief Migration Health Officer (CMHO) OR Under the overall and direct supervision of the Chief of Mission (COM) and the technical supervision of the (Deputy) Regional Health Assessment Programme Coordinator, and in close coordination with the National Health Operations Officer, the successful candidate will be responsible for the management of the Migration Health Assessment Centre (MHAC) in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

  1. Health Assessment Portfolio

    Clinical

    1. Organize and supervise CITY MHAC’s migration health assessment process to fulfill the technical requirements of the resettlement countries in the areas of:

      • Medical examinations;
      • Imaging;
      • Laboratory testing;
      • Vaccinations;
      • TB management;
      • Treatment and referrals;
      • Pre-departure procedures and medical movements;
      • Documentation, certification and information transmission; and,
      • Other technical areas as may be required.

    2. Conduct health assessment for refugees and migrants, including review of medical history, physical examination, evaluation of Chest X-ray (CXR) and review of the lab results in accordance with the technical guidelines of the resettlement countries.

    3. Maintain the infrastructure and equipment of MHAC premises including infrastructure and equipment of HAP premises so that they meet the professional standards of quality and safety and are sufficient and adequate for provision of the services.

    4. Coordinate with the CMHO if present or lead the coordination efforts in the country office to ensure human resources and MHAC organizational structure needs are sufficient and adequate for the planned levels of health assessments and that staff has necessary qualifications and skills. These efforts include the creation and continual review of the network of external human resources, such as consultants and medical escorts, to support health assessment process and travel assistance to ensure operational flexibility.

    5. Contribute to/lead and maintain efficient, client-centered procedures while ensuring a high level of integrity at all stages of the MHAC’s process, including client information and appointment system, payment, registration, pre- and post-test counselling, examination, testing, treatment and referrals, submission of health assessment results, pre-departure and other procedures. Establish within MHAC a system enabling clients to provide feedback.

    6. Contribute to/lead and maintain a system of quality improvement for each service area within the MHAC. Undertake quality control activities on a regular basis, including practice observation, desk audits and use of self-assessment tools. Use data analysis and web reporting system to monitor performance indicators. Ensure implementation of the global IOM Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs); create and implement CITY MHAC specific SOPs for each service area. Ensure proper reporting and management of incidents according to the Guidance Note for Incident Management.

    7. Collaborate with the CMHO (if present) or lead the efforts to incorporate additional public health interventions in the HAP context. Interventions may include surveillance for communicable diseases, outbreak preparedness and response, health education and health promotion, public health services for host communities, liaison with public health institutions and other activities.

    8. Operations (in coordination with the National Health Operations Officer)

    9. Ensure that the COM and CMHO (if present) or the technical supervisor at the regional level is informed about the MHAC’s health activities and that the IOM medical facilities have obtained approval to provide health assessments and related services.

    10. Supervise clinical- and non-clinical staff as well as external consultants in the MHAC involved in the health assessment process; ensure that performance evaluations for health staff are completed in a timely manner. Ensure that all staff are aware of the IOM Standards of Conduct under Article 42, and continuously reinforce these standards. Inform in due time the CoM and the IOM Office of Ethics and conduct of any issues regarding staff misconduct.

    11. Establish the MHAC staff development strategy in coordination with the CMHO if present, ensure that the appropriate plan is implemented. Within that plan, apart from attendance to external educational events, initiate, contribute to the organization and delivery of various professional in-house trainings.

    12. Liaise with external service providers to negotiate agreements in coordination with Resources Management Officer (RMO). Exercise quality control over outsourced services and take corrective measures if necessary.

    13. Provide oversight and coordinate the procurement of medical equipment, vaccines, medications and other medical supplies in coordination with the CMHO and the resource management unit.

    14. Financial and other data

    15. Maintain confidentiality and security of migration health data in accordance with the IOM Data Protection Principles.

    16. Organize systematic collection, processing and analyses of migration health data according to guidelines established by the CMHO. Ensure data quality. Provide periodic, as well as ad-hoc reporting to the CMHO for migration health activities.

    17. Oversee the financial aspects of the MHAC in close coordination with the mission's finance staff: supervise budget preparation, suggest adjustments and cost-effective solutions, and review financial reports.

    18. Other health activities

    19. Facilitate the integration of health assessment activities into the overall migration related programming of the Mission in CITY through close collaboration with the various units at the Country Office level.

    20. Advise IOM colleagues on the link between the HAP with the two other core MHD programme areas - Health Promotion and Assistance to Migrants and Migration Health Assistance to Crisis-Affected Populations.

    21. Perform such other duties as may be assigned by the direct supervisor.

Required Qualifications and Experience

Education

    • University degree in Medicine from an accredited academic institution with preferred specializations: internal medicine and its subspecialties, pediatrics, anesthesiology, emergency medicine, family medicine, obstetrics and gynecology; and minimum of seven (7) years of relevant professional experience of which at least three (3) years managerial responsibilities,

    • OR

    • University degree in Medicine from an accredited academic institution with preferred specializations: internal medicine and its subspecialties, pediatrics, anesthesiology, emergency medicine, family medicine, obstetrics and gynecology plus Master’s Degree in Community or Public Health, Medical Specialization in Infectious Diseases, Tropical Medicine or other related fields from an accredited academic institution with five (5) years of relevant professional experience of which at least three (3) years managerial responsibilities.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

Experience

  • Professional continuous clinical experience, preferably in a multidisciplinary hospital setting or at IOM/similar international clinic context;

  • Experience in Migration Heath Assessments;

  • Demonstrated progressive experience in health programme management;

  • Experience in project development, management and report writing;

  • Proven abilities to establish partnerships with government institutions, health institutions and other partners;

  • Knowledge of public health;

  • Demonstrable knowledge of patient safety and infection prevention and control;

  • Experience in migration health emergency response is an asset

  • Proven expertise or post-graduate diploma/degree in clinical specialization in the fields of pediatrics, pulmonology, or emergency medicine is an advantage.

  • Proven expertise or post-graduate diploma/degree in clinical specialization in the fields of internal medicine is an advantage.

  • Proven expertise and/or specialization in public health, health care administration, or healthcare management is an advantage.

  • Proven master trainer experience is an advantage.

Skills

  • Proficiency in managing healthcare facilities, including patient care and administrative tasks

  • Effective budgeting, financial reporting, and managing resources effectively

  • Proficiency in using software for managing clinic administration.

  • Proven excellent communication and interpersonal skills to interact with staff, patients, and other stakeholders.

  • Ability to lead and motivate a team, ensuring high performance and morale.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills to address issues and implement solutions efficiently.

  • Efficient customer Service and the ability to handle clinic operation and administration issues effectively.

  • Excellent organizational skills to manage multiple tasks and responsibilities simultaneously.

Languages

All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish).

For this position, for all applicants, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

Required Competencies

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

  • Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.

  • Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.

  • Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.

  • Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.

  • Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

Core Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2

  • Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.

  • Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.

  • Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.

  • Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.

  • Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

Managerial Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2, if with direct reports

  • Leadership: Provides a clear sense of direction, leads by example and demonstrates the ability to carry out the Organization’s vision. Assists others to realize and develop their leadership and professional potential.

  • Empowering others: Creates an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential.

  • Building Trust: Promotes shared values and creates an atmosphere of trust and honesty.

  • Strategic thinking and vision: Works strategically to realize the Organization’s goals and communicates a clear strategic direction.

  • Humility: Leads with humility and shows openness to acknowledging own shortcomings.

Notes

Please refer to this link for guidance on IOM Job Category.

Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.

This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months.

Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, security clearances.

IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities.

IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts.

IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM e-Recruitment system (for internal candidates link here). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application.

No late applications will be accepted. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: IOM Careers and Job Vacancies

title: Quality & Compliance Specialist
location: Corporate Office, San Francisco, CA, US
description:
PRC Baker Places is a non-profit organization dedicated to serving the San Francisco community through legal advocacy, workforce development, financial services, and residential treatment programs. We support formerly homeless adults living with co-occurring mental health and substance use disorders by providing a continuum of integrated direct care services. All of our programs are grounded in a social rehabilitation philosophy that integrates harm reduction and daily living skills within a safe and supportive environment.

title: Plant In-charge (RMC)
description:
A merger of experience and expertise, Dalmia is the pioneer and leader in innovation for the last seven decades. Our growth story is the effort of our people and our management. We have cement plants in southern states of Tamil Nadu (Dalmiapuram & Ariyalur) and Andhra Pradesh (Kadapa), with a capacity of 9 million tonnes per annum. A leader in cement manufacturing since 1939, DCBL is a multi spectrum Cement player with double digit market share and a pioneer in super specialty cements used for Oil wells, Railway sleepers and Air strips. We also hold a stake of 45.4 % in OCL India Ltd., a major cement Player in the Eastern Region. Recently we have acquired the brands Adhunik Cement & Calcom Cement in the North East and the group now controls an expandable cement capacity of 21.8 million tonnes including the new project incubated at Belgaum in Karnataka.

What makes us unique is our constant ability to innovate. On the key efficiency parameters, we rank right up there with the best in the industry. We have set up over 53 windmills in Muppandal (Tamil Nadu) to generate inexpensive and eco-friendly captive power for our plant. This power is wheeled through the State utility transporter for consumption at the plant.

With the plant located close to its source of raw materials, we keep our freight and transport costs low, giving it an edge over competition. Over 65 per cent of the cement consumption in India is catered to by the retail segment where branding and distribution are the critical drivers for leadership. And it is in this that we enjoy an edge over our competitors. We are the only single unit cement manufacturer to successfully market our brands in core markets at prices on par with those of large consolidated/national players. In our focus area of Tamil Nadu and Kerala, which are among the fastest growing in cement consumption, we enjoy a significant market share today. Our brands enjoy a very high recall among consumers and influencers while our relationships with our dealers are very strong. In fact, in some cases these relationships go back three generations.

Our USP is innovation, which has given us a leadership position in niche but fast-growing market segments.

title: Reliability Engineer
description:
Reliability Engineer

Department: Production

Job Status: Full-Time

Classification: Exempt

Reports To: Maintenance & Reliability Manager

Salary Range: DOE Direct Reports: None

Company Overview:

Douglas Products has pioneered manufacturing and marketing specialty products, focusing on high-quality brands in the global agriculture production and structural pest control markets for over 100 years. With a legacy built on partnership, innovation, and expertise, we are the market leader in structural and post-harvest agricultural fumigation, offering unparalleled solutions in drywood termite control through our flagship products, Vikane® and ProFume®. Our commitment to quality, stewardship, and regulatory excellence drives our mission to protect and enhance business value for our customers worldwide.

Summary:

The Reliability Engineer provides front-line reliability and maintenance engineering support to ensure safe, complaint, and efficient operation of equipment and processes. This role drives asset performance through preventive and predictive maintenance strategies, root cause analysis, and data-driven decision-making while supporting Mechanical Integrity and Risk-Based Inspection (RBI) programs in alignment with RMP/PSM requirements and industry standards. The position partners closely with operations, maintenance, and EHS teams to improve reliability, maintain accurate equipment documentation, and ensure work is executed in accordance with regulatory and internal requirements. Additional responsibilities include optimizing spare parts strategies, supporting CMMS (Maximo) reporting and analysis, and contributing to both small- and large-scale projects to enhance long-term equipment reliability and performance.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Establish, implement, and continuously improve preventive and predictive maintenance programs to optimize equipment reliability and reduce unplanned downtime.
  • Drive equipment reliability through root cause analysis, performance monitoring, and implementation of corrective and preventive actions.
  • Lead and support Mechanical Integrity and Risk-Based Inspection (RBI) programs to ensure compliance with regulatory and company standards.
  • Partner with maintenance and operations to improve job planning, work execution, and field readiness, ensuring work is completed safely, efficiently, and accurately.
  • Analyze and optimize spare parts inventory and MRO strategies to ensure critical part availability while managing cost and efficiency.
  • Utilize CMMS (Maximo) to track, analyze, and report on maintenance performance metrics, enabling data-driven decision-making.
  • Maintain and improve engineering standards, technical documentation, and equipment records to ensure accuracy, consistency, and compliance.
  • Provide reliability engineering support for capital projects, including equipment selection, design input, and startup/commissioning support.
  • Collaborate with EHS and operations teams to ensure all reliability activities align with safety, environmental, and regulatory requirements.

Education:

Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Chemical, or related engineering field required.

Experience:

  • Minimum of 5 years of experience in reliability, maintenance, or process engineering within an industrial or manufacturing environment.
  • Experience working in regulated environments (e.g., PSM/RMP) preferred.

Technical Knowledge & Skills:

  • Strong understanding of mechanical systems including pumps, piping, valves, and rotating equipment.
  • Experience with preventive and predictive maintenance strategies, including condition monitoring techniques (e.g., vibration analysis, oil analysis, thermography).
  • Knowledge of root cause analysis methodologies and continuous improvement practices.
  • Familiarity with Mechanical Integrity programs and applicable industry standards (e.g., API, ASME).
  • Understanding of Management of Change (MOC) processes and reliability-centered maintenance principles.
  • Ability to read and interpret P&IDs, process flow diagrams, and engineering drawings.

Systems & Tools:

  • Proficiency with CMMS systems (IBM Maximo or similar).
  • Strong Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel for data analysis and reporting.
  • Familiarity with EHS systems (e.g., Intelex) preferred.

Competencies:

  • Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects and priorities in a fast-paced environment
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex technical information to diverse audiences
  • High level of adaptability and problem-solving skills, with the ability to operate effectively in dynamic and evolving environments
  • Ability to collaborate across functions and organizational levels to drive results
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret data and support decision-making
  • Demonstrated commitment to safety, regulatory compliance, and continuous improvement

  • Able to work collaboratively across cultures and with individuals of diverse backgrounds.
  • Able to work effectively both in a team environment and independently.

Deliver weatherization auditing and inspection services in accordance with federal, state, local and utility standards. Perform occasional work involving installation of weatherization measures. Conduct training in proper installation of weatherization measures. Perform administrative work in an office setting. Assist in the development and delivery of Energy Education workshops.

  • Conduct detailed energy audits on residential structures. Enter collected data into home energy performance analysis software to determine cost/benefit analysis.
  • Administer diagnostic testing on all audited homes, including building and duct air leakage, static pressures, air handler performance, combustion appliance exhaust and draft testing, lead paint testing, and carbon monoxide testing. Collect samples when asbestos is suspected and submit them for testing.
  • Identify health and safety issues.
  • Make recommendations to management regarding selection of weatherization measures.
  • Submit applications and reports to the state and other partner entities.
  • Assist with administrative file work when needed.
  • Perform brief pre-audit home inspections.
  • Oversee contractor work through periodic inspections while jobs are in progress.
  • Serve as primary point of contact for contractors with technical needs or questions.
  • Support contractor work by offering hands-on or document-based training in areas where contractor knowledge or skill deficiencies are present.
  • Provide customer service to clients regarding matters such as job progress, feedback or questions regarding contractors, and education about weatherization measures.
  • Perform 6-month follow-up visits with clients to hear and address any concerns with completed work.
  • Collaborate with administrative staff in matters such as contractor scheduling and bid and work order issuance.
  • Abide by all compliance principles issued by Federal, State and Local rules and regulations relevant to client eligibility, file maintenance, audit and inspection standards, performance codes, and installation of acceptable weatherization measures and products.
  • Maintain tools and diagnostic equipment.
  • Ensure periodic maintenance schedules are met and perform safety checks for departmental vehicles.
  • Serve on agency safety committee.
  • Attend trainings to obtain certification requirements, learn new innovative technology, and incorporate new methods in our delivery of weatherization services.
  • Assist with the development and delivery of energy conservation training courses including the proper installation of self-help materials.
  • Read, analyze and interpret general business periodicals, professional journals, technical procedures, building codes, blueprints, and weatherization specifications.
  • Performs other duties as assigned by the Weatherization Manager.

REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, ABILITIES AND MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skills, abilities, and minimum qualifications necessary to perform the essential functions of the position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • Associate degree in related field, or three years of comparable experience and/or training, or equivalent combination of education and experience. Must have or obtain Oregon Lead Safe Renovator Certification, within 90 days from date of hire.
  • Must have or obtain the following certifications within two years from date of hire: Oregon Residential Energy Analyst, Building Performance Institute residential energy auditor and quality control inspector, REM Design user, and all other certifications as deemed necessary to meet program requirements.
  • Ability to work in a team environment. Must interact with the public, staff, contractors, peers and state program representatives in an informative and professional manner.
  • Professionalism and workplace etiquette is expected when in the office and when conducting inspections/audits.
  • Must present a clean, neat, and tasteful appearance during business hours or when representing CAPECO.
  • Have a general knowledge of building techniques and weatherization materials.
  • Ability to abide by regulations.
  • Ability to travel out of area to attend training or deliver weatherization services.
  • Working knowledge of office equipment (i.e. copier, fax, etc.)
  • Strong computer skills in excel, word and outlook.
  • Technical knowledge and ability to operate mechanical tools.
  • Ability to communicate in a clear and concise manner; both orally and written with State officials, contractors, professional peers, clients and staff.
  • Operate diagnostic equipment (blower door, duct blaster, infrared camera, pressure diagnostics, moisture meters, gas detection equipment, combustion analyzer, etc.) as required to meet program guidelines. Experience preferred.

WORK ENVIRONMENT AND PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

The physical demand and work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of the job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to stand; walk; sit; use hands to finger, handle or feel; climb or balance; stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl; twist; bend; reach with hands and arms; talk and hear; use hands to manipulate. All audits require the employee to be in confined spaces such as crawl spaces under homes or in attics. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move objects of light to moderate weight (up to 50 pounds). Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision and distance vision.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently exposed to outside weather conditions (extreme heat and cold); moving mechanical parts; fumes or airborne particles; or risk of electrical shock. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Must pass a criminal history background investigation; however, a conviction of a crime may not necessarily disqualify an individual from this position.
  • CAPECO is a drug free workplace and pre-employment drug screening will be required. Due to federal funding, our drug screenings include the use of marijuana.

  • Travel may be required within the service area, including occasional out-of-town or overnight travel. Travel may require the use of a personal vehicle. Mileage for the business-related use of a personal vehicle will be reimbursed at the standard mileage rate as published per IRS guidelines.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

title: Mobile Facility Technician II
description:

title: International Consultant – Development of Minimum Operational, Protection and Technical Standards and Tools for Temporary Holding Centres for Migrants
description:
Introduction

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

Project Context and Scope

The consultancy will be implemented within the framework of the NORAD-funded regional project “Enhancing Protection of Migrants from Violence, Exploitation and Abuse in Central Asia”, implemented by IOM in Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan.
The project aims to strengthen protection systems for migrants in vulnerable situations through improved institutional capacities, access to protection services, regional cooperation and practical tools for identification, referral and response. Under Output 2.2, the project supports protection and essential service providers in accessing and applying practical tools, guidelines and procedures to effectively respond to the protection needs and rights of vulnerable migrants, including children and victims of trafficking.
In Uzbekistan, the need has been identified for practical standards and tools to support the organization, management and operation of temporary holding centres for migrants. Such facilities may accommodate migrants with different legal and operational statuses and therefore require both common minimum standards and, where relevant, differentiated procedures and safeguards appropriate to the circumstances of the individuals concerned.
The assignment will support the development of a comprehensive framework of minimum operational, protection and technical standards and practical tools for such facilities. The framework will address conditions and management of temporary holding, relevant operational procedures and differentiated regimes, while integrating mechanisms for early identification of vulnerabilities and specific protection needs, application of appropriate safeguards, and referral to existing protection and essential services.
Particular attention will be given to strengthening practical interfaces between the relevant authorities and existing protection and social service systems, including the National Agency for Social Protection, drawing where relevant on the findings of the national mapping of services and protection gaps for vulnerable migrants conducted under the project.
The standards and tools will be informed by applicable national requirements, relevant international standards and guidance, and comparative foreign good practices and operational models. The consultancy will further support their practical application through the development and pilot delivery of a competency-based training package and preparation of the finalized training content for subsequent conversion into a self-paced digital learning module.

Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing Migrants Assistance and Protection Unit, IOM Uzbekistan
Category B Consultant - Tasks to be performed under this contract – under the direct supervision of the National Project Officer (Protection) and overall coordination of the Chief of Mission (CoM)
The overall objective of this consultancy is to develop a comprehensive, practical and context-appropriate framework of minimum operational, protection and technical standards and tools for temporary holding centres for migrants in Uzbekistan, taking into account different legal and operational categories of migrants and applicable regimes of stay.
The framework will aim to support safe, humane and effective operation and management of such facilities, in line with applicable national requirements, international standards and relevant comparative foreign good practices, while strengthening mechanisms for the identification of migrants in vulnerable situations, application of appropriate safeguards, and referral to existing protection and essential services.
The consultancy will also develop and pilot a corresponding competency-based training package and prepare the finalized training content for subsequent conversion into a self-paced digital learning module.
To complete the assignment, the Consultant will carry out the following tasks:
Scope of Work
1. Review the applicable legal, institutional, international and comparative framework
• Review applicable national legislation, regulations and institutional arrangements governing the placement, temporary holding, return, removal, onward transfer and other relevant migration-related procedures in Uzbekistan.
• Review applicable international standards, principles and guidance concerning immigration detention and temporary holding, conditions of stay, facility management, procedural safeguards and protection of migrants in vulnerable situations.
• Review relevant comparative foreign good practices and operational models for the organization and management of temporary holding/detention facilities for migrants, including approaches to conditions of stay, differentiated regimes, vulnerability identification, referral and protection safeguards.
• Review available information on the existing and/or planned organization, management and operation of relevant facilities in Uzbekistan.
• Seek consultations, where feasible and subject to stakeholder availability, with the Ministry of Internal Affairs and other relevant institutions to clarify existing practices, operational needs and institutional responsibilities.
• Where consultations or relevant information are unavailable, use available documentation, information provided by IOM and other relevant sources and clearly identify resulting limitations.
• Take into account relevant findings of the national mapping of protection services and gaps for vulnerable migrants, where available.
2. Identify and structure applicable categories and regimes
• Identify the principal legal and operational categories of migrants who may be temporarily held in the relevant facilities, to the extent supported by applicable legislation, institutional arrangements and available information.
• Develop an operational framework distinguishing, as relevant:
o persons temporarily held pending execution of return, removal or deportation procedures from Uzbekistan;
o persons temporarily held pending onward transfer, return or another migration-related procedure;
o other relevant categories identified through the assessment.
• For each applicable category/regime, identify relevant procedures, institutional responsibilities, safeguards, documentation requirements and possible pathways/outcomes.
• Identify common requirements applicable irrespective of status and areas where differentiated procedures or safeguards are required.
3. Develop common minimum operational, protection and technical standards
Develop minimum standards applicable across the relevant regimes, covering, as appropriate:
• admission, registration and provision of information;
• dignity, non-discrimination and treatment;
• accommodation capacity and occupancy;
• minimum space and technical requirements;
• functional zoning and separation arrangements;
• sleeping and common areas;
• sanitation and hygiene;
• food, water and other basic needs;
• healthcare and emergency medical response;
• accessibility and reasonable accommodation;
• communication and contact arrangements;
• staffing, roles and responsibilities;
• internal management and workflows;
• safety, security and incident management;
• confidentiality and data protection;
• complaints and feedback;
• monitoring and quality assurance;
• transfer, release, removal and other relevant exit procedures.
The standards should draw on applicable national requirements, international standards and relevant comparative foreign good practices and be adapted to the institutional and operational context of Uzbekistan.
4. Develop a vulnerability identification and differentiated protection response framework
• Establish practical procedures for early identification of vulnerabilities and specific protection needs among persons admitted to the facilities.
• Provide for reassessment where protection needs or individual circumstances emerge or change during the person's stay.
• Define appropriate additional safeguards for relevant categories and circumstances, including children, victims of trafficking, persons affected by GBV, persons with disabilities, persons with urgent health or psychosocial needs and other migrants in vulnerable situations.
• Identify circumstances requiring specialized assessment, additional safeguards, intervention by another competent authority and/or referral to appropriate services.
• Ensure that protection needs are considered alongside, and where relevant modify, the operational regime applicable to the individual.
5. Develop inter-agency protection and referral pathways
• Use the national service mapping and other available information to identify existing services and protection mechanisms relevant to migrants held in the facilities.
• Develop practical referral pathways between the facilities and relevant protection and essential service providers.
• Give particular consideration to interfaces with the National Agency for Social Protection and existing specialized protection mechanisms.
• Define, to the extent possible, roles, referral steps, contact arrangements, information-sharing requirements, feedback mechanisms and procedures for urgent cases.
• Provide for referral to existing specialized services, including shelter and protection mechanisms, where appropriate and subject to applicable eligibility, legal and institutional arrangements.
• Validate proposed referral arrangements with relevant stakeholders where feasible and subject to their availability.
6. Develop practical operational tools
Develop a coherent set of practical tools required to operationalize the standards and differentiated pathways, as appropriate, which may include:
• admission and status-assessment tools;
• vulnerability screening tools/checklists;
• referral decision tree;
• standardized referral forms;
• emergency referral and incident-management tools;
• individual safeguard/checklists;
• transfer/removal/exit checklists;
• facility compliance/self-assessment tools;
• monitoring and quality-assurance tools;
• other templates and job aids identified as necessary.
7. Validate and revise the draft standards and tools
• Present the proposed standards, procedures and tools for technical review by IOM and, where feasible, relevant national stakeholders.
• Assess their legal, institutional and operational applicability.
• Document areas where information or institutional confirmation remains unavailable.
• Revise the package based on available feedback.
• Identify elements requiring practical testing during pilot training.
8. Develop a competency-based training package
Develop a practical training package enabling relevant personnel to apply the standards and tools, including:
• training curriculum and learning objectives;
• facilitator manual;
• participant materials;
• presentations and visual materials;
• cases and scenarios reflecting different operational regimes and protection situations;
• practical exercises and simulations;
• exercises on vulnerability identification and referral;
• practical application of developed tools;
• pre- and post-training assessments;
• materials and instructions enabling subsequent replication.
9. Pilot the standards, tools and training package
• Deliver one face-to-face pilot training for an agreed target group.
• Test application of the standards and operational tools through cases, scenarios and simulations.
• Collect structured participant and stakeholder feedback.
• Assess clarity, feasibility and practical applicability of the standards, procedures and tools.
• Identify modifications required before finalization.
10. Finalize the operational and face-to-face training package
• Incorporate relevant findings from technical review and pilot implementation.
• Resolve identified inconsistencies, ambiguities and implementation difficulties.
• Finalize the standards, differentiated procedures, referral pathways and operational tools.
• Finalize the face-to-face training package and assessment materials.
11. Develop a digital-ready self-paced learning package
Adapt the finalized training content for subsequent technical conversion into a self-paced digital learning module, including:
• digital course architecture and learning sequence;
• learning objectives for each unit;
• complete content/storyboard;
• final learner-facing content;
• cases and scenario-based activities;
• interactive exercises and knowledge checks;
• assessment questions, answer options and explanatory feedback;
• pre-/post- and final assessment content;
• completion/pass requirements;
• downloadable reference materials and job aids;
• specifications for diagrams, illustrations, video, audio, animation or other multimedia elements, where relevant;
• navigation and learner-interaction instructions.
The package shall contain all substantive content and instructional specifications necessary for subsequent technical production of the digital course without requiring substantive redevelopment or further input from the Consultant.
Methodological Approach and Guiding Principles
The assignment shall combine legal and institutional review, analysis of applicable international standards and guidance, comparative review of relevant foreign practices and operational models, and assessment of their applicability to the context of Uzbekistan. The methodology should be practical and implementation-oriented and should support the development of standards and tools that can be applied in the day-to-day organization and management of temporary holding centres.
The following principles shall guide the assignment:
1. National applicability and legal and institutional feasibility
The applicable national legal and institutional framework shall serve as the starting point for the analysis and development of the standards and tools. Recommendations shall take into account the mandates, responsibilities, procedures and operational capacities of relevant institutions in Uzbekistan. Where gaps, inconsistencies or areas requiring further clarification are identified between existing national arrangements and relevant international standards, these shall be clearly documented and, where appropriate, accompanied by feasible options or recommendations.
2. International standards as a normative benchmark
Applicable international human rights and protection standards, principles and guidance shall provide the normative benchmark for the development of the proposed framework, including in relation to conditions of temporary holding, dignity and humane treatment, procedural safeguards, non-discrimination, health and safety, protection of children, identification of vulnerabilities and access to appropriate protection and essential services.
The Consultant shall distinguish, where relevant, between binding national requirements, applicable international standards and recommended good practices.
3. Comparative and adaptable use of foreign good practices
Relevant foreign operational models and good practices shall be reviewed comparatively and selected on the basis of their relevance to the purpose, institutional setting and operational characteristics of the facilities concerned. Foreign approaches shall not be replicated mechanically. The Consultant shall identify elements that may reasonably be adapted to the context of Uzbekistan and explain their relevance and practical applicability.
4. Common minimum standards with differentiated procedures and safeguards
The framework shall be based on a common set of minimum operational, protection and technical standards applicable across the facilities and relevant categories of migrants. Within this common framework, procedures shall be differentiated where required by the legal or operational status of the person concerned.
Individual vulnerability or specific protection needs shall be treated as a cross-cutting consideration rather than as a separate operational regime. Identified vulnerabilities shall trigger, as appropriate, additional safeguards, differentiated treatment, further assessment and/or referral to relevant protection and essential services.
5. Protection mainstreaming and timely identification of vulnerabilities
Protection considerations shall be integrated throughout relevant stages of temporary holding, from admission and registration to transfer, removal, release or other exit from the facility. The methodology shall provide for early identification of vulnerabilities and specific protection needs and for reassessment where such needs emerge or circumstances change during the person's stay.
The framework shall support practical decision-making by personnel and clarify the actions and safeguards required when a protection concern is identified.
6. Use of existing protection and service systems
The assignment shall prioritize linkages with existing national protection, social, health and other essential service systems rather than proposing parallel structures or services within temporary holding centres where these are neither necessary nor appropriate.
Referral arrangements shall build, where possible, on existing institutional mandates and service mechanisms and shall take into account relevant findings of the national mapping of protection services and gaps for vulnerable migrants. Particular attention shall be given to practical coordination and referral interfaces between the relevant authorities, the National Agency for Social Protection and other competent service providers.
7. Operational usability
The standards and tools shall be designed for practical application rather than solely as normative or descriptive guidance. They should translate relevant requirements into clear operational procedures, responsibilities, decision points, safeguards, referral steps and practical tools that can be used by personnel responsible for the management and operation of the facilities.
The level of detail shall be sufficient to support consistent implementation while allowing for adaptation to the legal status, individual circumstances and operational context of each case.
8. Proportionality and functionality of technical requirements
Technical and facility-related requirements shall be developed to the level necessary to support safe, humane, dignified and protection-sensitive operation of temporary holding centres. This may include requirements relating to capacity and occupancy, minimum space, functional zoning, sanitation and hygiene, accessibility, healthcare and first-aid arrangements, safety and emergency preparedness, and other relevant functional requirements.
The assignment is not intended to constitute architectural or engineering design. Detailed construction specifications, structural calculations, bills of quantities or other engineering design products shall therefore fall outside the scope of the consultancy unless specifically agreed otherwise by IOM.
9. Evidence-based analysis and transparency of limitations
The Consultant shall use and triangulate, to the extent possible, relevant legislation and official documentation, international standards and guidance, comparative foreign practices, information provided by IOM, available research and data, and information obtained through stakeholder consultations where feasible.
The Consultant shall clearly distinguish between requirements established by applicable national legislation or official arrangements, international standards, comparative good practices and recommendations developed under the assignment. Where access to information, facilities or relevant stakeholders is limited, such limitations and their implications for the analysis or proposed standards shall be explicitly documented.
Lack of access to a particular stakeholder or source of information shall not in itself prevent completion of the assignment where the relevant analysis can reasonably be undertaken on the basis of other available and sufficiently reliable sources.

Required Qualifications and Experience

  • Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in law, human rights, migration studies, public administration, social sciences, international relations or a related field with at least five years of relevant professional experience; or a university degree in the above fields with at least seven years of relevant professional experience.

  • Demonstrated professional experience in migration management, migrant protection, human rights, return and removal procedures, immigration detention/temporary holding or other closely related areas.

  • Demonstrated experience in analysing legal, institutional and operational frameworks and developing practical standards, procedures, guidelines, protocols or operational tools based on such analysis.

  • Sound knowledge of applicable international human rights and migrant protection standards, including safeguards and protection considerations relating to migrants in vulnerable situations.

  • Demonstrated ability to analyse relevant international and foreign practices and adapt applicable approaches to specific national and institutional contexts.

  • Experience in developing practical training materials, including case studies, exercises, simulations and assessment tools.

  • Experience related to immigration detention, temporary holding or reception facilities, inter-agency referral mechanisms and/or cooperation with law-enforcement, migration, social protection or other relevant public authorities would be a strong asset.

  • Strong analytical, drafting and communication skills, including the ability to translate complex legal, institutional and protection requirements into practical and user-friendly operational solutions.

  • Ability to work independently, manage a complex multi-stage assignment and engage professionally with government institutions and other relevant stakeholders.

  • Fluency in written and spoken English and Russian is required; knowledge of Uzbek is an advantage.

Candidates are required to submit a separate financial proposal indicating the total professional fee for completion of the assignment.

Languages

For this consultancy, Fluency in written and spoken English and Russian is required; knowledge of Uzbek is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

Travel required

The consultancy will be home-based. The Consultant will be required to participate in person in the face-to-face pilot training in Tashkent, Uzbekistan.

If the selected Consultant is based outside Uzbekistan, one mission to Tashkent will be required for the delivery of the pilot training. The timing and duration of the mission will be agreed in advance with IOM. Required travel will be arranged and covered separately by IOM in accordance with applicable IOM rules and procedures and should not be included in the Consultant's professional fee.

Other consultations, technical discussions and validation activities are expected to be conducted remotely or in person, as appropriate and subject to arrangements agreed with IOM.

Purpose of Assignment and Scope of the work

The consultancy will be performed primarily on a home-based basis, in close coordination with the Migrants Assistance and Protection Unit of IOM Uzbekistan. The Consultant will be required to participate in person in the face-to-face pilot training in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, as specified under Section 9 of these Terms of Reference.

The Consultant shall carry out the assignment in accordance with the agreed methodology and workplan and shall maintain regular coordination with IOM throughout the assignment. Any substantive adjustments to the agreed methodology, approach or scope arising during implementation shall be discussed and agreed with IOM in advance.

title: Senior/Staff AI Engineer, Quality & Evals (m/f/x)
description:
About us

We’re Cortea, a Berlin startup transforming audits with AI. Manual, document-heavy audits waste expert time while demand keeps rising. Our AI-powered software and specialized AI agents remove the repetitive work so auditors can focus on judgment.

Backed by top-tier VCs with >15m EUR funding, with a working product and paying customers, we’re rapidly scaling.

We value first-principles thinking, speed, trust, and kindness. We build side by side in our Berlin office.

Your Role

We are looking for an engineer with strong backend, data, and AI systems experience to build the evaluation and observability foundation for production-grade LLM agents used in complex audit workflows.

This role sits at the intersection of backend engineering, data infrastructure, and AI quality. You will build the evaluation systems that power our multimodal retrieval agents and continuously improve critical quality metrics across current and future pipelines.

You’ll work at the edge of applied AI and information retrieval, building multimodal agentic pipelines and solving hard context and agent-harness engineering problems.

This is not a traditional analytics, BI, or dashboarding role. You should expect to write production code, design data architecture, work inside backend systems, and directly improve the quality, cost, reliability, and performance of LLM-based agents.

What you’ll do

You will help build and operate the technical systems around our AI agents, with a focus on data infrastructure, evaluation, observability, and optimization. You will:

  • Build online and offline evaluation systems for LLM agents, including pipelines that use golden datasets, ground-truth data, human review workflows, and experiment results.

  • Create automated quality gates so changes to prompts, context, models, or agent logic can be tested before reaching production.

  • Analyze large volumes of agent traces and executions in columnar and analytical databases such as BigQuery or ClickHouse to identify failure modes, quality regressions, latency issues, reliability gaps, and cost optimization opportunities.

  • Build reliable data retention and replay mechanisms for long-term analysis of production agent behavior.

  • Manage observability tools for tracing, monitoring, debugging, and experiment management of our audit agents.

  • Team up with backend engineers to improve the speed and reliability of our retrieval and reasoning agents.

You will fit into the role if you...

  • Have strong Python and/or backend engineering experience.

  • Have a solid understanding of how LLM and agent systems are evaluated—including deterministic checks, ground truth, LLM-as-judge, human review, and quality metrics—and can reason about when each approach is appropriate.

  • Have deployed and operated systems in the cloud, ideally on GCP.

  • Have hands-on experience building end-to-end retrieval or ML pipeline evaluation systems and using LLM observability or experimentation tools such as Braintrust, MLflow, Langfuse, or Weights & Biases.

  • Are comfortable working with analytical databases, data warehouses, columnar stores, and high-volume event or trace data.

  • Understand system design, reliability, observability, monitoring, logging, debugging, and operational trade-offs.

  • Bring senior-level engineering judgment: you can make architectural decisions, communicate trade-offs, and build systems that other engineers can extend.

  • Are comfortable with ambiguity, able to reason from first principles, and excited to build infrastructure for AI systems that are actively used in production.

Nice-to-haves that are a plus:

  • Designing data pipelines, ETL/ELT workflows, event-processing systems, or feedback loops for production data.

  • Building infrastructure around LLM-based products or agentic systems, including optimizing LLM usage, context windows, reasoning tokens, or model selection.

  • Working with production traces from complex distributed systems.

  • Building internal platforms for engineers, domain experts, or operations teams.

  • Using workflow orchestration systems such as Temporal or similar.

  • Familiarity with audit, finance, compliance, or other high-accuracy domains.

  • Experience in an early-stage startup or fast-moving engineering environment.

No-one checks every box. If you’ve shipped retrieval systems and like owning evaluations and pipelines, let’s talk.

What we offer

  • High impact & growth: Shape strategy at a scaling AI startup from day one.

  • Mission-driven culture: Ambitious team valuing first-principles thinking and bold ideas.

  • Attractive compensation: competitive salary plus significant equity.

  • Best tools for the job: Generous coding tools budget so you can use the best tools for the job.

  • Startup perks: Flexible vacation, team lunches, retreats, central Berlin office.

Interview process

  • First Call — Intro to Cortea with Liza

  • Second Call — Technical interview with Vlad

  • Third Call — Deep dive into our culture with our Co-Founder Philipp

  • On-site Day (Berlin) — Meet the team and work on a real problem together

We’re an equal-opportunity team and encourage women and underrepresented groups to apply.

Find more English Speaking Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

title: Sample Scout 2nd Yr
description:
Fresh Del Monte Produce Inc. is a global leader in the production, distribution, and marketing of fresh, value-added, and shelf-stable fruits and vegetables under our Fresh and Foods divisions. Our diverse product portfolio proudly bears the Del Monte® brand and also includes prepared fruits and vegetables, juices, beverages, snacks, and desserts—available in over 80 countries worldwide. With operations spanning more than 35 countries, we’ve proudly been nourishing families for over 135 years.


Purpose of Position:


Del Monte Foods is the Foods Division of Fresh Del Monte, a global grower, producer and marketer of fresh, value-added, and shelf-stable produce. Del Monte Foods has a powerful portfolio of brands, including the iconic Del Monte®, Contadina® and S&W®. We are currently seeking a 2nd year Sample Scout.


Our company is committed to maintaining a safe and productive work environment. As a drug free workplace, all candidates selected for hire in our operations, warehouse, quality assurance, transportation and production roles must complete and pass a pre-employment drug test.

Accountabilities:

  • Field Scouting and Crop Monitoring

  • Support field teams with collection and review of grower pesticide records.

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.

  • Strong attention to detail and ability to maintain accurate records.
  • Basic computer skills, including Microsoft Office.
  • Ability to communicate effectively with supervisors, growers, and coworkers.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality with company and grower information.
  • Ability to safely travel between field locations.
  • Ability to work flexible schedules, overtime, weekends, and extended hours during harvest periods.
  • Ability to walk long distances in fields and work outdoors in varying terrain and weather conditions.
  • Ability to bend, lift, and carry up to 50 pounds on an occasional basis.

  • Previous agricultural, scouting, farming, field research, or crop monitoring experience preferred.
  • Experience working with crop scouting software, field mapping tools, or data entry systems preferred.
  • Knowledge of pests, diseases, insects, weed identification, and crop development stages preferred.
  • Previous experience working outdoors in agricultural environments preferred.
  • Wisconsin Pesticide Applicator Certification preferred or ability to obtain.
  • Forklift certification preferred or ability to obtain.

  • Equivalent combinations of education, training, and experience that provide the required knowledge, skills, and abilities will be considered.
