title: Director of Security
description:
Position Summary:

The Director of Security implements the overall security strategy, policies, and Gun Lake Casino Resort standards to ensure the physical safety of all Guests, Team Members, and Vendors and the security of the property and assets. The Director of Security implements staff training and establishes operational plans for crisis response, disaster recovery, evacuation, workplace violence, and other emergencies. This position manages and maintains access control systems, physical key control, alarms, and other physical security measures. Additionally, the Director of Security delivers education programs and communications on security policies and topics to ensure Team Members are adequately informed and equipped to manage potential security issues. Participate in tribal, local, state, or federal working or advisory groups to keep up-to-date with all security-related information, directives, and events. Leads and directs significant investigations and critical event responses in coordination with law enforcement and other officials or agencies. This role reviews incident reports, develops security process improvements, handles budgets, and allocates resources for security operations.

About Us:

At Gun Lake Casino Resort, every Team Member is an ambassador, essential to the success of our company and our culture. We expect that all Team Members take personal ownership in ensuring that everything they do is in the best interest of Gun Lake Casino Resort and embody the core values of the Seven Grandfather Teachings:

Love: Love your brothers and sisters and share with them.

Truth: Be true in everything you do. Be true to yourself and to your fellow Humans.

Respect: You must give respect if you expect respect. Respect everyone, all persons, and all the things created.

Bravery: To do what is right, even in the most difficult of times.

Honesty: Be honest in every action and provide good feelings in your heart.

Wisdom: We cherish knowledge; wisdom is used for the good of the people.

Humility: Know that you are equal to everyone else, no better, no less.

In this Role:

  • Responsible for practicing, supporting, and always promoting Gun Lake Casino Resort’s Four Diamond Standards.
  • Lead all Team Member Engagement activities for the Security Department.
  • Responsible for department management to ensure excellent Guest service, obtain optimum efficiency and economy of operations, and maximize profits and property presentation according to policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements.
  • Responsible for reviewing and updating department Policies and Procedures.
  • Ensures all policies and procedures, laws, Tribal Gaming Commission regulations, and internal controls are enforced.
  • Responsible for maintaining accurate, thorough, and confidential internal security and personnel investigations as directed.
  • Responsible for auditing and maintaining inventory of both controlled and non-controlled keys.
  • Responsible for managing access control systems for card reader access.
  • Establish a working relationship with tribal, local, state, and federal law enforcement agencies and emergency services.
  • Coordinate with local law enforcement regarding illegal activities occurring on the property.
  • Direct emergency management during emergencies.
  • Provide immediate response and direct internal investigations. Stays current with best practices in effective security operations and participates in continuing education opportunities to maintain knowledge of and compliance with laws and regulations.
  • Responsible for developing and implementing organizational goals, business strategies, policies, and operational plans/budgets.
  • Responsible for all employment-related actions, including hiring, termination, and evaluation of Team Members within the department.
  • Responsible for always practicing, supporting, and promoting Gun Lake Casino Resort’s “Unsurpassed Service Standards.”
  • Practice teamwork, support fellow Team Members, and create an energized, positive, team-oriented work environment.
  • Conducts regular audits and inspections to assess, identify and mitigate any security vulnerabilities or gaps.
  • Interact with Guests in a friendly and courteous manner and handle all Guest opportunities.
  • Other job-related duties as assigned.


Essential Qualifications:

  • Must be 21+ years of age.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Criminal Justice, Business, or related field preferred.
  • Five years of law enforcement or equivalent experience as a Security Manager and/or Director. Casino experience required.
  • Must possess a valid Driver’s License.
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills; ability to relate well with all levels of the organization and guests; strong listening and critical thinking skills.
  • Proven experience and in-depth comprehensive knowledge in security, investigation, loss prevention, safety awareness, and risk management.
  • Must have advanced computer skills and working knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite.
  • Proven experience with maintaining a high level of confidentiality.
  • Demonstrated prior success with leading staff in the development of departmental goals.
  • Ability to evaluate courses of action and reach sound, non-judgmental, management decisions and resolutions.
  • Must know the SDS booklet location(s) for your area.
  • Ability to handle multiple tasks and prioritize efficiently.
  • Proven experience with maintaining a high level of confidentiality.
  • Ability to evaluate courses of action and reach sound, non-judgmental management decisions, and resolutions.
  • Must possess or be able to obtain an Alcohol Awareness Card (TIPS). If not already certified, training will be provided.
  • Ability to obtain a gaming license with the Gun Lake Tribal Gaming Commission.

Physical Requirements:

  • Requires normal, corrective vision range, the ability to see color, and the ability to distinguish letters, numbers, and symbols.
  • Strength to subdue a person(s). Must be able to run after suspects. Must be able to drag an unconscious person during an evacuation.
  • Requires the stamina to climb stairs, sit, stand, or walk for long periods of time.
  • Requires an acute sense of smell and sound and the ability to talk on and hear through a two-way radio and telephone.
  • Must be able to lift 50 lbs with or without assistance.
  • Further physical requirements include, but are not limited to, standing, kneeling, crouching, walking, bending, lifting, climbing, grasping, and reaching.

Work Conditions:

Work is typically in an area, which may be unusually hot, cold, noisy, and may contain second-hand smoke. Work may be performed in small areas with a 3 ft. wide access. Tasks performed from a sitting or non-sitting position. Performance of job duties will require standing, walking, lifting, reaching, pushing, pulling, and grasping. These tasks include the maintenance and care of assigned areas. Work may entail trained chemical usage. Constant contact with fellow Team Members and Guests.

Disclaimer and Conditions of Employment:

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by persons assigned to this job. These statements are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required.

All applicants must be able to demonstrate their US work authorization during the employment verification process. The pre-employment process also requires the ability to pass a criminal background investigation, and drug test.

Indian Preference:

The Match-E-Be-Nash-She-Wish Band of Pottawatomi Indians abides by Native American preference in its hiring and employment policies.

Gun Lake Tribal Gaming Authority reserves the right to make changes to the above job description as necessary.

title: Converting Supervisor
description:
At Hood Container Corporation, we’re searching for a Converting Supervisor at our Greensboro, NC plant.

This role is responsible for managing to meet manufacturing and production schedules, providing overall direction to production floor employees, including production, scheduling, performance management, training and other related areas, striving to improve overall operational efficiencies during the designated shift. This role is responsible for coordinating production operations and maintaining effective quality procedures and safety regulations for the facility. The ideal candidates must be a self-driven individual with a passion for excellence in Safety, People Development, Manufacturing, and Customer Focus.

The plant runs Monday-Friday with weekend work as needed. Must provide leadership on the operating floor and striving for compliance in safety, health, environmental, and quality. Also responsible for coaching, training, and developing operations personnel in safety, quality, production, problem solving, and technical and interpersonal communication skills; addressing key issues and concerns; and interacting with employees from other departments to ensure quality and on-time production. Drive safety excellence through promoting employee involvement, ownership and accountability to proactively identify hazards and implement the appropriate mitigating strategies; investigate incidents and participate in resolution of causes Ensure best practices are being followed for minimization of waste at machine centers. Track continuous improvement opportunities where performance issues are apparent and provide leadership/action plans for gap closure. Strictly adhere to plant safety and housekeeping efforts. Identify repairs needed at machine centers and create work requests for completion; follow up as required. Plan, assign and direct work for all hourly production employees; appraise performance and provide feedback as needed; assist in resolving complaints; hold employees accountable as needed; communicate issues and results on a daily basis. What it Takes:

  • 3-5 years in a leadership role within the manufacturing industry.
  • Must be able to work high temperature & humidity conditions while wearing proper PPE including, but not limited to, hearing protection, steel toe shoes and safety glasses.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced and dynamic environment.
  • Corrugated industry experience preferred
  • Must be able to lift 50lbs

Our Story:

Hood Container Corporation is a family-owned, mill to market company specializing in containerboard and kraft paper, corrugated boxes, high graphic displays and contract packaging. Our goal is to be a diverse workforce that is representative, at all job levels, of the citizens and customers we serve. We are committed to building a team that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. The more inclusive we are, the better our work will be.

description:

title: Sr. Director of IT Applications
description:
The Senior Director, IT Applications is a senior technology leader responsible for the strategy, leadership, delivery, performance, and optimization of Community Behavioral Health’s (CBH) enterprise application portfolio. Reporting to the Chief Information Officer, this position oversees internally supported and vendor-supported applications that enable CBH’s clinical, operational, financial, and administrative functions, including the organization’s claims adjudication system and enterprise clinical dashboard.

A central accountability of this role is establishing and maturing CBH’s Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) capability, including the governance, processes, tools, environments, controls, and standards required for disciplined application development and delivery. The Senior Director will ensure SDLC practices are fully adopted and consistently utilized across internal teams and applicable vendors, while building the organizational structure, talent, accountability, and partnerships necessary to deliver secure, reliable, high-quality solutions with accuracy and predictability.

Salary: Starts at $129,500 and above, depending on experience.

Key Responsibilities:

Organizational and Talent Leadership

  • Build and lead a high-performing enterprise applications organization with the structure, capacity, and capabilities required to support CBH’s current and future needs.
  • Recruit, onboard, develop, and retain high-quality technology talent, capable of effective application delivery within a mature SDLC.
  • Establish clear roles, performance expectations, accountability, professional development, and succession plans.
  • Cultivate a culture of ownership, collaboration, transparency, customer service, continuous improvement, and disciplined execution.

Enterprise Partnership and Communication

  • Serve as a trusted technology partner to executive leaders, business stakeholders, and colleagues across CBH.
  • Build strong partnerships across IT and with clinical, operational, financial, compliance, data and administrative leaders to translate business priorities into effective technology solutions.
  • Communicate proactively regarding application performance, delivery commitments, SDLC progress, risks, significant incidents, resource needs, and key decisions.
  • Translate complex technology issues into clear business terms and provide actionable recommendations, options, risks, and tradeoffs.

Application Strategy, Governance and SDLC Leadership

  • Develop and execute an enterprise applications strategy and roadmap aligned with CBH’s organizational priorities and technology strategy.
  • Establish and mature CBH’s enterprise SDLC framework, including governance, methodologies, processes, tools, environments, documentation, controls, and performance measures.
  • Ensure SDLC practices are consistently applied across application development, configuration, integration, testing, release, deployment, maintenance, and major vendor-supported implementations.
  • Establish a clear applications operating model with defined roles, decision rights, prioritization, standards, and accountability.
  • Partner with the CIO and IT leadership team to prioritize investments, modernize the application portfolio, and ensure solutions support enterprise needs.

Enterprise Application Management and Delivery

  • Provide end-to-end oversight of mission-critical applications throughout their lifecycle, including requirements, design, development/configuration, integration, testing, deployment, maintenance, enhancement, upgrades, and support.
  • Provide executive oversight of CBH’s claims adjudication system, enterprise clinical information system, and other critical application platforms.
  • Establish disciplined requirements, testing, quality assurance, change, release, and deployment practices that improve delivery speed, quality, predictability, traceability, and production readiness.
  • Ensure appropriate development, test, staging, and production environments and supporting delivery infrastructure are established, governed, and effectively utilized.
  • Maintain clear visibility into application roadmaps, priorities, backlogs, delivery commitments, risks, dependencies, performance, and technical debt; ensure critical issues are escalated and resolved with appropriate urgency.

Vendor Management

  • Serve as the senior IT relationship owner for strategic application vendors and hold partners accountable for performance, service levels, delivery, issue resolution, and applicable CBH SDLC, security, testing, and change-management expectations.
  • Establish effective vendor governance and partner with appropriate internal stakeholders on contracts, renewals, licensing, performance, risks, and technology value.

Risk, Security and Compliance

  • Ensure enterprise applications and SDLC practices operate in accordance with CBH policies and applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Partner with Information Security, Privacy, Compliance, and Legal to embed appropriate security, privacy, access, testing, change-management, documentation, and audit controls throughout the application lifecycle.
  • Support audits, risk assessments, and remediation activities, and proactively address application risks including technical debt, vendor dependencies, unsupported technologies, integration challenges, and process/control gaps.


Position Requirements:

Education

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field required.
  • Master’s degree or relevant advanced professional credentials preferred.

Experience

  • Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible information technology experience, including significant responsibility for enterprise applications, software development/application delivery, or software platforms, with at least 5 years in senior leadership.
  • Demonstrated expertise establishing, maturing, governing, and driving adoption of SDLC processes, methodologies, tools, controls, environments, and delivery infrastructure.
  • Demonstrated success building or maturing an enterprise applications or software delivery function and recruiting, developing, and retaining high-performing technology professionals.
  • Significant experience overseeing mission-critical enterprise applications, including implementations, integrations, upgrades, modernization, production support, release management, and strategic software vendors.
  • Healthcare technology experience, including claims processing, clinical systems, care management platforms, healthcare data, or related technologies strongly preferred.
  • Experience within a Medicaid Managed Care Organization, health plan, behavioral health organization, healthcare delivery system, or similarly regulated environment strongly preferred.


Philadelphia Residency Requirement:

  • The successful candidate must be a current Philadelphia resident or become a resident within six months of hire.

U.S. Authorization Requirement:

  • CBH does not provide sponsorship for applicants requiring future work authorization. All candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States without requiring sponsorship now or in the future.

Equal Employment Opportunity:

  • We strive to promote and sustain a culture of diversity, inclusion and belonging every day. CBH is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate in recruiting, hiring, promotion, or any other personnel action based on all qualified individuals. This is without regard to race, ethnicity, creed, color, religion, national origin, age, sex/gender, marital status, gender identity, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, disability, protected veteran status, genetic information or any other characteristic protected individual genetic information, or non-disqualifying physical or mental handicap or disability in each aspect of the human resources function by applicable federal, state, or local law.

Requesting An Accommodation:

  • CBH is committed to providing equal employment opportunities for individuals with disabilities or religious observance, including reasonable accommodation when needed. If you are hired by CBH and require an accommodation to perform the essential functions of your role, you will be asked to participate in our accommodation process. Accommodations made to facilitate the recruiting process are not a guarantee of future or continued accommodation once hired.
  • If you would like to be considered for employment opportunities with CBH and have accommodation needs for a disability or religious observance, please send us an email at CBH.Recruitment@Phila.gov

title: Defueling Functional Area Planner (FAP)
description:

title: Catastrophe Field Adjuster - South Carolina Territory
description:
At Frontline Insurance, we are on a mission to Make Things Better, and our Catastrophe Field Adjuster - South Carolina Territory plays a pivotal role in achieving this vision. We strive to provide high quality service and proactive solutions to all our customers to ensure that we are making things better for each one.

If you’re looking for a role, as a Catastrophe Field Adjuster - South Carolina Territory where you can make a meaningful impact and grow your career, your next adventure starts here!

What you can expect as a Catastrophe Field Adjuster- South Carolina Territory:

This will include collecting and reviewing all loss related facts, performing an analysis under the terms of the insurance policy to make a coverage decision, and issuing a payment within the applicable authority level.

Must be able to carry, set up, and safely climb a ladder with a Type IA rating (Extra Heavy Capacity, 300 LB/136 KG), weighing equal to or more than 50 pounds.   • Analyze the policy to determine the coverage for the loss. Evaluate coverage and make a coverage recommendation on each claim.

  • Respond to all questions in a timely manner.

  • Collaborate with team members and stakeholders to resolve various claims related issues as they arise.

We provide a collaborative, inclusive, and growth-oriented work environment where every team member can thrive.


Frontline Insurance is an equal-opportunity employer that is committed to diversity and inclusion in the workplace. We prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind based on race, color, sex, religion, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws.

title: Direct Service Advocate_Domestic Violence Shelter_2nd Shift_FT
description:
Job Title: Direct Service Advocate

Reports to: Assistant Program Director

Schedule: Tuesday- Saturday 3pm-11pm (FT); 75 hours bi-weekly

Starting Rate: $21.00


FLSA Status: Non-Exempt

​


The YWCA of Western MA is dedicated to eliminating racism and empowering survivors. The YW provides a safe place for survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, and human trafficking. Our programs and services include crisis shelter and transitional housing for survivors and their families, counseling, SAFEPLAN court advocacy, community education, supervised visitation, and vocational training for youth. The YWCA provides services at several sites, including Holyoke, Northampton, Westfield, and our primary Springfield campus.

Expectations of all employees

In the performance of essential and general job responsibilities, all YWCA employees are expected to:

  • Demonstrate commitment to the YW’s mission and principles of trauma-informed work.
  • Represent the YW in a professional and competent manner to participants, community members, organizational partners, and other stakeholders.
  • Support policies, practices, and decisions that demonstrate our shared accountability for racial equity.
  • Communicate openly and contribute to the development of others.
  • Coordinate efforts across teams, programs, and partner organizations.
  • Maintain professional behavior and strict confidentiality.

Position Purpose

The Direct Service Advocate (DSA) is responsible for providing support, advocacy and role modeling to adult, teen, and child program participants living in the YWCA’s residential programs. DSA’s are part of a team model working with peers, supervisors, clinicians and outside connections to best serve program participants. DSA’s support the agency mission and trauma informed service model in order to provide safe, consistent and quality services to vulnerable populations.

Essential Responsibilities

  • Conduct shelter intakes as needed.
  • Provide crisis intervention as needed.
  • Accurately record documents (Laundry sheets, Support Services Request sheets, Bus/Uber documents) that needs to be handed to management.
  • Help residents become acquainted with shelter and other residents upon arrival.
  • Provide counseling to resident upon arrival and as needed throughout their stay.
  • Responsible for maintenance and upkeep of the facility and property (including, but not limited to: vacuuming, laundry area, shoveling, mopping).
  • Enforce shelter rules and guidelines.
  • Engage with residents at meal time and ensure that residents clean up their area prior to leaving dining area.
  • Ensure completion of chores as applicable.
  • Required to work alone in the event of a staff call-out.
  • Complete all required paperwork and maintain client records.
  • Attend monthly staff meetings.
  • Perform other related duties as needed.

Qualifications

  • Associate’s degree plus 1 - 3 years of experience in human services;
  • Experience working in residential setting preferred;
  • Familiarity with issues of domestic violence;
  • Experience with survivors of gender-based violence and exploitation;
  • Experience addressing the impacts of decisions and actions on multiple communities;
  • Understanding of both interpersonal and structural racism and bias;
  • Ability to represent agency from a management perspective in an active union environment;
  • Excellent written and organizational skills including computer skills;
  • Reliable transportation, safe driving record, and valid driver’s license required. Must be able to be covered by the agency's insurance policy.
  • Must be able to lift 40 lbs.

EEO STATEMENT

It is the policy of YWCA of Western Massachusetts to provide equal employment opportunity (EEO) to all persons regardless of age, color, national origin, citizenship status, physical or mental disability, race, religion, creed, gender, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, genetic information, marital status, pregnancy or maternity, status with regard to public assistance, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local law. In addition, the YWCA will provide reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities.

DISCLAIMER

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees assigned to this classification. They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties and skills required of employees assigned to this position.

AT-WILL EMPLOYMENT

The YWCA is an “at-will” equal opportunity employer. While the YWCA will continue to operate with care regarding employment decisions, the YWCA and its employees may terminate the employment relationship at any time and for any reason, with or without cause, and without advance notice. Exceptions include select, non-exempt positions covered under the Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA). This position is covered under the CBA (union) and is subject to union dues.

CRIMINAL BACKGROUND CHECKS

The YWCA, in our effort to provide safety to those we serve, and to protect our agency, performs criminal offender record information (CORI) checks on all prospective employees. Final offers of employment are contingent upon receipt of an acceptable CORI report as solely determined by the YWCA.

INTRODUCTORY PERIOD

All employment at the YWCA begins with a 150-day Introductory Period.

title: STEM Inspiration Coordinator for ESA Education Office
description:
Telespazio Belgium can count on almost 40 years of experience in the field of Space Operations Service & Engineering activities.

We provide a significant contribution to the most major Space programs of the European Space Agency. Our core business is to work on the ground to build bridges into space, contributing to the success of ambitious missions.

The European Space Agency is our biggest client and we provide highly qualified employees to many sites of ESA but mainly for ESTEC in the Netherlands, and we provide a permanent contract with great benefits, a good salary, a relocation package along with genuine support to our employees.

On behalf of the European Space Agency, we are looking for a highly skilled STEM Inspiration Coordinator for ESA Education Office to work in ESTEC, in the Netherlands.

Candidates must be eligible for a security personal clearance from an EU Member State national security administration

What is expected from you:

In this position you will:

  • Design and deliver inspiration and non-formal education activities in different formats, with support-ing outreach and educational materials
  • Coordinate the planning and delivery of STEM educational activities in orbit for instance on the international Space Station (ISS)

The main activities of the STEM Inspiration include:

  • Support the set-up, planning, design, organization, logistics, coordination and execution of the ESA STEM inspirational and non-formal education activities - in person and on-line - either organized by ESA or by/with other external partners (e.g. Space events and/or camps, hackathons, exhibitions, conferences, fairs...
  • Define the content and coordinate the production (also with ESA’s external providers) of the relevant supporting outreach and educational materials: online media (e.g. dedicated internet, intranet or social media sections), audiovisual products (e.g. videos, webinars, etc), promotional and exhibition materials, non-formal didactics resources for the non-formal education context, activity guidelines
  • Draft the Joint Education Plans for educational/inspirational activities around every ESA mission to the ISS, liaising with the partners and stakeholders indicated by ESA
  • Define, plan, execute, monitor and control the execution of all formal processes required to implement in-orbit education activities, as well as the related ground activities
  • Train educators within and outside ESA (e.g. ESEROs or other national trainers indicated by ESA) on tools and/or education protocols used during in-orbit activities, and create corresponding tutorials in appropriate formats, contribute to the organization and delivery of additional teacher/educator training modules in the areas of concern when requested
  • Coordinate the technical set-up and in-orbit operational aspects of educational in-flight calls and other in-orbit inspirational activities with ARISS and other organizations indicated by ESA

What you offer :

  • University education in a STEM subject
  • Additional university qualification in school-level STEM-education or secondary-level teaching qualifications in a STEM subject
  • Experience in instructional design and state-of-the-art STEM pedagogical approaches, theoretical and practical;
  • Specific experience in the design and development of didactic content on scientific subjects applied to secondary school curricula, the addition of primary level pedagogy/didactics qualification and/or experience is considered an asset
  • Direct teaching experience and/or teacher training experience
  • At least 3 years of experience of relevant professional experience in the domain
  • Fluent in spoken and written English; Knowledge of French is an asset.
  • Strong interest in education activities, and in the field of science and technology in general.
  • Experience in space project management, teaching or in educational projects is a strong asset.
  • Proven ability to effectively coordinate work contributions from several different parties, and ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with all stakeholders (ESA, the involved international partners, industry, academia, and students).
  • Candidates will be expected to have strong organizational and reporting skills, as well as a strong proactive, self-starter and autonomous attitude.
  • Strong capacity to learn and adapt as well as an excellent aptitude for resolving problems autonomously and diplomatically, as the successful applicant will be in direct contact with many different stakeholders, from a wide range of ESA staff at different levels, to representatives of academia, experts, industry, and ESA’s international partners
  • Excellent communication skills
  • Familiar with the ESA environment and programs is an asset

What we offer:

  • A competitive salary
  • 30 days of paid annual leave, plus the days ESTEC is closed including public holidays (~12 days) based on a 40-hour working week;
  • Hybrid working scheme (3 days in the office and 2 days remote in the Netherlands)
  • Flexible working hours; you are in charge of your own agenda respecting core working hours
  • Fully paid collective extensive health insurance scheme;
  • A good pension scheme with no personal contribution;
  • A career development (Coursera membership + training budget);
  • Travel allowance;
  • Extensive relocation package

Where:

You will be working within ESTEC, the European Space Agency’s offices in the Netherlands as a contractor for Telespazio Belgium. We don’t expect the employees to be on-site full time however you will still have to relocate to the Netherlands for this position.

Deadline to apply: ASAP

title: Director of Transportation
description:
Summary

The Director of Logistics provides strategic and operational leadership for the Company's transportation and logistics functions across multiple facilities. This position is responsible for developing and executing transportation strategies that ensure safe, reliable, timely, and cost-effective movement of products while supporting customer service, production requirements, and overall business objectives.


The Director oversees transportation operations, carrier and fleet performance, logistics personnel, transportation technology, freight spend, regulatory compliance, international logistics, and continuous improvement initiatives. This position partners closely with Operations, Supply Chain, Sales, Customer Service, Finance, Warehousing, Information Technology, and other departments to optimize the Company's transportation network and ensure customer commitments are achieved.


The Director is expected to balance service, cost, capacity, safety, compliance, and operational requirements while developing scalable logistics processes that support continued business growth.

Education, Licensure and Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Business Administration, Operations Management, or a related field preferred.
  • Five or more years of progressively responsible logistics, transportation, supply chain, or related experience preferred.
  • Three or more years of demonstrated leadership and people-management experience required.
  • Experience managing transportation operations across multiple facilities or locations strongly preferred.
  • Experience managing company-owned or dedicated fleets, drivers, and third-party transportation providers preferred.
  • Experience with Oracle Transportation Management (OTM) or a comparable Transportation Management System (TMS) required; OTM experience strongly preferred.
  • International logistics experience, including working with freight forwarders, customs brokers, and import/export transportation processes, preferred.
  • Working knowledge of applicable DOT, FMCSA, transportation safety, and carrier compliance requirements.
  • Experience with truckload, less-than-truckload (LTL), dedicated fleet, brokerage, intermodal, international, and other transportation modes as applicable to Company operations.
  • Demonstrated experience with carrier sourcing, rate negotiations, transportation contracts, and carrier performance management.
  • Strong financial and analytical skills, including transportation budgeting, forecasting, cost analysis, and KPI management.
  • Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Excel and working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications, databases, reporting tools, and transportation technology.
  • Strong verbal, written, presentation, negotiation, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to analyze complex problems, identify root causes, make sound decisions, and implement sustainable corrective actions.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities, work effectively under pressure, and meet deadlines in a fast-paced operating environment.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Demonstrated ability to build effective working relationships with employees, customers, carriers, vendors, and senior leadership.
  • Ability and willingness to travel between Company locations and to other domestic or international locations as business needs require.

Qualifications

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be a minimum of 18 years of age and must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.


Essential Duties and Responsibilities include the following (Please note: This in no way states or implies that these are the only duties you will be required to perform. The omission of specific duties does not exclude them from the position. Other duties may be assigned as deemed necessary and appropriate.):

Strategic Leadership and Transportation Management

  1. Develops and executes the Company's transportation and logistics strategy across multiple manufacturing and distribution locations.
  2. Provides leadership and oversight for inbound, outbound, intercompany, customer, and international transportation activities, as applicable.
  3. Optimizes the transportation network by evaluating routes, modes, carriers, capacity, equipment utilization, service requirements, consolidation opportunities, and total delivered cost.
  4. Establishes and maintains transportation policies, procedures, routing guides, service standards, escalation protocols, and operating expectations across Company locations.
  5. Partners with Operations, Sales, Customer Service, Supply Chain, Finance, Warehousing, and other departments to align transportation capabilities with production schedules, customer requirements, inventory needs, and business objectives.
  6. Evaluates transportation capacity requirements and develops strategies to support seasonal demand, production changes, customer growth, new business, and changing market conditions.
  7. Leads logistics planning for new customers, facilities, products, acquisitions, network changes, and other significant business initiatives as required.

Carrier and Fleet Management

  1. Develops and maintains a reliable, competitive, and diversified carrier network capable of meeting Company capacity, service, safety, and cost requirements.
  2. Leads carrier sourcing, bid processes, rate negotiations, contract negotiations, lane awards, and transportation-provider selection.
  3. Establishes carrier performance standards and scorecards and conducts regular performance reviews addressing service, cost, capacity, safety, claims, responsiveness, and compliance.
  4. Ensures appropriate carrier qualification and monitoring processes are maintained, including operating authority, insurance requirements, safety performance, and applicable regulatory requirements.
  5. Develops contingency capacity and alternative transportation strategies to minimize disruption during carrier shortages, weather events, equipment failures, production interruptions, or other unexpected events.


Transportation Technology and Analytics

  1. Serves as the business leader for the Company's Transportation Management System (TMS), including Oracle Transportation Management (OTM), and promotes consistent utilization across facilities, employees, carriers, and other transportation partners.
  2. Ensures transportation data is accurate, timely, and reliable and establishes expectations for carrier and employee system compliance.
  3. Utilizes transportation technology, analytics, and reporting tools to improve routing, load optimization, carrier selection, shipment visibility, cost management, and decision-making.
  4. Establishes and maintains meaningful transportation KPIs and dashboards and regularly reports performance and trends to senior leadership.
  5. Uses data and root-cause analysis to identify service failures, excessive costs, process gaps, and improvement opportunities and ensures corrective actions are implemented and sustained.

International Logistics and Trade Support

  1. Oversees international transportation activities and relationships with freight forwarders, customs brokers, carriers, and other logistics service providers, as applicable.
  2. Ensures appropriate processes are maintained for international shipping documentation, customs clearance, Incoterms, duties and tariffs, and other applicable import/export transportation requirements.
  3. Monitors international transportation risks, port or border disruptions, capacity constraints, and regulatory changes that may affect cost, lead time, or customer service.
  4. Partners with appropriate internal and external resources to ensure international shipments comply with applicable Company policies and legal and regulatory requirements.
  5. Other Duties as assigned.


Supervision

They must also possess the skills, knowledge, and abilities to fill in for any of the Supervisors reporting to them if necessary. The incumbent will perform either set of duties with minimal supervision and direction. The logistics manager is responsible for the competence of the organization and must also possess the skills, knowledge, and abilities to fill in for the shift supervisors when necessary. The incumbent will perform either set of duties with minimal supervision and direction.


Supervises personnel to ensure quality service in accordance with the Personnel Manual and applicable laws. Responsibilities include but are not limited:

Must be able to effectively communicate in both individual and group settings. Must be able to present information and respond to questions from individuals and/or groups including residents, employees, managers, and the general public.

  1. Add, subtract, multiply, and divide all units of measure such as whole numbers, fractions, percentages, and fractions.
  2. Compute rate, discounts, ratios, and percent, and
  3. Make, read and interpret financials, graphs, rates, ratios, and percentages.

Other Skills and Abilities

  4. Ability to lead structured problem-solving and troubleshooting efforts involving complex operational issues.
  5. Ability to motivate, develop, train, and coach employees to achieve strong performance and engagement.
  6. Strong planning, organizational, and priority-setting skills.
  7. Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, dynamic, multi-location environment.
  8. Ability to establish strong working relationships across organizational levels and functional areas.
  9. Ability to work in varying office, warehouse, transportation, and production environments, including areas subject to heat and cold.
  10. Ability and willingness to work extended hours, weekends, holidays, or outside normal business hours when operational needs require.
  11. Ability to provide visible leadership and guidance to employees in office, warehouse, production, and transportation environments.

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to use hands and/or fingers to feel, manipulate small objects, write, and type. The employee is frequently required to bend, squat/kneel; twist/turn; sit; talk; hear and reach with hands and arms. The employee is occasionally required to push/pull; climb; walk; stand; and balance. The employee is rarely required to smell and/or taste. title: Strategic Operations Advisor, Expert
description:

Orbis Operations is a technology company that delivers sovereign intelligence and decision capabilities to the United States Government and its allies. Solutions forged from experience, that is how we build, and it is how we hire.

Job Summary

Orbis is seeking an experienced Strategic Operations Advisor, Expert to lead program planning and evaluation activities for a client in the US Intelligence Community. The Strategic Ops Advisor will have the opportunity to demonstrate subject matter expertise, intellectual agility, all source analysis, and research acumen by leading operational efforts to produce key performance insights. Further, the Consultant will lead the implementation of recommendations when they are adopted by the customer. This project features the opportunity to interact with a wide range of key stakeholders, including those at senior levels. This is an exciting opportunity for an intellectually curious, energetic, data-savvy consultant to work on a project with real impact, helping our client develop ways to understand and improve performance of activities that support delivery of our customers’ mission.

Travel: TDY. The position includes occasional travel overseas in support of client objectives

Key Responsibilities

  • Consult with teammates and clients on the development, prioritization, and implementation of process improvement and program evaluation tasks.
  • Develop recommendations for changes to policy, processes, communications, and training to enable achievement of vision.
  • Develop and implement research designs with practical strategies for measuring performance of organizational units and/or unit activities--to include development of performance measures and design of actionable methods for collecting and analyzing data; implement strategies and refine as needed.
  • Perform a variety of research activities to include document reviews, structured interviews, and gap analyses--to include stakeholder identification and logistical coordination for data collection activities and documentation of discussions.
  • Analyze both qualitative and quantitative information to provide the customer with comprehensive insights into organizational strengths and challenge areas.
  • Socialize results and recommendations with the team at the working-level.
  • Prepare visual presentations of data and analysis.
  • Prepare reports and presentations for senior leadership based on research plans, activities, findings and recommendations.
  • Brief senior level customers on research plans, activities, findings and recommendations.
  • All-source intelligence research, analysis, and report writing/editing
  • TDY travel

Supervisory Responsibilities

  • This position has no supervisory responsibilities

Required Qualifications

  • Active TS/SCI clearance with Poly
  • Must have a Bachelor’s degree and a minimum of 10 years' experience in a consulting role in the IC or at least 10 years combined experience with the IC and positions relevant to required skills.
  • A minimum of 5 years of relevant experience as an analyst, targeting officer, technical Targeter, desk officer, operations officer, or reports officer within the sponsor's organization or other relevant organization(s) in the Intelligence Community.
  • Experience in the South American AOR
  • Excellent analytical skills and problem-solving abilities
  • Excellent oral presentation and briefing skills
  • Knowledge of and experience in the fundamentals of all-source intelligence analysis
  • Familiarity with the customer’s report writing standards
  • Attention to detail and the ability to effectively follow through and manage status reporting, scheduling, and project communications
  • High degree of personal integrity
  • Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to work well both independently and as part of a team
  • Ability to work in a dynamic environment, juggling concurrent tasks and meeting deadlines

Desired Qualifications

  • Relevant targeting, desk officer, or technical or operations skills
  • Experience deploying strategic communications
  • Experience in SIGINT, GEOINT and Technical Targeting methods
  • Proficiency with software and databases used in support of research and analysis for the U.S. Government

Physical Requirements

  • Sedentary Work: Primarily performs work in a seated position for extended periods of time; occasionally required to stand, walk, or move about the work area
  • Fine Motor Skills: Regularly required to use hands and fingers to operate a computer keyboard, mouse, and other standard office equipment
  • Vision: Ability to read and view a computer screen for extended periods; close vision and the ability to adjust focus required
  • Hearing & Speech: Ability to communicate clearly and effectively in person, via telephone, and through video conferencing platforms; ability to hear and understand spoken information in a professional setting
  • Lifting: Occasionally required to lift and/or move up to 10 pounds (e.g., files, documents, office supplies)
  • Concentration: Ability to maintain focus and attention to detail in a professional office or remote work environment
  • Travel: TDY. The position includes occasional travel overseas in support of client objectives

Orbis Benefits

Beyond the opportunity to work alongside practitioners who have operated at the mission edge, joining Orbis means real ownership over outcomes that matter — the chance to build technology that gives the United States Government and its allies a genuine decision advantage, not just another dashboard. From competitive retirement matching to a PTO policy that encourages real time off, we're committed to creating an environment where our team can do their best work and still have a life outside of it.

Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to meet the diverse needs of our employees and their families. A full list of benefits is shared with candidates following an initial conversation with our HR team, so you'll have a clear picture of the support and resources available to you as part of the Orbis team.

Orbis Locations

Orbis works in whatever arrangement the mission requires. Depending on the role, that might mean five days a week on a customer site, full-time in one of our offices, a hybrid schedule, or fully remote work — our team is spread across 25 states and four countries to match. We make sure every team member has the tools and access needed to do the work, wherever that work happens.

Travel is common across many Orbis roles, particularly those supporting customer missions in the field.

Orbis is headquartered in McLean, VA, with additional office locations in Taipei, Taiwan, and Canberra, Australia.

Orbis Operations is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We are committed to providing a work environment free of discrimination and harassment, and we make employment decisions based on merit,

qualifications, and business need. Orbis does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, genetic information, or any other status protected by applicable law.

Orbis complies with all applicable equal opportunity and non-discrimination laws in every jurisdiction in which we operate. Reasonable accommodation is available to applicants and employees with disabilities upon request.

title: Entertainment Technician

Skills

title: Director of Finance Strategic Initiatives
description:
Position Summary:

The Director of Finance Transformation serves as a strategic transformation leader responsible for advancing finance modernization, process improvement, technology adoption, and data-informed decision-making across Gun Lake Casino Resort, Tribal Government, and affiliated entities. This role partners with the Chief Financial Officer, the Vice President of Finance and Administration, and leaders across the organization to improve financial operations, strengthen reporting capabilities, standardize processes, and support scalable, sustainable growth.


This position leads high-impact finance transformation initiatives that may include ERP optimization, automation, process redesign, reporting enhancements, financial close improvement, purchase-to-pay modernization, credit and collections improvement, change management, and cross-functional adoption of new tools, workflows, and best practices. The role is accountable for translating transformation goals into practical implementation plans, measurable outcomes, stakeholder alignment, and consistent communication with senior leadership.


As a senior leader within the Finance function, the Director of Finance Transformation is expected to lead with curiosity, integrity, courage, humility, and adaptability while fostering a culture of innovation, accountability, continuous learning, collaboration, and respect. This role supports Gun Lake Casino Resort's "Unsurpassed Service" standards, Four Diamond expectations, and the Seven Grandfather Teachings by strengthening how financial information, systems, and processes enable leaders to make timely, accurate, and responsible business decisions.

About Us:

At Gun Lake Casino Resort, every Team Member is an ambassador, essential to the success of our company and our culture. We expect that all Team Members take personal ownership in ensuring that everything they do is in the best interest of Gun Lake Casino Resort and embody the core values of the Seven Grandfather Teachings:

Love: Love your brothers and sisters and share with them.

Truth: Be true in everything you do. Be true to yourself and to your fellow Humans.

Respect: You must give respect if you expect respect. Respect everyone, all persons, and all the things created.

Bravery: To do what is right, even in the most difficult of times.

Honesty: Be honest in every action and provide good feelings in your heart.

Wisdom: We cherish knowledge; wisdom is used for the good of the people.

Humility: Know that you are equal to everyone else, no better, no less.


In this Role:

Finance Strategy & Transformation

  • Serve as a strategic partner to the Chief Financial Officer, Vice President of Finance & Administration, and senior leadership to identify opportunities that enhance financial performance, operational efficiency, governance, and long-term organizational effectiveness across Tribal enterprises.
  • Lead the development and execution of the Tribe's finance transformation strategy, aligning initiatives with organizational priorities, enterprise objectives, and long-term financial sustainability.
  • Identify opportunities to optimize financial operations through process redesign, standardization, automation, data analytics, technology enablement, and continuous improvement.
  • Evaluate organizational risks, dependencies, and impacts associated with transformation initiatives while recommending practical solutions and measurable outcomes.


Enterprise Transformation Leadership

  • Lead enterprise-wide finance transformation initiatives, including ERP implementation and optimization, financial systems integration, workflow redesign, reporting modernization, automation, and process improvement.
  • Partner with leaders across Tribal Government, Gaming, Hospitality, Investments, Information Technology, Procurement, Regulatory Compliance, and other business functions to ensure financial processes and systems support organizational goals.
  • Build strong relationships with executive leadership, Tribal Council, department leaders, and external partners to establish alignment, drive collaboration, and sustain engagement throughout transformation efforts.
  • Establish key performance indicators (KPIs) and success metrics to measure the effectiveness, adoption, and business impact of transformation initiatives.

Technology & Process Improvement

  • Lead or support the evaluation, selection, implementation, integration, and optimization of financial technologies, including ERP platforms, reporting tools, analytics solutions, workflow automation, and related systems.
  • Champion best practices in financial process design, governance, and technology utilization to improve accuracy, efficiency, scalability, and decision-making.
  • Monitor emerging trends in finance technology, analytics, automation, artificial intelligence, and organizational transformation to identify opportunities for innovation.

Change Leadership & Organizational Development

  • Develop and execute comprehensive change management strategies that support successful implementation of new systems, standardized processes, reporting enhancements, and evolving operating models.
  • Design and facilitate training and knowledge transfer programs that enable finance professionals and business partners to successfully adopt new technologies, processes, and ways of working.
  • Mentor, coach, and develop finance team members by building capabilities in financial analysis, project leadership, technology adoption, process improvement, and continuous learning.
  • Foster a culture of innovation, collaboration, accountability, continuous improvement, and data-informed decision-making across all finance transformation initiatives.

Executive Communication & Governance

  • Provide regular updates to the Chief Financial Officer, executive leadership, and other stakeholders regarding project status, organizational impacts, risks, recommendations, and key decisions requiring executive action.
  • Ensure finance transformation initiatives comply with Tribal policies, internal controls, regulatory requirements, and applicable Tribal, Federal, State, and gaming regulations.
  • Support organizational priorities by providing interim leadership or assuming additional responsibilities as business needs require.

Leadership Expectations

  • Maintain the highest standards of integrity, professionalism, confidentiality, and stewardship when handling Tribal, financial, operational, guest, Team Member, and organizational information.
  • Build collaborative partnerships across the organization while promoting trust, accountability, and shared ownership of enterprise transformation initiatives.


Other Duties

  • Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned.


Other Skills and Abilities:


  • Stay ahead of emerging trends in finance technology and innovation, ensuring the finance function leverages the latest tools to stay competitive.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities to navigate complex governance issues.
  • Ability to communicate effectively with executive level employees, Tribal members & staff from a variety of backgrounds and maintain favorable working relationships.
  • Effectively skilled in exercising a high degree of initiative, judgment, discretion, and decision-making to achieve organizational objectives.
  • Must be dependable and flexible with work schedule.
  • Ability to leverage technology to drive organizational effectiveness including, but not limited to, Microsoft Office 365, Microsoft Dynamics Business Central, Power BI or G Suite and skills, with the ability to familiarize and operate organizational-specific programs and software.
  • Maintain the highest standard of confidentiality in all areas as required.
  • Must be highly ethical and possess a prominent level of integrity.
  • May supervise project teams or cross-functional working groups as assigned.

Essential Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Business Administration, or related field required; Master’s degree preferred.
  • CPA, CMA, or similar professional credential preferred.
  • Eight or more years of progressive leadership experience in Tribal gaming, hospitality, or large-scale enterprise finance transformation.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of Tribal operations, including government, gaming, hospitality, or business enterprise operations.
  • Proven experience in finance process transformation, organizational effectiveness, staff development, project management, and change management
  • Experience with ERP implementation (preferably Microsoft Dynamics Business Central or similar platforms), data analytics, and visualization tools.
  • Certification in project management, change management, or process improvement methodologies (e.g., Six Sigma, Lean) preferred.
  • Advanced technology skills, including proficiency with Microsoft 365, Microsoft Dynamics Business Central, Power BI, Power Automate, and other finance-related software.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present complex financial concepts to non-financial stakeholders.
  • Willingness to learn and respect Pottawatomi culture and traditions; experience working in diverse, multicultural environments preferred.


Physical Requirements:

  • Ability to read, analyze, interpret, and communicate information through written, verbal, and electronic means.
  • Ability to use standard office equipment, computers, mobile devices, presentation technology, and other equipment necessary to perform essential job functions.
  • Ability to view and interpret information displayed on computer screens, reports, presentations, and other business documents for extended periods of time.
  • Ability to distinguish colors, letters, numbers, and symbols and maintain visual acuity necessary to perform the essential functions of the position, with or without reasonable accommodation.
  • Ability to prepare, review, and present reports, business analyses, presentations, and strategic plans.
  • Ability to access and travel throughout all property locations, including casino, hotel, entertainment, food and beverage, administrative, retail, and operational areas.
  • Ability to remain stationary for extended periods while working at a computer, attending meetings, reviewing materials, or conducting presentations.
  • Ability to move about the property regularly to observe operations, interact with guests and Team Members, and attend meetings and events.
  • Ability to occasionally lift, carry, push, pull, or move materials and equipment consistent with normal executive and administrative responsibilities.


Work Environment:

  • Must possess the ability to work in a varied-paced, multi-tasking environment, sitting for extended periods of time, bending, lifting, and reaching.
  • May require non-traditional hours, including evenings, weekends, and holidays as required to meet deadlines.
  • Ability and willingness to travel, locally and out of state, for meetings and continuing education.
  • Commitment to ongoing professional development in finance transformation, technology, and Tribal governance.
  • Willingness to learn Pottawatomi culture and traditions.
  • Responsible for safeguarding sensitive financial and operational data in compliance with Tribal, state, and federal regulations.

title: Director of MDS
description:
Title: Director of MDS

ABOUT THE COMPANY

Cherry Brook Health Care Center, a division of New Horizons, Inc. is a stand alone 100 skilled nursing facility located in Canton, CT. Our dedicated staff provides individualized care with compassion, dignity and respect. Our facility has spacious private and semiprivate rooms, a well-appointed dining area, comfortable lounges and a beautiful landscaped outdoor terrace.

Cherry Brook’s mission is to provide the highest quality of care and customer service to our residents and their families by using best practices, highly trained staff and innovative programs and services designed to meet their needs.

PURPOSE OF YOUR POSITION:

The primary purpose of your job position is to plan, organize and direct the MDS process in accordance with federal and state standards, guidelines, and regulation that govern our facility.

RESPONSIBILITIES INCLUDE:

  • Coordination of MDS process.
  • Identifies data integrity weaknesses in medical records and communicates findings.
  • Issues and delivers denial notices timely and appropriately.
  • Complete and transmit all CMS approved item sets (MDS)
  • Must be knowledgeable of and follow current CMS regulatory guidelines as described in RAI Manual.
  • PPS must know current Medicare as per MBM.
  • Attendance at RCCs to lead discussion, documenting appropriately.
  • Schedule interim conference for condition changes: i.e., URI, UTI, Cataract Surgery, etc. (OBRA)
  • Attend morning report, maintain communication and rehab services, nursing staff and others to keep abreast of resident condition change.
  • Complies with facility privacy policies and procedures and protects residents’ individual health information.
  • Maintains Medicare meeting minutes per Medicare program agreement.
  • Daily review with rehab manager (or designee) of minutes and rehab status.
  • Issues and delivers Medicare BN (denial letters) per CMS regulation.
  • Assures appropriate management of residents’ Medicare/Insurance benefits.
  • Maintains adequate systems to ensure appropriate document (i.e., MD certs, IDT program, insurance authorization) is sufficient to support billed services.
  • Fully complies with all federal and state laws and standards of ethical and professional conduct applicable to the position.
  • Knowledge about laws and regulations relating to job responsibilities, e.g., EEO, OSHA, patient rights, HIPAA, fraud/abuse laws.
  • Participates in triple check process.
  • Completes and maintains all documentation as appropriate.
  • Demonstrates strong computer skills and demonstrates ownership over the MDS department, working in conjunction with part time MDS staff.

EDUCATION:

title: Senior DevOps Engineer (all genders) | Data Platform
location: Remote oder Köln / Darmstadt / Düsseldorf / Berlin
description:
Anstellungsdetails

Permanent Contract, Full- or Part-Time, Remote or Cologne / Düsseldorf / Darmstadt / Berlin


Info

Who we areWe are the tech powerhouse behind Kaufland’s international online marketplaces and a company within the Schwarz Group. Driven by a start-up mentality and working on an equal footing within flat hierarchies, we develop the best marketplace solutions for our customers, sellers and partners. #FromEuropeForEurope

Day by day, our Tech & Product Team of about 400 experts pursues the goal of creating the best possible customer shopping experience for our online marketplace. Through innovative technical developments, they not only create an outstanding shopping experience but also lay the foundation for an optimal selling experience for our sellers. Learn more about our division, areas, and cross-functional teams here!


Aufgaben

Your tasks – this is what awaits you in detail

  • You run and own our self-hosted Apache Kafka backbone and Schema Registry end-to-end, managing ACLs, client quotas, certificates, upgrades, and disaster recovery
  • You operate our Debezium-based change data capture pipelines, overseeing connectors, snapshots, offsets, replica lag, and BigQuery sink loaders
  • You run our workloads on Kubernetes, including Navarch - our self-built workflow orchestrator executing ~7,500 SQL and Python tasks daily - owning resource management, autoscaling, and debugging
  • You automate and own access management and infrastructure as code across our self-hosted GitLab CI/CD pipelines, replacing manual tickets with code-driven policies
  • You own observability and infra costs - Datadog across Kafka and sink loaders, Slack-native alerting, and maintaining an honest view of K8s, Kafka retention, and log volume expenses
  • You carry your share of triage, one week in three - handling ingestion and access requests, schema alerts, and supporting analysts, while helping automate this layer via AI-assisted review
  • You act as a senior sparring partner alongside two senior data engineers (reporting to the Head of Data & Analytics) - driving design reviews and multi-quarter initiatives, with room to grow into BigQuery architecture over time: access frameworks, partitioning and slot strategy, the pipelines and models on top
  • Optional: You take part in our 24/7 on-call rotation


Profil

Your profile – this is what we expect from you

  • You have several years of experience operating production infrastructure you were personally responsible for, including on-call rotation. You have run systems that broke, can explain what went wrong and how you permanently fixed it, and can detail a specific trade-off you navigated backed by concrete numbers
  • You have deep hands-on expertise in Apache Kafka broker operations, including cluster sizing, partition rebalancing, replication, ISR behavior, and version upgrades
  • You have operated cross-system data replication in production - ideally Debezium on Kafka Connect, or database replication via binlog, GTID, WAL, or agent-based pipelines
  • You demonstrate strong production experience with Kubernetes, master resource management and autoscaling, and possess sharp debugging reflexes for complex failure modes
  • You manage infrastructure and access as code across multiple environments (ideally Terraform and Ansible; Pulumi, Helm or serious configuration management also counts) following a strict least-privilege IAM approach across multiple environments, ideally with GCP experience or transferable AWS/Azure knowledge
  • You use production-grade Python and SQL as practical tools, applying a cost-conscious mindset to query performance, scanning volume, and data pruning
  • You thrive in a low-process, Kanban-driven environment where seniors self-organize, rotate weekly triage duties without micro-management, and prefer automating recurring requests over manually repeating them
  • Optional: You bring skills or interest in object-oriented design, data modeling/dbt, BigQuery architecture, orchestration frameworks (Airflow, Dagster), stream processing (Beam, Flink, Spark), or internal automation (n8n, AI triage bots).
  • You are fluent in English (C1 level) and enjoy working in an international team environment


Benefits

What we offer

  • Create your own work-life balance: You have the flexibility to choose between working remotely (within Germany) or from one of our locations in Cologne, Darmstadt, Düsseldorf, or in Berlin!
  • Do you want to move to Germany? No problem – we offer you an attractive relocation package to give you a smooth start.
  • Urban Sports Club and RSG Group Fitness Studios: Get top deals for fitness, swimming, yoga and more
  • Mental Well-Being: We support you on your well-being journey with special offerings such as Instahelp, the digital platform for online psychological counseling
  • Vacation & Sabbatical: Enjoy 30 days of vacation per year and the opportunity to take a sabbatical once you have been part of the team for a certain period!
  • Option for Pluxee restaurant vouchers: Buy Pluxee vouchers through us and benefit from tax-advantaged meal allowances!
  • ‘Deutschlandticket’: We subsidize your train season ticket for more mobility
  • Employee Discount: You will receive a monthly coupon for Kaufland.de
  • Free choice of operating system: MacOS or Ubuntu Linux, it's up to you
  • Boost your growth: Benefit from our online language learning programs, diverse in-house training, and our automated 360-degree feedback. We cover the costs for relevant conferences, training opportunities, and approved team workshops to strengthen personal interactions
  • This is who we are: Our dynamic culture combines flat hierarchies, a start-up mentality, an international team of over 65 nationalities, and the strength of the Schwarz Group to provide you an agile and secure working environment.
  • We are team players: From day one, you will connect not only with your team but also with others through our digital onboarding journey, the buddy program, and regular team and company events, all-hands meetings, powerful mornings, and much more!
Check out our Principles & our blog for even more insights into our company culture!

We are signatories to the Charta der Vielfalt (German Diversity Charter) – because we know that extraordinary things can only be achieved with diversity. Read more here! As we have very international teams, we would highly appreciate it to receive your CV or profile link in English.

We are looking forward to your application!

title: Parts Counter Clerk
location: Morgan City, LA, Morgan City, LA, US
description:
About Company:

At Morgan City Toyota, we're not just selling cars; we're building a team that's as passionate about service as we are about vehicles.

As a new and growing, truly customer-centric business, we pride ourselves on offering competitive prices and exceptional service to our customers.

For our employees, this means a dynamic and supportive environment where hard work is recognized, growth is encouraged, and fun is a key ingredient in our daily operations.

We believe that when our team is happy and thriving, they naturally deliver the outstanding experiences our customers have come to expect,

making Morgan City Toyota and the Buddy Automotive Group a rewarding place to achieve your career goals.

About the Role:

The Automotive Parts Counter Clerk plays a crucial role in ensuring the smooth operation of automotive parts sales and inventory management within a retail or wholesale environment. This position is responsible for providing exceptional customer service by accurately identifying and supplying the correct automotive parts to customers, technicians, and service personnel. The role requires maintaining organized inventory records, processing sales transactions efficiently, and assisting with stock replenishment to meet customer demand. The clerk acts as a knowledgeable resource, offering technical information and guidance on parts compatibility and usage. Ultimately, this position supports the overall success of the parts department by facilitating timely and accurate parts distribution, contributing to customer satisfaction and operational efficiency.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • Basic knowledge of automotive parts and terminology.
  • Experience with point-of-sale (POS) systems and inventory management software.
  • Strong customer service and communication skills.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced environment and handle multiple tasks simultaneously.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Previous experience working in an automotive parts department or related retail environment.
  • Familiarity with automotive repair processes and vehicle systems.
  • Proficiency with computerized parts catalog systems and ordering platforms.
  • Ability to lift and move automotive parts weighing up to 50 pounds safely.
  • Certification or coursework related to automotive technology or parts management.

Responsibilities:

  • Greet customers promptly and professionally, assessing their automotive parts needs and providing expert assistance.
  • Identify and locate automotive parts using catalogs, computer systems, and product knowledge to ensure accurate order fulfillment.
  • Process sales transactions, including cash, credit, and invoicing, while maintaining accurate records of sales and inventory.
  • Manage inventory by receiving shipments, stocking shelves, conducting regular inventory counts, and reporting discrepancies.
  • Collaborate with service technicians and other departments to ensure timely parts availability and resolve any order issues.
  • Maintain a clean and organized parts counter and storage area to facilitate efficient operations.
  • Provide technical information and advice on automotive parts, compatibility, and installation when requested.

Skills:

The required skills enable the clerk to efficiently identify and locate automotive parts, ensuring customers receive the correct items promptly. Strong communication and customer service skills are essential for understanding customer needs and providing clear, helpful information. Proficiency with POS and inventory software supports accurate transaction processing and inventory tracking, which are critical for maintaining stock levels and minimizing errors. Preferred skills, such as familiarity with automotive repair and parts catalog systems, enhance the clerk's ability to assist customers with technical questions and streamline ordering processes. Physical stamina and organizational skills contribute to maintaining a well-stocked and orderly parts counter, supporting overall operational effectiveness.

Our programs and services include crisis shelter and transitional housing for survivors and their families, counseling, SAFEPLAN court advocacy, community education, supervised visitation, and vocational training for youth. The YWCA provides services at several sites, including Holyoke, Northampton, Westfield, and our primary Springfield campus.

  • Foster a positive working environment.
  • Communicate openly and contribute to the development of others.
  • Coordinate efforts across teams, programs, and partner organizations.

Position Purpose

The Llámanos Hotline Advocate provides support, advocacy and crisis response on our 24-hour hotline for survivors of domestic violence, sexual violence, and human trafficking, significant others, and professionals. Hotline Workers are part of a team model working with peers, supervisors, and outside connections to best serve those calling our hotline.

Essential Responsibilities

  • Provide trauma-informed, strengths-based telephone interventions that incorporate safety planning and assessment of immediate needs;
  • Answer 24-hour Llámanos Hotline Line within the first three rings, unless assisting another caller;
  • Provide back-up support to the YW’s new Homelessness Helpline by responding to calls, helping the caller to create a safety plan, and making referrals to the Outreach Worker or Case Manager;
  • Ensure bed-update system receives a login and updates/changes within the 1st hour of each shift and again as space changes;

Qualifications

  • Associate’s degree or equivalent preferred, or 1 - 3 years of experience in human services;
  • Spanish Bilingual;
  • Verbal, written, and organizational skills, including strong computer skills;
  • Ability to resolve conflict using de-escalation techniques and trauma informed skills;
  • Prior experience working with survivors of violence and/or those who have perpetrated violence in an intimate partner relationship;
  • Experience and knowledge of child development and impact of domestic violence on children;
