title: Fiber Route Patrolle - Wickenburg, AZ
description:
Fiber Route Patroller

Role Overview

The Fiber Route Patroller is a field-based role focused on proactive fiber route patrol, infrastructure inspection, and damage prevention. The position supports the integrity and security of long-haul fiber infrastructure by identifying potential risks, monitoring activity near fiber routes, documenting field conditions, and escalating concerns when appropriate.

The role requires a combination of field awareness, basic knowledge of telecommunications and underground utilities, and the ability to safely operate in construction and outside-plant environments.

Responsibilities

  • Conduct regular patrols of long-haul fiber routes to identify potential risks, damage, construction activity, or environmental threats.
  • Inspect fiber infrastructure, including cabinets, handholes, markers, access points, and buried cable routes.
  • Monitor third-party construction and excavation activity near fiber routes to help prevent damage to critical infrastructure.
  • Support utility locating activities using standard locating techniques and available mapping and utility records.
  • Read and interpret maps, utility prints, construction drawings, and other records to understand fiber placement and identify potential risks.
  • Respond to active construction sites or other areas of concern near fiber infrastructure and assess potential exposure or risk.
  • Identify and escalate conditions that may threaten fiber infrastructure, including excavation activity, damaged facilities, exposed infrastructure, or changes in site conditions.
  • Document field activities, site conditions, construction activity, infrastructure observations, and utility information.
  • Support damage investigations by collecting field information, photographs, site observations, and other relevant documentation.
  • Maintain infrastructure security and site integrity through routine inspections and timely reporting of concerns.
  • Coordinate and communicate effectively with field technicians, engineers, utility locators, contractors, construction crews, and other stakeholders.
  • Follow applicable safety requirements, including OSHA guidelines and established field safety procedures.
  • Operate effectively in both independent and team environments.
  • Maintain assigned vehicles, tools, and field equipment in safe working condition.
  • Perform other related field and damage-prevention duties as required.

Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.
  • Two (2) or more years of relevant field, utility, telecommunications, construction, or outside-plant experience preferred.
  • Basic knowledge of telecommunications infrastructure, underground utilities, construction, or fiber optic systems preferred.
  • Familiarity with utility locating practices and equipment is preferred.
  • Ability to read and interpret maps, utility prints, construction drawings, and related field documentation.
  • OSHA or other applicable safety certifications preferred.
  • Ability to develop technical knowledge related to fiber infrastructure, utility locating, construction practices, and damage prevention.
  • Ability to work outdoors in varying weather, terrain, and environmental conditions.
  • Ability to work safely around construction sites, roadways, and utility infrastructure.
  • Strong attention to detail, situational awareness, communication skills, and willingness to learn.
  • Valid driver’s license and ability to safely operate a vehicle as required for field responsibilities.

title: Product Developer

  • Partner closely with Designers to execute seasonal collections that align with customer needs and brand standards.
  • Manage seasonal Time & Action (T&A) calendars and ensure all development milestones are achieved on schedule.

  • Review silhouettes, fabrications, trims, washes, graphics, embellishments, and construction details to ensure product integrity.

Fabric & Trim Development

  • Collaborate with Sourcing to identify cost-effective materials while maintaining design intent.

Licensing & Brand Compliance

  • Coordinate licensed product approvals and submissions according to licensor timelines.
  • Ensure artwork, product execution, labeling, and packaging comply with licensor guidelines.
  • Track approval status and communicate revisions with internal teams and vendors.


Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partner with Production to ensure a smooth transition from development into bulk production.
  • Work with Technical Design to address fit and construction issues.
  • Collaborate with Merchandising and Sales to ensure products meet customer requirements.
  • Coordinate with Sourcing to support target costing and supplier capabilities.


Reporting & Documentation

  • Maintain accurate development calendars, WIP reports, sample trackers, and approval logs.
  • Organize development files, specifications, BOMs, artwork, and seasonal documentation.
  • Prepare status updates for management and cross-functional meetings.
  • Ensure all development documentation is complete before production handoff.


Continuous Improvement

  • Identify opportunities to improve product development processes and communication.
  • Stay informed on apparel trends, consumer preferences, fabric innovations, and manufacturing capabilities.
  • Support initiatives that improve speed to market, quality, and operational efficiency.


Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Fashion Design, Product Development, Fashion Merchandising, Apparel Production, or a related field preferred.

Experience

  • 3–5 years of experience in Apparel Product Development, Design, or Product Management.
  • Experience with licensed apparel, private label, or mass-market retail programs preferred.
  • Experience working with overseas factories and international vendors.
  • Strong understanding of garment construction and apparel manufacturing processes.


This is a temporary, 2-month assignment with the possibility of transitioning to a permanent, full-time position based on business needs and performance.

title: Senior Director, Finance
location: Hudson Yards, NY, New York, NY, US
description:
COMPANY PROFILE: EQUINOX HOTELS


Equinox Hotels is a luxury lifestyle hospitality brand built on the evolution of Equinox and its experience-defining approach. Adapting Equinox’s founding principles to hospitality, the brand has envisioned and introduced a new category of modern luxury - purposeful, performance-driven, and restorative.

Equinox Hotels is designed to amplify each guest’s stay at the intersection of work, play, movement, nourishment, and regeneration. These pillars are woven into every touchpoint, expressed through meticulous attention to detail and elevated service standards, the on-site fitness Club, Food & Beverage, The Spa by Equinox Hotels, and the in-room experience. Born from an esteemed global fitness platform with a loyal following in major cities worldwide, Equinox Hotels occupies a category of its own - where hospitality, wellness, and lifestyle converge for a guest who values design, discretion, performance, and personalization over traditional luxury formality.

THE OPPORTUNITY

This is a rare opportunity to help shape the financial infrastructure of a growing luxury hospitality brand at a formative stage. As Senior Director of Finance, you will serve as the senior corporate finance leader for Equinox Hotels, supporting the President and leadership team as the portfolio expands from its current flagship operation to multiple properties.

The Senior Director of Finance is responsible for corporate and portfolio financial planning, accounting oversight, reporting, internal controls, owner and lender reporting, and finance systems. The role also provides direct leadership and support to property Directors of Finance (DOFs), establishing consistent standards and scalable processes across the portfolio.

You will report directly to the President and operate as a trusted financial partner to leadership, ownership, and hotel teams, balancing hands-on execution with forward-looking analysis. The right person will be equally comfortable reviewing a hotel P&L, improving an accounting process, guiding a DOF, presenting to ownership, and building the tools required to support growth.


ROLE SCOPE & RESPONSIBILITIES


Financial Leadership & Strategy

  • Serve as the senior corporate finance partner to the President and leadership team, providing insight and recommendations on financial planning, budgeting, capital allocation, cash flow, and business performance.
  • Develop and maintain multi-year forecasts, scenario analyses, annual budgets, and portfolio performance models that support operating and growth decisions.
  • Develop and continuously refine the financial reporting infrastructure, ensuring leadership and ownership receive timely, accurate, and actionable insight into performance, trends, opportunities, and risks.
  • Partner with functional and hotel leaders to define and track KPIs, translating operational activity into financial outcomes and identifying opportunities to improve profitability and productivity.


Property Finance Leadership & Performance Management

  • Directly lead, mentor, and develop property Directors of Finance, establishing clear expectations for financial performance, reporting quality, controls, and partnership with General Managers and operating leaders.
  • Establish and maintain standardized accounting policies, reporting frameworks, chart-of-accounts standards, and internal control requirements across corporate and property finance teams.
  • Conduct regular property financial and operational reviews, including GOP, EBITDA, NOI, forecast accuracy, cost controls, productivity, working capital, and other relevant performance measures.
  • Support property DOFs in budgeting, forecasting, audits, owner reporting, corrective action plans, and the resolution of significant accounting or control matters.
  • Ensure property Directors of Finance comply with HMA terms, including but not limited to fee calculations, allocations, and reporting requirements.


Ownership, Asset Management & Lender Relations

  • Serve as a key financial interface with ownership and investment partners, managing reporting cadences, responding to financial inquiries, and supporting alignment between ownership objectives and operational execution.
  • Review annual business plans and capital expenditure programs and provide recommendations to leadership and ownership; monitor property performance against approved plans and investment objectives.
  • Serve as the day-to-day finance contact for lenders across reporting, covenant compliance, appraisals, and site visits; support refinancing and new financing initiatives.
  • Monitor financial obligations under leases, hotel management agreements, loan documents, and other material agreements, coordinating with leadership and legal counsel when interpretation or amendments are required.
  • Support the negotiation of amendments to hotel management agreements, loan documents, and partnership or shareholder agreements, working with leadership and outside counsel.
  • Support ongoing asset reviews and value-creation initiatives focused on revenue growth, margin improvement, cash flow, NOI, and long-term asset performance.


Accounting, SOP Governance & Internal Controls

  • Oversee corporate and portfolio accounting processes, treasury and cash management reporting, consolidations, and close/reporting disciplines, ensuring accuracy, consistency, and continuous improvement.
  • Establish, implement, and continuously refine finance and accounting Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) across corporate and property teams.
  • Maintain a robust internal control framework to safeguard assets and promote financial integrity; conduct periodic control and process reviews, identify gaps, and coordinate corrective actions.
  • Ensure compliance with GAAP (IFRS Internationally) and applicable accounting standards, federal, state, and local tax requirements, management agreements, lender requirements, and ownership reporting standards.


Audit, Tax & Compliance

  • Coordinate and oversee external audit processes at corporate and property levels, including audit schedules, financial statements, supporting documentation, and timely resolution of findings.
  • Serve as a primary finance contact for external auditors, tax advisors, ownership representatives, and other financial stakeholders.
  • Coordinate tax compliance and reporting with internal and external resources, ensuring required filings and support are complete and timely. (US)
  • Stay current on labor policies, regulations, and collective bargaining requirements that affect the operating portfolio, partnering with Operations and People teams on financial and compliance implications. (US)


Financial Systems & Reporting Infrastructure

  • Own the functional roadmap and administration of finance and reporting systems, including accounting platforms, consolidation and reporting tools, and integrations with PMS, POS, and other operating systems.
  • Partner with internal resources, external vendors, and consultants to select, implement, integrate, maintain, and improve financial systems and reporting tools appropriate for a scalable multi-property operation.
  • Maintain data integrity, reporting structures, and standardized financial master data; identify opportunities to automate recurring processes and improve efficiency and control.
  • Coordinate troubleshooting, upgrades, and finance-system enhancements, ensuring business continuity and appropriate documentation.


Growth & Expansion

  • Assist Development Team as needed to build and present pro forma financial models for new properties, development opportunities, and potential acquisitions, including market assumptions, scenario modeling, and investment-return analysis.
  • Partner with Development, Operations, PropCo, and ownership groups on financial diligence, underwriting support, pre-opening planning, and evaluation of new opportunities.
  • Support market and competitive analyses and assess the operating and capital implications of proposed growth initiatives.
  • Maintain short- and long-term cash flow and capital forecasts to support liquidity planning and portfolio growth.


Team & Culture

  • Build and develop a high-performing finance organization as the portfolio grows, creating clear accountability, strong technical standards, and consistent development opportunities for finance leaders.
  • Communicate financial complexity clearly to non-finance audiences, helping leaders understand performance drivers, tradeoffs, and actions required.
  • Promote a culture of precision, discipline, transparency, continuous improvement, and high performance aligned with the Equinox Hotels brand.

WHO YOU ARE

  • You are a seasoned hospitality finance leader who is equally comfortable working with ownership and senior leadership and operating in the details of hotel financial performance. You thrive in a lean, entrepreneurial environment where the finance leader is expected to be hands-on, resourceful, commercially minded, and accountable for execution.
  • You think and act like a partner, not just a function head.
  • You combine strategic perspective with strong accounting and operational finance discipline, and you know when to move from analysis to action.
  • You communicate financial complexity clearly to ownership groups, hotel operators, executive teams, and non-finance partners, earning trust through accuracy, consistency, and sound judgment.
  • You are forward-looking: you do not simply report what happened; you identify what is changing, why it matters, and what should happen next.
  • You are comfortable building and improving processes in an evolving organization without sacrificing control, accuracy, or accountability.
  • You are a strong coach and team builder who can elevate property finance leaders while maintaining clear standards across the portfolio.
  • You are a multiplier — people grow professionally around you, and you create the conditions for that intentionally.
  • You are comfortable with ambiguity and growth, and you understand that scaling from one hotel to a multi-property portfolio requires stronger systems, governance, and consistency at every stage.


CANDIDATE PROFILE

Required

  • 10+ years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including significant leadership experience in the hospitality industry.
  • Demonstrated experience overseeing hotel financial operations across portfolio of properties, with direct exposure to property Directors of Finance or comparable finance leaders.
  • Strong command of hotel financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, internal controls, audits, cash flow, and owner reporting.
  • Meaningful experience with asset management, ownership structures, management agreements, and lender or financing requirements.
  • Demonstrated ability to build or improve scalable financial processes, reporting infrastructure, and SOPs in a lean or growing organization.
  • Strong relationship-management and communication skills with ownership, operators, auditors, lenders, vendors, and senior leadership.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.


Preferred

  • CPA, MBA, or other relevant advanced credentials.
  • Experience in luxury or lifestyle hospitality brands and multi-property environments.
  • Background in real estate finance, asset management, development, or other asset-intensive businesses.
  • Experience evaluating, implementing, integrating, and administering hotel finance and reporting systems.


COMPENSATION PACKAGE

  • Base Salary: $240,000.00 to $250,000.00 (commensurate with experience)
  • Annual Incentive Bonus: 30% target bonus opportunity
  • Benefits/Perquisites: Complimentary Equinox Club “All Access” Membership for one (1)

Equinox Hotels is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

title: Logs and Records Clerk
description:
About AVMAC LLC:

AVMAC was founded by two former Naval Aviation Maintenance Officers, Bert Ortiz and Don Buzard, who collectively have more than eight decades of experience assigned to, or directly supporting, both carrier and amphibious aviation.

AVMAC’s corporate staff and leadership team employ many with similar backgrounds and experience, which makes it a highly knowledgeable force multiplier to their customer base. The company prides itself on hiring, recruiting and training veterans as it continues to serve the Department of Defense and the Department of Transportation Homeland Security and commercial customers nationwide.

Position Summary:

The Logs and Records Clerk is responsible for maintaining accurate and up-to-date records on aircraft maintenance, inspections, and modifications for the FA-18 aircraft. This role involves managing logbooks, aeronautical equipment service records (AESRs), historical documents, and electronic databases. The clerk ensures compliance with aviation maintenance directives, supports operational readiness, and assists in audits, inspections, and reporting.

This position is Fulltime, hourly position and the job duties are performed onsite on Marine Corps Air Station Miramar, located in San Diego, California.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Key duties include initiating and updating aircraft logbooks, tracking component life limits and scheduled maintenance, coordinating with maintenance control, and verifying entries for accuracy and completeness. The clerk serves as a vital link between maintenance personnel, quality assurance, and command leadership, contributing directly to aircraft airworthiness and mission capability.
  • Thorough knowledge of the OPNAVINST 4790.2H, Naval maintenance publications, maintenance requirement cards, aircraft and engine logbooks, scheduled removal component cards, and the ability to document maintenance utilizing the Naval Aviation Logistics Command Information System (NALCOMIS).
  • Possess extensive knowledge of Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Must have the ability to document all maintenance performed at the Organizational maintenance level.
  • Capable of preparing Naval correspondence documents, maintaining Naval aircraft maintenance publications/files, and the ability to prepare, and analyze maintenance reports.
  • Operate data entry equipment, set up, operate, and perform minor maintenance on the Naval Aviation Logistics Command Management Information System (NALCOMIS) hardware and its associated remote peripheral subsystems.
  • Analyze charts, graphs, and man-hour statistical information to aid maintenance managers and logisticians.

Qualifications, Knowledge and Skills Required:

  • Five years’ aircraft maintenance administration experience.
  • Must have completed the Naval Aviation Maintenance Administration Course and the Data Analysis Course, or a military/civilian equivalent

Physical and Environmental Requirements:

  • This position requires normal physical functions.
  • Work will require frequent bending, reaching and climbing.
  • Frequently lift and carry items weighing up to fifty pounds and occasionally lift heavier items with the assistance of other workers.
  • Work may be performed on top or under equipment in cramped or awkward positions.

What We Offer: (benefits vary based on FT, PT, or On-Call status)

  • Benefits offered include Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance
  • Employer-paid Life insurance, long-term disability and short-term disability
  • Paid time off -including 11 Holidays (8 hours per holiday)
  • Participation in the AVMAC LLC 401(k) plan

The hourly rate for this position is $48.79 (this does not include Health and Welfare)

This position is subject to union and Collective Bargaining requirements.

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by the individual(s) assigned to this position. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, and skills required. Management reserves the right to modify, add, or remove duties and to assign other duties as necessary.

title: Inventory Control Specialist
description:

title: Packaging & Product Photographer Designer
description:
Position Summary

  • Strong understanding of print production, packaging materials, and manufacturing processes.
  • Experience preparing production-ready artwork and print files.
  • Excellent typography, layout, color, and composition skills.
  • Strong photo retouching and image editing abilities.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects while meeting tight deadlines.
  • Exceptional attention to detail and organizational skills.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.

Preferred

  • Experience working with licensed consumer products.
  • Experience designing packaging for apparel, accessories, gifts, toys, or consumer goods.
  • Knowledge of photography lighting equipment and studio setup.
  • Experience with digital asset management systems.
  • Understanding of retailer packaging requirements.
  • Experience working with overseas manufacturing partners.

Technical Skills

  • Adobe Illustrator
  • Adobe Photoshop (Advanced)
  • Adobe InDesign
  • Adobe Lightroom
  • Microsoft Office Suite
  • Mac OS environment
  • Product photography equipment and lighting
  • Color management and print production
  • Packaging die lines and prepress preparation
  • File management and digital asset organization


Key Competencies

  • Creative Thinking
  • Packaging Design Expertise
  • Product Photography

  • Print Production Knowledge
  • Attention to Detail
  • Time Management
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration
  • Problem Solving

Working Conditions

At Mad Engine Global, creativity drives everything we do. title: COMM/NAV Tech II
description:
About AVMAC LLC:

AVMAC was founded by two former Naval Aviation Maintenance Officers, Bert Ortiz and Don Buzard, who collectively have more than eight decades of experience assigned to, or directly supporting, both carrier and amphibious aviation.

AVMAC’s corporate staff and leadership team employ many with similar backgrounds and experience, which makes it a highly knowledgeable force multiplier to their customer base. The company prides itself on hiring, recruiting and training veterans as it continues to serve the Department of Defense and the Department of Transportation Homeland Security and commercial customers nationwide.

Position Summary: A highly skilled and detail-oriented F/A-18 COM/NAV Collateral Duty Inspector (CDI) is responsible for performing, inspecting, and verifying the installation, maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair of communication and navigation systems on F/A-18 aircraft. This role ensures that all COM/NAV system work is completed in accordance with Naval Aviation Maintenance Program (NAMP) standards and safety protocols.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Troubleshoots malfunctions in F/A18 airframe, weapons, and engine electrical systems of moderate difficulty at the organizational maintenance level. This technician repairs, replaces, and rebuilds electrical system wiring, connectors, and components using hand tools, power tools, and applicable test equipment. This technician reads and interprets manufactures maintenance manuals service bulletins, technical data, engineering data and other specifications to determine the feasibility and method of repairing or replacing damaged wiring, malfunctioning or damaged components.
  • Applies professional technical expertise and guidance to solve complex problems by interpreting technical data such as blueprints or manufacturers manuals. Work typically requires a thoroughly comprehensive knowledge of aircraft mechanical component troubleshooting/repair procedures, and replacement of components, a thorough knowledge of aircraft wiring systems. The ability to determine functionality of non-complex electrical systems. A detailed knowledge of aircraft unique tools such as test equipment, torque wrenches, dial indicators, micrometers, cable tension meters, sheet metal brakes and sheers, etc. is required.
  • Must possess the experience and ability to provide technical support to Electrical/mechanical engineers and customers alike must possess excellent organizational skills in prioritizing workload to meet aircraft delivery schedule. This mechanic will be required to make entries in aircraft logs and records and is responsible for providing guidance and technical expertise to lower-level technicians throughout all aircraft modifications and/or maintenance efforts

Qualifications, Knowledge and Skills Required:

  • High school diploma or GED required and must be capable of operating support equipment
  • Level II – Five (5) years previous experience as an COMNAV Technician. (CDI Experience). Must be capable of attaining Collateral Duty Inspector (CDI) within required timeframe.
  • Working knowledge of the COMNAVAIRFORINST 4790.2 Series.
  • Training to include NAMTRGD Navy AME “A” or factory equivalent ejection seat and environmental control system course of instruction.
  • Knowledge of naval maintenance publications, maintenance requirement cards, and the ability to document maintenance utilizing the Naval Aviation Logistics Command Information System (NALCOMIS).

Physical and Environmental Requirements:

  • Ability lift and carry items weighing up to fifty pounds and occasionally lift heavier items with the assistance of other workers.
  • Must be able to stand, walk, bend, and reach for extended periods.
  • This position requires normal physical functions.
  • Work may be performed on top or under equipment in cramped or awkward positions.
  • Normal color perception required.
  • Required to work in areas in the hangar and on the flightline that are noisy and dusty.
  • Exposed to heat, cold and wind

Individuals who are interested in this position should demonstrate the following qualifications and personal attributes:

  • A comprehensive background in maintenance practices.
  • Developed technical skills and experience relevant to their areas of responsibility.
  • Proficiency in researching, reading, and interpreting engineering drawings, technical manuals, and applicable directives.
  • Strong technical writing abilities, with an emphasis on clarity and accuracy. An observant, alert, and inquisitive disposition.
  • A commitment to promoting operational stability and excellence in performance.
  • Motivated and a personal drive to continually expand their technical knowledge and expertise.
  • The ability to collaborate effectively and work well with others.

What We Offer: (benefits vary based on FT, PT, or On-Call status)

  • Benefits offered include Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance
  • Employer-paid Life insurance, long-term disability and short-term disability
  • Paid time off -including 11 Holidays (8 hours per holiday)
  • Participation in the AVMAC LLC 401(k) plan

They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, and skills required. Management reserves the right to modify, add, or remove duties and to assign other duties as necessary.

AVMAC is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to a diverse workplace and affirm equal opportunity for all qualified applicants in accordance with applicable law, including affirmative action for qualified individuals with disabilities and veterans.

title: Fiber Route Patroller - Bullhead, AZ
description:
Fiber Route Patroller

Role Overview

The Fiber Route Patroller is a field-based role focused on proactive fiber route patrol, infrastructure inspection, and damage prevention. The position supports the integrity and security of long-haul fiber infrastructure by identifying potential risks, monitoring activity near fiber routes, documenting field conditions, and escalating concerns when appropriate.

The role requires a combination of field awareness, basic knowledge of telecommunications and underground utilities, and the ability to safely operate in construction and outside-plant environments.

Responsibilities

  • Conduct regular patrols of long-haul fiber routes to identify potential risks, damage, construction activity, or environmental threats.
  • Inspect fiber infrastructure, including cabinets, handholes, markers, access points, and buried cable routes.
  • Monitor third-party construction and excavation activity near fiber routes to help prevent damage to critical infrastructure.
  • Support utility locating activities using standard locating techniques and available mapping and utility records.
  • Read and interpret maps, utility prints, construction drawings, and other records to understand fiber placement and identify potential risks.
  • Respond to active construction sites or other areas of concern near fiber infrastructure and assess potential exposure or risk.
  • Identify and escalate conditions that may threaten fiber infrastructure, including excavation activity, damaged facilities, exposed infrastructure, or changes in site conditions.
  • Document field activities, site conditions, construction activity, infrastructure observations, and utility information.
  • Support damage investigations by collecting field information, photographs, site observations, and other relevant documentation.
  • Maintain infrastructure security and site integrity through routine inspections and timely reporting of concerns.
  • Coordinate and communicate effectively with field technicians, engineers, utility locators, contractors, construction crews, and other stakeholders.
  • Follow applicable safety requirements, including OSHA guidelines and established field safety procedures.
  • Operate effectively in both independent and team environments.
  • Maintain assigned vehicles, tools, and field equipment in safe working condition.
  • Perform other related field and damage-prevention duties as required.

Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.
  • Two (2) or more years of relevant field, utility, telecommunications, construction, or outside-plant experience preferred.
  • Basic knowledge of telecommunications infrastructure, underground utilities, construction, or fiber optic systems preferred.
  • Familiarity with utility locating practices and equipment is preferred.
  • Ability to read and interpret maps, utility prints, construction drawings, and related field documentation.
  • OSHA or other applicable safety certifications preferred.
  • Ability to develop technical knowledge related to fiber infrastructure, utility locating, construction practices, and damage prevention.
  • Ability to work outdoors in varying weather, terrain, and environmental conditions.
  • Ability to work safely around construction sites, roadways, and utility infrastructure.
  • Strong attention to detail, situational awareness, communication skills, and willingness to learn.
  • Valid driver’s license and ability to safely operate a vehicle as required for field responsibilities.

title: Breast Cancer Risk Assessment Associate
description:
PRIMARY FUNCTIONS: The Breast Cancer Risk Assessment Associate is part of the FOCUS Breast Cancer Screening and Linkage to Care Program, a pilot program aimed at advancing timely diagnosis of breast cancer in vulnerable populations. This role ensures that patients are assessed for their risk of developing breast cancer and receive follow up genetic counseling and testing in a timely fashion so that patients receive appropriate screening. Incumbent will assist with developing preliminary risk screening tool, conducting screening outreach to patients, contacting patients to perform full breast cancer risk assessments, assisting patients with follow-up testing and appointments for counseling, and ensuring that patient data is accurately collected, tracked, and analyzed.

Incumbent must have a deep interest in women’s health and/or cancer screening, be bilingual in Spanish and English, and have a strong commitment to Neighborhood Health’s mission to improve health and advance health equity by providing high-quality primary care regardless of ability to pay.

• Administer full breast cancer risk assessment for patients with initial positive screen

• For patients at elevated risk, ensure patients are connected to genetic counseling and testing

• Assist patients with financial aid applications as needed

• Educate patients about the importance of assessing risk and genetic counseling and testing through phone calls and texting

• Educate patients on risk assessment results and what it means for breast cancer screening

• Refer patients needing special breast imaging cadence to their medical provider and breast cancer screening navigators

• Manage the database tracking risk assessment outreach, results, and connection to genetic testing, counseling, and specialty care if necessary

• Assist navigation team with making appointments at radiology providers by calling the patient, scheduling their mammogram, asking required patient assessment questions, sending appointment reminders, and arranging for transportation if needed

• Follow up with unable-to-reach clients and assess reasons for declining risk assessments and/or genetic testing and counseling, and identify patterns and barriers and rescheduling no-shows

• Document all patient interactions and ensure risk assessment results and outside testing are in electronic medical record

title: Project Manager

description:
Insidesource DEI Statement

By nurturing a culture where everyone experiences a deep sense of belonging and equity of opportunity, we will uphold our vision to “unleash human and business potential.” We commit to being an anti-ism workplace and embedding diversity, equity, and inclusion throughout our business.


Job Summary

The Project Manager is responsible for leading all aspects of labor scope, scheduling, logistics, and budget management for complex commercial furniture projects. This role combines expertise in project management, construction coordination, and furniture systems to ensure projects remain on schedule, risks are proactively identified and mitigated, and documentation is accurate, timely, and clearly communicated. The Project Manager plays a critical role in delivering exceptional client experiences by effectively coordinating with internal cross-functional teams, clients, and external project stakeholders. Through strong leadership, communication, and execution, the Project Manager ensures projects run smoothly from inception through final completion.

Request for Proposal (RFP) Participation

  • Participates in team interviews as a project management and logistics subject matter expert.

Planning

  • Participates in project meetings with clients and internal teams (Sales, Sales Support, Design) to develop and track project objectives, scope of work, timelines, and budgets.
  • Leverages technical and industry expertise to identify, anticipate, and mitigate project risks impacting quality, schedule, or budget.
  • Develops work plans, micro-schedules, and logistics strategies, organizing deliveries based on project parameters, scope, timeline, and customer goals.
  • Participates in Owner/Architect/Contractor (OAC) meetings as required.
  • Ensures compliance with building requirements by obtaining Certificates of Insurance and coordinating all rules and regulations, site protection, security protocols, and required training.
  • Serves as the primary point of contact for project scheduling, logistics, and third-party trade coordination, including architecture and design firms, contractors, cabling vendors, building managers, electricians, movers, client facilities teams, and IT groups.
  • Maintains detailed project documentation of key decisions, customer requests, and revisions.
  • Provides timely, formal written communication throughout the project lifecycle and disseminates critical information to clients and project teams.
  • Reviews furniture plans and specifications prior to installation for accuracy, completeness, and alignment with project scope.


Budget Management

  • Collaborates with labor providers to request, review, and finalize labor quotes, time-and-materials work, and associated change orders throughout the project.
  • Estimates and tracks Project Management service fees.
  • Ensures reporting requirements are met for prevailing wage projects in compliance with DIR/DAS standards.

Site Management

  • Completes site surveys to validate conditions, field dimensions, and paths of travel, ensuring furniture can be delivered and installed as planned and fits appropriately per specifications and scope.

  • Conducts and documents furniture inventories as required.

Project Closeout

  • Obtains work order sign-offs from clients.
  • Closes out all required change orders.
  • Conducts, documents, and tracks final punch list items through completion.

None

title: Senior Demand Planner
description:
Family owned and operated, Bake’n Joy Foods, Inc. is a leading manufacturer of top-quality bakery products that began over eighty years ago in 1941. We manufacture a variety of products for professional bakers including frozen scoop batters, predeposited muffin, cornbread, loaf cakes and Boston Coffee Cakes, mixes as well as an expanding line of fully baked items such as coffee cakes, loaf cakes and more. We remain committed to providing top quality products, service, and value to our customers.


**********STAFFING AGENCIES AND RECRUITING FIRMS - PLEASE DO NOT CONTACT BAKE'N JOY FOR THIS ROLE**********


Senior Demand Planner

Classification

  • Exempt

Reports To

  • Director of Supply Chain

JD Review Date

  • September 2026

Job Summary/Objective

The Senior Demand Planner is responsible for owning and executing the demand planning process across all food categories and sales channels to ensure product availability while minimizing waste and inventory costs. This role partners closely with Sales, Marketing, Finance, Production, and Customer Service teams to deliver accurate forecasts that support production scheduling, procurement, and distribution.

The Senior Demand Planner will play a key role in establishing forecast governance, improving cross-functional alignment, supporting SKU portfolio optimization, and helping build a single trusted demand plan across the organization. This role will also support the implementation and adoption of demand planning technologies and processes that improve visibility, scalability, and decision-making.

In addition to managing the day-to-day forecasting process, this role will play a critical part in evolving and maturing demand planning capabilities, transitioning from largely manual processes toward more automated, system-driven planning. The Senior Demand Planner will help build trust in data, improve forecast accuracy, and enable more effective use of ERP/MRP systems to support scalable growth.

This role operates within a well-established organization with deep institutional knowledge and long-tenured teams. Success will require a thoughtful, respectful approach to change, balancing process improvement with an appreciation for existing expertise. The Senior Demand Planner will build strong relationships, listen actively and partner cross-functionally to drive an evolution of capabilities grounded in trust, collaboration, and shared ownership.

The ideal candidate is a collaborative, hands-on professional with experience in food manufacturing operations, a curious and independent learning style, comfort navigating ambiguity, and the ability to lead through change, influence stakeholders, and continuously improve processes and systems.

Essential Functions

  • Develop and maintain short- and long-term demand forecasts for food products, incorporating shipment history and relevant demand drivers such as market trends, seasonality, promotions, new product launches and downstream consumption data.
  • Partner closely with Sales and customer-facing teams to understand demand drivers, challenge forecast assumptions, improve forecast accountability, and develop a collaborative planning process.
  • Support the development of demand planning governance, standard planning cadences, and cross-functional alignment while helping the organization progress toward a more formal S&OP and integrated business planning process. Act as a change leader, building trust and driving adoption of improved planning practices across the organization.
  • Proactively identify forecast risks, demand exceptions, and emerging business trends, facilitating timely cross-functional action and decision-making.
  • Monitor forecast accuracy (e.g., MAPE, bias), analyze root causes of variance, and incorporate evolving demand signals, including shipment trends, customer inventory dynamics (e.g., forward buys), and POS data where available, to continuously refine forecast assumptions.
  • Support SKU portfolio optimization and rationalization initiatives through analysis of demand trends, inventory performance, customer adoption, lifecycle status, and business value.
  • Contribute to the reduction of finished goods inventory carrying costs by enhancing forecast accuracy, increasing visibility to inventory health (e.g., aging, excess, obsolescence), and partnering cross-functionally to help right-size inventory while maintaining service and freshness standards.
  • Partner with production and procurement to align on forecasted needs and ensure timely material availability.
  • Support the implementation and adoption of demand planning technologies, systems and processes that improve forecast visibility, data integrity, collaboration, and scalable planning workflows.
  • Lead or support new product introduction (NPI) forecasting and lifecycle management.
  • Develop and present demand planning reports and KPIs to senior leadership, including forecast accuracy, demand variability, and insights on inventory health trends and carrying cost drivers.

Competencies

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate data into actionable business decisions.
  • Effective communication and influencing skills, with a demonstrated ability to build credibility and trust across cross-functional and tenured teams.
  • Experience managing demand forecasts across a large SKU portfolio with seasonality and shelf-life considerations.
  • Understanding of relationship between shipment and downstream demand signals (e.g., POS), and the ability to incorporate these insights as data availability evolves.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence inventory outcomes, including reducing excess and carrying costs through improved forecasting, data-driven insights, and cross-functional alignment.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead change in established organizations, operate effectively in evolving environments, establish structure where processes are still developing, and influence stakeholders without direct authority.
  • Experience transforming manual forecasting processes into scalable, system-enabled workflows, with strong ERP/MRP proficiency (e.g., JD Edwards or similar).
  • Deep knowledge of food industry supply chain requirements, including food safety, freshness, and traceability.


Required Education & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Business, Food Science, or a related field.
  • 5-8+ years of experience in demand planning or forecasting, preferably within the food or CPG industry.
  • Experience using demand planning software and ERP systems, with participation in system implementations, process transformations, or planning technology deployments strongly preferred.
  • Strong understanding of the food supply chain dynamics, including shelf life, cold chain logistics, and seasonality.
  • Proven track record of improving forecast accuracy and driving cross-functional collaboration.


Preferred Education & Experience

  • APICS certification (CPIM, CSCP) is preferred.
  • Advanced Excel and forecasting tool experience.
  • Familiarity with data visualization tools (e.g., Power BI, Tableau).
  • Experience working in a fast-paced, perishable goods environment.
  • Knowledge of food regulatory compliance (e.g., FDA, USDA) is a plus.


Key Performance Indicators (KPIs):

  • Forecast Accuracy (MAPE, Bias)
  • Inventory Turns and Waste Reduction
  • Service Level / Fill Rate
  • On-Time Production Planning Alignment
  • Stockouts vs. Overstocks
  • Days of Inventory (especially for perishable SKUs)


Work Environment

  • Primarily a manufacturing plant environment with exposure to noise, temperature variations, and machinery
  • Use of personal protective equipment as required


Physical Demands

  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs.
  • Prolonged standing and walking on concrete floors
  • Use of personal protective equipment


Position Type

  • Full-Time

Work Hours

  • Typical work hours: Monday to Thursday: 8:00AM - 5:00PM, Friday 8:00AM - 3:00PM

Travel

  • Some travel required between sites or to customer locations

Compensation

The typical starting salary range for this position is $93,100 - $123,300 a year. Several factors, including skills, experience, education, certifications, and the location of the job will determine the actual pay offered. The salary range for this role reflects the competitive labor market value for associates in these positions.

This position may also be eligible to receive a variable annual bonus based on company, team, and/or individual performance results in accordance with company policy. Bake’n Joy offers its full-time associates a comprehensive Total Rewards package, which includes affordable, quality healthcare for our associates and their families, life insurance and disability benefits to provide security, and retirement benefits to help plan for the financial future.

Bake’n Joy is committed to fostering an environment where associates from all backgrounds can build long and meaningful careers. Through strong relationships, comprehensive benefits, and continuous learning opportunities, we seek to create an environment where associates can succeed, both professionally and personally.


Equal Employment Opportunity Policy

Bake’n Joy provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training.

title: RCM Specialist
description:
About Company:

Join Druid City Infusion — part of the Vital Care Infusion Services network!


We’re a rapidly growing home and alternate-site infusion therapy provider delivering compassionate, high-quality care for acute and chronic conditions right in patients’ homes or local clinics.


We support infusion therapy programs across multiple states, including Colorado, Georgia, Alabama, Arkansas, Mississippi, New Mexico, South Carolina, Louisiana, Tennessee and beyond through the broader Vital Care network.

At Druid City Infusion, you’ll help bring advanced therapies like IVIG, neurology, rheumatology, pulmonary care, and more to patients in communities that need them — with strong clinical support and opportunities for professional growth.


Make an impact where it matters most — grow your career with a team delivering care across the nation!


About the Role:

The RIT Billing/Collections Specialist plays a critical role in managing the financial operations related to patient billing and collections within a healthcare setting. This position is responsible for ensuring accurate and timely billing processes, resolving billing discrepancies, and facilitating effective communication between patients, insurance companies, and healthcare providers. The specialist will work diligently to optimize revenue cycle management by monitoring accounts receivable and implementing collection strategies that comply with healthcare regulations. By maintaining detailed records and providing exceptional customer service, the role supports the financial health of the organization while fostering positive patient experiences. Ultimately, this position contributes to the seamless financial workflow that enables the delivery of quality healthcare services.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • High school diploma or equivalent; associate degree or higher preferred.
  • Minimum of 2 years experience in medical billing, collections, or related healthcare financial services.
  • Familiarity with medical billing software and electronic health record (EHR) systems.
  • Strong understanding of insurance claim processes, billing codes, and healthcare regulations.
  • Excellent communication and organizational skills.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Certification in medical billing or coding (e.g., CPC, CCA) is highly desirable.
  • Experience working within a hospital or clinical environment.
  • Knowledge of HIPAA compliance and patient privacy regulations.
  • Proficiency with advanced billing software and data analysis tools.
  • Demonstrated ability to handle complex billing issues and negotiate payment arrangements.

Responsibilities:

  • Prepare and submit accurate patient bills and insurance claims in accordance with healthcare policies and regulations.
  • Review and reconcile billing statements to identify and resolve discrepancies or errors promptly.
  • Communicate with patients, insurance providers, and internal departments to address billing inquiries and facilitate payment collections.
  • Monitor accounts receivable and implement follow-up procedures to ensure timely payment and reduce outstanding balances.
  • Maintain detailed documentation of billing activities, payment plans, and collection efforts to support audit and compliance requirements.

Skills:

The required skills enable the specialist to accurately process and manage billing information, ensuring compliance with healthcare standards and timely revenue collection. Strong communication skills are essential for effectively interacting with patients and insurance representatives to resolve billing questions and disputes. Organizational skills support the management of multiple accounts and documentation, facilitating efficient workflow and audit readiness. Preferred skills such as certification and advanced software proficiency enhance the specialist’s ability to navigate complex billing scenarios and optimize financial outcomes. Together, these skills ensure the specialist can maintain accuracy, compliance, and professionalism in a fast-paced healthcare financial environment.


Commitment to Diversity and Inclusivity

At Druid City Vital Care, we believe that diversity and inclusivity are essential to delivering exceptional care and fostering innovation. We are committed to creating a workplace where every individual is respected, valued, and empowered—regardless of race, ethnicity, gender identity, age, ability, or background.

Our Approach Includes

  • Inclusive Hiring Practices: Ensuring equal opportunities for all candidates.
  • Ongoing Education: Providing training to promote cultural competence and eliminate bias.
  • Collaborative Environment: Encouraging diverse perspectives to strengthen patient care and organizational success.

By embracing diversity and inclusion, we aim to reflect the communities we serve and build a culture of belonging for our employees and patients alike.

title: AVP of Business Loan Operations
description:
Thank you for taking the time to review our AVP of Business Loan Operations position. At Leaders Credit Union, our mission is to “Power your passion and make lives better.” We are very intentional about the hiring and interview process, which means we take our time. We want to make sure that you find the perfect career path! We truly appreciate your interest in Leaders Credit Union.

Who is Leaders Credit Union? We are a member-owned financial cooperative. This means that we exist to serve the needs of the consumers who own accounts at Leaders Credit Union. They are owners, and their financial well-being is at the heart of every decision we make. We are one of the largest credit unions in West Tennessee, and one of the most stable. Our purpose is simple: to provide a sound, convenient alternative to traditional banking.

What are our core values? As a team member of Leaders Credit Union, you would be asked to adhere to a specific set of core values. These values should govern all decisions that are made when serving our members’ needs. These values are:

  • Member Focused
  • Team Oriented
  • Community Minded
  • Forward Thinking
  • Trusted Partner

Why Leaders? Leaders Credit Union has been ranked one of the Best Credit Unions to Work for three years in a row. So, what makes Leaders such a great place to work?

  • Great benefits! We offer healthcare, vacation time, sick time, 401k options, and a profit-sharing plan (just to name a few!) Our Human Resources team is always looking to ensure that our benefit packages are competitive.
  • Work with a mission! Our mission statement isn’t just something written on a billboard, we truly look to “power your passion and make lives better.” That mission is lived out by member-facing personnel as well as our back-office employees.
  • Extensive training! We go to great lengths to make sure you know your job responsibilities and are comfortable through a very thorough training process. But our training goes beyond that. We offer monthly classes on everything from mortgage products to conflict resolution. We give you the tools you need to succeed.
  • Room for growth! At Leaders, you are only limited by your own ambition. Being part of a quickly growing financial institution leaves room for personal growth, and we do our best to promote from within whenever possible.


What does a day as an AVP of Business Loan Operations look like?

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Oversee day-to-day Business Lending Operations, including loan processing, closing, booking, servicing, and portfolio support.
  • Build and improve workflows, procedures, controls, and performance metrics to keep operations running smoothly.
  • Manage loan pipelines and turnaround times to ensure loans are processed accurately and on schedule.
  • Oversee the review, closing, funding, and boarding of commercial, real estate, construction, SBA, and participation loans.
  • Ensure loan documentation, collateral, insurance, approvals, and post-closing requirements are completed accurately and on time.
  • Maintain compliance with regulatory requirements and internal policies while identifying and addressing operational risks.
  • Partner with lending, credit, compliance, accounting, and member service teams to improve processes, reporting, systems, and the overall member experience.



What is the schedule? Our hours for this position are 8:00 am to 5:00pm Monday through Friday. Sometimes giving top-notch member service may require a little overtime, but we value work-life-balance and do our best to limit this.


Does your skill set and experience line up? For this role, we are looking for someone who:

  • Has at least 2 years of supervisory experience in a financial services position
  • Has a college degree
  • Must have strong attention to detail, strong math and organizational skills, and the ability to multitask.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Suite of Products (Excel, Outlook, Word, etc.)
  • Must maintain a professional, courteous, and friendly atmosphere for members and co-workers
  • Must have very strong communication skills (both written and verbal)


What is next? If you think this role is the perfect fit for you, please apply, and upload your resume online. Once you have applied you will receive an email from our system saying your application has been received. Keep an eye on your email over the next few weeks as this is our main form of communication. If the next step for you is an interview, we will reach out via email. If this position isn’t the right fit at this time, we will keep your resume on file in case anything else comes available that you might be a great fit for.


Thank you for choosing Leaders!

title: Program Manager
description:

At Honeywell Aerospace (NASDAQ: HONA), we're launching as an independent, publicly traded aerospace and defense company built on a legacy of operational excellence and mission-focused execution.

Our new brand identity pairs that heritage with real momentum, as we build technology that helps pilots navigate with confidence, aircraft operate more efficiently, and operators stay ahead of change. With our systems on board 90% of the world's aircraft, your work here has reach that's rare to find anywhere else.

Focusing on our customers, investing in innovation, and building a culture of accountability and performance is how we're shaping what comes next.

Every horizon. Every mission. Every day.

WE VALUE

  • Ability to work collaboratively in cross-functional teams
  • Attention to detail and ability to prioritize tasks effectively
  • Adaptability and flexibility to manage changing project requirements
  • Passion for innovation and continuous learning

Due to compliance with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidate must be a U.S. Person, which is defined as, a U.S. citizen, a U.S. permanent resident, or have protected status in the U.S. under asylum or refugee status or have the ability to obtain an export authorization.

title: Head Varsity Lacrosse Coach
description:
Marlborough School

Head Varsity Lacrosse Coach

Part-Time, Seasonal

Non-Exempt

Founded in 1889, Marlborough School is an independent girls college-preparatory school for grades 7 through 12 located in Los Angeles, California. Marlborough is the oldest independent girls’ school in the Southern California region. Central to Marlborough’s vision that Equity Leads Education is the belief in and passion for empowering young women to use their immense talents to better the world and become trailblazers in their own right. Bolstered by world-class faculty and staff, Marlborough students are challenged and inspired to work towards their own personal best and, in doing so, have an almost endless array of courses, extracurriculars, electives, and programs to spark their curiosity, deepen their compassion for one another, and lead lives of purpose.

OPPORTUNITY STATEMENT

Marlborough School seeks a dynamic and dedicated individual to fill the role of Head Lacrosse Coach. Reporting to the Director of Athletics, the Head Lacrosse Coach will play a vital role in shaping the future of our student-athletes. This opportunity is perfect for someone who is innovative, engaged, highly organized, and passionate about nurturing the talents of young athletes.

KEY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Starting at the beginning of the School Year, the Head Coach is responsible for strategically planning the Lacrosse Season. To ensure the program remains at the forefront, they commit to staying updated on the latest ideas, techniques, and rules by attending various clinics and workshops. Furthermore, the coach remains actively involved in professional organizations within the sport and participates in key school activities by attending school admissions events.


Pre-Season (Winter):

  • Coordinates with athletic trainers to ensure athletes are cleared for participation.

  • Organize pre-season parent and staff meetings, clarifying rules and expectations.

  • Distribute practice schedules and required training proof.

  • Facilitate a pre season practice plan to develop all levels.

  • Work with coaching staff to create program standards and expectations

  • Work with AD to create an appropriate game schedule


In Season (Spring):

  • Supervise all phases of teams, emphasizing safety and ethical conduct.

  • Organize regular practice sessions to develop athletes' potential.

  • Ensure facility regulations are understood and enforced.

  • Report contest outcomes to the media and Athletic Director.

  • Instruct players on rules, techniques, and safety procedures.

  • Adhere to Marlborough School's rules and regulations.


PostSeason (Spring):

  • Arrange systematic return, cleaning, storing, and inventory of all equipment/uniforms.

  • Recommend student athletes for awards and evaluate past seasons.

  • Recommend improvements for facilities and personnel.

title: Direct Service Advocate_HYPP_2nd Shift_FT
description:
Department: Holyoke Young Parent Program


Reports to: Program Director


Schedule: Full-time, 75 hours/bi-weekly; 3pm-11pm


FLSA Status: Non-Exempt


Starting Rate: $21


The YWCA of Western MA is dedicated to eliminating racism and empowering survivors. We provide a safe place for survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, and human trafficking. Our programs and services include crisis shelter and transitional housing for survivors and their families, counseling, SAFEPLAN court advocacy, community education, supervised visitation, and violence prevention education. The YWCA provides services at several sites, including Holyoke, Northampton, Westfield, and our primary Springfield campus.

Expectations of all employees

In the performance of essential and general job responsibilities, all YWCA employees are expected to:

  • Demonstrate commitment to the YWCA’s mission and principles of trauma-informed work.
  • Represent the YWCA in a professional and competent manner to participants, community members, organizational partners, and other stakeholders.
  • Support policies, practices, and decisions that demonstrate our shared accountability for racial equity.
  • Foster a positive working environment.
  • Coordinate efforts across teams, programs, and partner organizations.
  • Maintain professional behavior and strict confidentiality.


Position Purpose

The Direct Service Advocate (DSA) is responsible for providing support, advocacy and role modeling to adult, teen and child program participants living in the YWCA’s residential programs. DSA’s are part of a team model working with peers, supervisors, clinicians and outside connections to best serve program participants. DSA’s support the agency mission and trauma informed service model in order to provide safe, consistent and quality services to vulnerable populations.


Essential Responsibilities

  • Nurture and support a milieu approach that is participant-guided, family-driven, strengths-based, and trauma-informed; and embraces a framework of empowerment and encouragement, engaging with 100% of individuals and families that are on-site each shift;
  • Encourage and support the development of life skills, positive parenting and improved parent-child interaction- 1:1 or group format to include recreational, educational, and cultural or those that promote family engagement;
  • Follow and encourage the programs daily schedule and facilitate resident participation and community responsibilities, taking into account individualized plans for each participant;
  • Ongoing individual resident support with 85% of time on shift in direct service role providing face to face contact and interaction with participant’s and their children in order to support;
  • Ensure program procedures, rules, regulations and policies are followed to ensure a safe and supportive living environment including completion of 100% of all required safety sweeps (minimum of four times) each shift to ensure premises including alarms, doors, windows, appliances and bedrooms are all safe;
  • To facilitate integration into the program, provide orientation and emotional support to participants upon arrival;
  • To ensure participants are properly welcomed to the program, prepares rooms for new families within 1-2 shifts from previous exit;
  • Provide daily information as it relates to data collection and outcome measurements through the completion of 100% of AWARDS logs prior to end of shift;
  • Required documentation and daily program communication including case notes, resident files and communication logs, completing 100% of all documentation prior to the end of shift;
  • Perform regular job duties to be observed by new staff during the job shadowing portion of program orientation;
  • Engage with residents at 100% of all meal times and ensure that participants clean up the dining area prior to leaving as well as kitchen prior to cooking;
  • Ensure thorough communication of staff from shift to shift;
  • Assist with child care as needed to support service planning goal activities completion;
  • To support children’s safety and well-being, ensure mothers supervise children at all times and offer support to moms during a crisis or periods where they may be overwhelmed;
  • Conducts safety checks on residents and children as needed and completes 100% of all required safety checks;
  • Answer phones and provide information and referral;
  • Attend scheduled staff meetings, supervision and trainings as required;
  • Responsible for the upkeep of the facility and property, completing tasks that include, but are not limited to, vacuuming, laundry, assisting with loading/unloading groceries, mopping, preparation of bedrooms, ensuring 100% of chores are completed properly before signing off on the chore list during your shift;
  • Provide transportation to residents and adhere to all safety laws/policies regarding seat belts, car seat requirements and speed limits at all times to include ratio of 1:6; and
  • Perform other related duties as needed.


Qualifications

  • A.A. or equivalent education or experience in a human service field, preferred;
  • At least one year of counseling and direct service experience;
  • Experience in a domestic violence setting;
  • Experience with survivors of gender-based violence and exploitation;
  • Experience addressing the impacts of decisions and actions on multiple communities;
  • Reliable transportation, safe driving record, and valid driver’s license required. Must be able to be covered by the agency's insurance policy.
  • Must be able to lift 40 lbs.

title: Retail Planner/Analyst
description:
POSITION SUMMARY

As a Retail Planner/Analyst, you will sit at the center of analytics, product, and planning for the division—turning data into insights that help drive smarter decisions across sales, merchandising, demand planning, replenishment, and supply chain. This role is ideal for someone who is passionate about data and product; someone who can “read the tea leaves” in POS and category data to anticipate customer needs, identify emerging opportunities, and support strategic assortment decisions. As the peer connector to Sales, Replenishment Planning, and Customer Service, this role ensures demand signals, sales forecasts, category insights, and assortment plans accurately inform replenishment strategy, inventory planning, and both commercial and wholesale supply chain planning.

The ideal candidate is curious, commercially minded, highly analytical, and energized by uncovering opportunities, influencing product decisions, and helping the business stay one step ahead of the customer.

This position is located in our Frisco office.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

1. Sales Analytics and Category Management:

  • Serve as the analytics hub for sales, category, item, and channel performance across the omni-channel business.
  • Translate POS, margin, sell-through, distribution, availability, and productivity trends into clear, actionable insights that help drive business decisions.
  • Support strategic assortment decisions by identifying category shifts, whitespace opportunities, item productivity, customer demand, and channel-specific performance trends.
  • Answer the “why behind the what” in the data to anticipate customer needs, spot emerging product opportunities, and clarify what is working, what is not working, and where demand is moving next.
  • Communicate risks, opportunities, and recommended actions with clarity and urgency to leadership, sales, customer service, design, and customer-facing partners.

2. Demand Planning:

  • Build and maintain sales reports, dashboards, forecasts, ladder plans, and assortment planning tools that keep the division aligned and informed.
  • Translate sales history, store selling, seasonality, customer plans, and category performance into demand forecasts that tell a clear commercial story.
  • Partner with Sales, Merchandising, Account Management, Merchant teams, and Replenishment Planning to ensure forecasts reflect business strategies, customer expectations, and emerging marketplace signals.
  • Serve as the demand-planning peer to Replenishment Planning, ensuring the demand signal accurately supports replenishment strategy, inventory planning, and supply chain decisions.
  • Connect commercial and wholesale planning by ensuring forecasts, assortment plans, and demand assumptions are communicated clearly across planning and supply chain partners.


QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Fashion Merchandising, Retail Management, Finance, Analytics, or a related field.
  • 5+ years of retail, wholesale, or apparel industry experience, preferably in sales analytics, category analytics, assortment planning, demand forecasting, or retail planning.
  • Strong analytical curiosity with the ability to turn sales, category, channel, and demand data into clear insights, recommendations, and business narratives.
  • Advanced Excel skills and proficiency with reporting, ERP, retail analytics, and Microsoft Office tools; experience with project management systems is a plus.
  • Collaborative communicator who can partner effectively with Sales, Merchandising, Account Management, Replenishment Planning, and supply chain teams.
  • Detail-oriented, organized, and energized by using data and product insights to anticipate customer needs and drive action in a fast-paced environment.

title: Volunteer Museum Docent
description:
Job Title: Fire Department Museum Docent

Location: Windsor-Severance Fire Museum, 121 N 6th St, Windsor, CO

Position Type: Volunteer

Schedule: A minimum of one Saturday per month from 12:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. and additional availability for fire museum events

POSITION DESCRIPTION:

Join us as a Volunteer Museum Docent and help us inspire future generations while honoring the legacy of firefighters in the towns of Windsor and Severance. The Volunteer Fire Museum Docent position offers a rewarding opportunity to engage with the rich heritage of Windsor-Severance Fire Rescue (WSFR) dating back to 1902. As a volunteer docent, you will play a vital role in preserving and sharing the history of fire departments and fire safety with the community.

ABOUT THE MUSEUM:

Established in 2010, the Windsor Severance Fire Museum celebrates the heritage of Windsor-Severance Fire Rescue (WSFR) dating back to 1902. Located at 121 N 6th Street in Windsor, CO, it's open every Saturday from 12 to 4 p.m.

The museum showcases three original antique fire trucks used by the Windsor Fire Department, offering visitors a glimpse into firefighting history and the evolution of technology. With artifacts, photographs, and equipment on display, the museum honors the dedication and innovation of the firefighting profession and pays tribute to its courageous service to the community.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES:

  • Guided Tours: Conduct guided tours of the fire museum for community members, school field trips, and various community groups interested in learning about fire department history and fire safety.
  • Event Participation: Provide information, interact with attendees, and represent the museum at community events, including the Harvest Festival Parade, the parade during Severance Days, WSFR Annual Open House, library events, and other town and local events.
  • Customer Service: Interact with visitors of all ages, providing exceptional customer service and answering questions about the exhibits and artifacts.
  • Cleaning and Maintenance: Maintain the cleanliness of the museum by dusting, sweeping, cleaning glass surfaces, and general tidying to ensure a welcoming environment for visitors.
  • Sales: Sell museum merchandise, including t-shirts and other items. Experience with cash handling is a plus.
  • Educational Outreach: Utilize teaching skills to deliver educational programs and presentations on fire safety and the history of fire departments.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:

  • Ability to treat coworkers and community members with dignity and respect regardless of their race, religion, gender, age, socioeconomic status, etc.
  • Ability to make ethical decisions, display ethical conduct and be a representative of the district to the community.
  • Ability to teach different age groups one-on-one and in groups.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to interact effectively with diverse groups of people.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Attention to detail and willingness to perform cleaning and maintenance tasks.
  • Passion for preserving and sharing the history of fire departments and fire safety.
  • Ability to read, write, and speak in the English language.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Must be 18 years old
  • Possess a Valid Colorado Driver’s license
  • Ability to pass WSFR background check
  • Ability to work in the US

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Customer service, teaching, or public speaking experience
  • Cash handling experience
  • Experience driving a straight-drive manual engine with a double clutch. We need volunteers who can learn how to safely drive our three antique fire engines to community events and parades. We also offer fire engine rides during museum hours.

TRAINING AND CERTIFICATIONS:

  • Possess and maintain an American Heart Association BLS CPR Provider certification (WSFR will provide)
  • Attend WSFR annual diversity and harassment training.
  • Attend WSFR annual bloodborne pathogen training.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by a volunteer to successfully perform the essential functions of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

While performing the duties of this position, the volunteer is frequently required to:

  • Reaching: Extending hand(s) and arm(s) in any direction.
  • Standing: Remaining upright on the feet, particularly for sustained periods of time.
  • Lifting: Raising objects from a lower to a higher position or moving objects horizontally from position to position.
  • Grasping: Applying pressure to an object with the fingers and palm.
  • Talking: Expressing or exchanging ideas using the spoken word; those activities where detailed or important spoken instructions must be conveyed to other workers accurately, loudly, or quickly.
  • Hearing: The ability to perceive the nature of sounds at normal speaking levels with or without correction, to receive detailed information through oral communication, and to make fine discriminations in sound.

Type of work:

  • Light work: Exerting up to 20 pounds occasionally and/or 10 pounds of force frequently. Ability to stand and walk on concrete during the majority of the volunteer shift.

Visual acuity:

  • The worker is required to have visual acuity to determine the accuracy, neatness, and thoroughness of the work assigned
  • The worker may be required to have visual acuity to operate motor vehicles or heavy equipment.

WORK ENVIRONMENT:

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

  • While performing the duties of this job, the worker is subject to inside environmental conditions: Protection from weather conditions but not necessarily from temperature changes.
  • The worker occasionally works in outside weather conditions, including temperature extremes.
  • The worker occasionally works near moving mechanical parts and is occasionally exposed to wet or humid conditions, fumes or airborne particles, moving vehicles, and vibration.

BENEFITS:

  • Opportunity to contribute to the preservation of local history and community education.
  • Gain experience in customer service, teaching, and public speaking.
  • Build connections within the community and with fellow volunteers.
  • Satisfaction with making a meaningful impact by educating others about fire safety.
  • This is an unpaid volunteer role.
