title: Optometric Technician
description:
PRIMARY FUNCTIONS: The Optometric Technician functions as a member of the vision care team by performing and documenting results of selected tests and measurements, maintaining adequately supplied workstations, maintaining a clean work environment, and promoting timely and efficient patient flow through the clinic. Has primary responsibility for the collection, processing, and recording of data from vision and eye testing, including eyeglasses prescriptions and frames. Assists with patient treatments during clinical sessions.

Demonstrates a sincere dedication and loyalty to the philosophy and mission of Neighborhood Health.

DUTIES/ RESPONSIBILITIES: (Essential Functions: Duties and responsibilities noted with bullets are considered to be the essential functions of the job)Performs measurements of auto-refraction, auto-keratometry, lensometry, pupillary distance, visual acuity, color vision testing, stereopsis testing, eyeglasses measurements.

· Records physical measurements referring to past visit measurements as appropriate. Notifies optometrist of any significant changes or abnormalities in these measurements.

· Obtains health history information and completes medication reconciliation.

· Performs other diagnostic testing as directed such as anterior segment imaging, retina imaging, optical coherence tomography, visual field testing.

· Records results of all eye and vision tests and notifies optometrist of any abnormal values.

· Processes and packages lab samples for analysis by off-site lab services.

· Assists clients in applying for eyeglasses via charity sources, and in selecting frames that are appropriate for them and in the preferred style and color.

· Submits eyeglasses orders to charity sources and/or vision insurance-affiliated labs, tracks arrivals, notifies optometrist and clients of eyeglasses arrival, dispenses eyeglasses, reports patient concerns or non-adaptation to optometrist.

· Orders trial contact lenses, tracks arrivals, notifies optometrist and clients of contact lens trial arrivals.

· Assists in teaching proper contact lens hygiene, insertion and removal skills to clients.

· Assists in demonstrating proper eye patch use and/or eye drop or ointment instillation to patients and caretakers.

· Ensures patients are appropriately checked out, i.e. testing or labs performed, eye drops and other medications or materials given, home testing provided, and patient education given as directed by optometrist.

· Addresses telephone encounters in a timely manner.

OTHER DUTIES:

· Performs daily, weekly, and monthly equipment maintenance according to manufacturer’s instructions.

· Cleans all medical equipment and exam chairs according to OSHA standards.

· Maintains clean, well-stocked exam rooms.

· Assists in supply and clinic medication ordering.

· Prepare and maintain special internal and external reports as requested by Supervisor and/or Department Head.

· May be assigned to various project lead roles to advance the development of the department and support ad hoc needs.

· Able to work under minimal supervision.

· Employee will be asked to perform additional duties and take on other responsibilities as dictated by events and circumstances.

QUALIFICATION/EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS:

· High School Diploma or equivalent required.

· Some experience in optometry or medical office preferred.

· Certification preferred.

· Good oral and written communication skills in English and Spanish.

· Familiar with electronic medical records.

· Attention to detail and excellent technical skills.

· Good interpersonal skills.


Travel Requirements: Local travel to other community health clinics.

title: Employee Engagement & Learning Specialist
description:
Applicants must be authorized to work lawfully in the United States for NCCPA as NCCPA will not sponsor or take over sponsorship of employment visas.

As the Employee Engagement & Learning Specialist, you will be responsible for coordinating and enhancing the employee experience throughout the employment lifecycle, including onboarding, professional development, employee engagement, wellness, recognition, and internal communications.

Reports To: Senior Manager of Human Resources

Who We Are

National Commission on Certification of Physician Assistants (NCCPA) is the only certifying organization for physician assistants in the United States. Established as a not-for-profit organization in 1974, we are dedicated to assuring the public that board certified PAs meet established standards of clinical knowledge and cognitive skills upon entry into practice and throughout their careers. All U.S. states, the District of Columbia and the U.S. territories have decided to rely on NCCPA certification as one of the criteria for licensure or regulation of PAs.

Location: NCCPA is a hybrid work environment with our headquarters located in Johns Creek, Georgia. NCCPA has determined that the telecommuting status of this position is hybrid, which means that employees in hybrid positions are allowed to split their work hours between working remotely and working onsite at the NCCPA headquarters. The duties of this position require that the candidate report on-site to the Johns Creek headquarters, at minimum, on a weekly basis and live within the commutable distance. NCCPA has defined commutable distance as within the State of Georgia and within 85 miles of ground transportation, one-way between an employee’s primary residence and the NCCPA headquarters in Johns Creek, Georgia.

Why Work at NCCPA

We get to do meaningful work every day, and we enjoy working and having fun together! We’re proud to be recognized by the Atlanta Journal-Constitution as a Top Workplace in the metro Atlanta region.

How Will You Make a Difference? You will…

  • Design and coordinate a welcoming and effective onboarding experience, including new hire orientation, resources, agendas, and learning pathways.
  • Develop and support initiatives that strengthen employee engagement, connection, culture, and retention across NCCPA’s hybrid work environment.
  • Coordinate employee recognition, appreciation, wellness, and engagement programs, including service awards and other employee-focused initiatives.
  • Support the annual employee engagement survey, employee check-ins, and action planning based on employee feedback.
  • Coordinate and facilitate learning and professional development programs, including workshops, webinars, lunch and learns, and required organizational training.
  • Maintain training calendars, attendance, completion records, and other learning-related documentation.
  • Evaluate learning and engagement programs through surveys, assessments, feedback, and program metrics.
  • Partner with managers, subject matter experts, and committees to identify employee and organizational development needs.
  • Research training vendors and serve as a resource for employees and managers seeking professional development opportunities.
  • Develop and maintain employee-facing HR communications and content across the intranet, SharePoint, newsletters, announcements, and other communication channels.

Hard Skills You Will Have

  • Bachelor's degree in Human Resource Management, Organizational Development, or related field. Experience in lieu of education will be considered as well.
  • At least four years of progressive experience in employee development, engagement, training, people operations, human resources, or a related field.
  • Working knowledge of employment law and HR compliance fundamentals.
  • Experience facilitating and/or coordinating both in-person and virtual training and evaluating training options and alternatives.
  • Experience with HRIS and LMS systems such as ADP Workforce Now, Traliant, or similar platforms.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and related program software.

Soft Skills You Will Bring

  • Strong organizational and project management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and follow through on details.
  • Excellent written, verbal, presentation, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • A collaborative and approachable style that allows you to build positive relationships with employees, managers, leadership, and external partners.
  • A customer-service mindset and genuine interest in creating a positive employee experience.
  • Sound judgment and the ability to handle confidential and sensitive information with discretion.
  • Curiosity and creativity when identifying ways to improve employee learning, engagement, and connection.

Extra Skills You Can Bring Along

  • Master’s degree in Human Resource Management or a related field.
  • Experience supporting employee engagement initiatives, onboarding programs, or workplace operations.
  • Training or HR-related specialized credentials.
  • Knowledge of adult learning approaches, theories, and curriculum development.

We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression, or veteran status. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.

title: Revenue Consultant
description:
Role and Responsibilities

The Senior Consultant / Project Manager is responsible for leading client engagements focused on revenue accounting, Quorum systems, and operational process improvement for upstream oil & gas clients. This position combines project leadership, technical expertise, and consulting to help clients solve complex business challenges, optimize accounting processes, and successfully manage system implementations, upgrades, and ongoing support.

This role partners closely with client accounting teams, finance leadership, and software vendors to define project scope, implement solutions, manage change, and deliver successful outcomes. The ideal candidate is equally comfortable leading executive discussions, managing projects, and providing hands-on support during critical accounting and system initiatives.

JOB DUTIES

Client Consulting & Project Management

  • Lead consulting engagements from project scoping through implementation and client handoff.
  • Define project objectives, timelines, deliverables, budgets, risks, and communication plans.
  • Manage multiple client engagements while maintaining high-quality service and meeting project deadlines.
  • Build trusted relationships with client stakeholders ranging from accounting staff to Controllers and Finance executives.
  • Identify opportunities to improve client processes, controls, and system utilization.

Revenue Accounting Consulting

  • Serve as the subject matter expert for upstream revenue accounting processes, including:
    • Revenue distribution
    • Division Orders
    • Owner Relations
    • Revenue allocations
    • Prior period adjustments
    • Suspense accounting
    • Production and severance taxes
    • Month-end close
  • Assist clients in identifying accounting issues, process inefficiencies, and operational risks.
  • Provide hands-on support during critical accounting periods, including month-end close and special projects when needed.

Quorum Systems Support

  • Support implementation, configuration, optimization, and ongoing administration of Quorum Revenue Accounting (QRA), Enterprise Accounting (MQA), and related Quorum applications.
  • Plan and coordinate software upgrades, patches, and hot fixes while minimizing operational disruption.
  • Perform user acceptance testing (UAT), validation, and reconciliation activities to ensure system changes produce accurate accounting results.
  • Diagnose and resolve system configuration issues while recommending long-term process improvements.
  • Support data validation, workflow improvements, and system troubleshooting across multiple client environments.

Client & Vendor Collaboration

  • Serve as the primary liaison between clients and Quorum Software support and product teams.
  • Translate business requirements into system solutions while communicating technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders.
  • Guide clients through software changes, process updates, and organizational change management activities.
  • Maintain proactive communication regarding project status, risks, and recommendations.

Process Improvement & Leadership

  • Develop documentation, implementation methodologies, and consulting best practices.
  • Mentor junior consultants and provide guidance on accounting, systems, and project delivery.
  • Contribute to the continuous improvement of PetroLedger's consulting services and delivery model.

SKILLS

  • Strong knowledge of upstream oil & gas revenue accounting principles
  • Advanced knowledge of Quorum Revenue Accounting (QRA), MyQuorum Accounting, and related Quorum applications
  • Strong project management and organizational skills
  • Ability to manage multiple consulting engagements simultaneously
  • Excellent verbal, written, and presentation skills
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities
  • Experience facilitating software implementations, upgrades, and change management initiatives
  • Ability to build strong client relationships and communicate effectively with executive leadership
  • Self-motivated with the ability to work independently in ambiguous environments

QUALIFICATIONS AND EDUCATION

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, Information Systems, or related field required
  • Five or more years of experience in upstream oil & gas revenue accounting
  • Previous consulting or project management experience preferred
  • Demonstrated experience with Quorum Revenue Accounting (QRA) and MyQuorum Accounting
  • Experience supporting software implementations, upgrades, patches, and user acceptance testing
  • Experience working directly with upstream operators and/or consulting firms preferred
  • CPA or PMP certification is a plus
  • Experience with Power BI, SAP, or other ERP platforms is preferred

Additional Notes

This job description outlines the core responsibilities of the role but is not exhaustive. Additional goals may be assigned in alignment with PetroLedger’s values and evolving needs.

Why Join PetroLedger?

At PetroLedger, we’re more than an outsourced accounting and land services provider; we’re a collaborative partner to our clients and a growth-focused environment for our people.

What you can expect:

  • Meaningful work supporting complex oil & gas operations and client-owned assets
  • Collaborative, team-oriented culture with direct access to leadership
  • Career growth opportunities, including progression to Senior Lease & Title Analyst roles
  • Exposure to diverse clients and systems to expand your expertise
  • Flexible, hybrid work environment supporting work-life balance

Benefits

PetroLedger offers a competitive and comprehensive benefits package, including:

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Short-term and long-term disability coverage (STD & LTD)
  • Life insurance
  • Paid time off (PTO) and company holidays
  • Professional development and growth opportunities

title: Documentation Control Specialist
description:
Job Overview

As a Document Control Specialist, you will be responsible for managing and maintaining critical documentation in compliance with Rampart standard operating procedures, FDA regulations and ISO13485 quality standards. The Document Control Specialist is responsible for the administration of the electronic Quality Management System software. This position is a leader in document management systems, data entry, and administrative support to ensure accuracy, accessibility, and regulatory compliance across all organizational records. This position reports directly to the Director of Quality Assurance/Regulatory Affairs

Roles And Responsibilities

The Document Specialist plays a vital role in supporting quality management processes and maintaining the integrity of Rampart’s documentation infrastructure.

  • Provide administrative support related to document-related projects as needed
  • Manage and maintain electronic and paper-based documents using document management systems such as SharePoint and electronic Quality Management software.
  • Ensure all documentation complies with ISO 13485, and other relevant regulations and standards.
  • Perform data entry, filing, and records management to ensure accurate and accessible documentation.
  • Proofread and review documents for accuracy, consistency, and clarity before approval or distribution.
  • Support quality management initiatives by organizing and updating procedural documents, work instructions, and policies.
  • Assist with document control activities related to Quality Management systems and other technical platforms.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to ensure timely updates and proper version control of all documentation.

  • Participate in internal audits by providing necessary documentation and supporting records management processes.
  • Support technical writing tasks related to standard operating procedures (SOPs), work instructions, and other quality documents.
  • Assist in document control activities such as version control, document review cycles, and approval workflows
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to facilitate document updates and retrievals efficiently
  • Provide status reports on various documentation levels to management.
  • Review of DCO/ECO packages for adequacy and content
  • Complete assignments assigned by Supervisor.

Qualifications Required

A Bachelor or Associate degree in Science or General Studies is required with a minimum of 3 years relevant experience or 5+ years relevant work experience. Prior experience in a regulated industry such as medical devices or manufacturing is required

Must be able to occasionally travel to the manufacturing site for audit support.

Skills:

  • Candidate must be highly motivated with excellent communication skills and proven ability to work as part of a team.
  • Strong organizational skills with meticulous attention to detail.
  • Experience with document management systems such as SharePoint or similar platforms.
  • Knowledge of ISO 13485 and ISO 9001 standards related to quality management systems.
  • Proficiency in data management, data entry, and records management practices.
  • Excellent proofreading, editing, and technical writing skills.
  • Familiarity with ERP systems used for document control or quality assurance workflows.
  • Administrative experience supporting document control or quality assurance functions preferred.
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks efficiently while maintaining accuracy under tight deadlines.

title: Director, Brand Management
description:
Position Summary

Mad Engine Global is a leading designer, manufacturer, and distributor of licensed and branded apparel, accessories, and consumer products. The Director, Brand Go-To-Market is responsible for bringing newly signed and existing brand partnerships to market by serving as the central connector between brand partners, internal teams, and commercial stakeholders.

This role owns the end-to-end go-to-market process for assigned brands, ensuring that brand strategy is translated into commercially viable product direction, seasonal line plans, sales tools, approval workflows, launch calendars, and retailer-facing execution. The ideal candidate is highly organized, commercially minded, brand fluent, and capable of driving alignment across Sales, Design, Merchandising, Product Development, Licensing, Creative, Planning, Sourcing, E-commerce, and external brand partners.

This is not a traditional marketing-only role. It is a brand commercialization and cross-functional leadership role focused on ensuring that the brands Mad Engine signs are successfully launched, supported, sold, and scaled in the marketplace.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Brand Go-To-Market Leadership

  • Lead the go-to-market process for assigned brand partnerships from initial onboarding through seasonal launch and ongoing market execution.
  • Serve as the primary internal business lead for assigned brands, ensuring that all stakeholders understand the brand strategy, consumer target, market opportunity, product direction, and commercial priorities.
  • Translate brand partner objectives, guidelines, and positioning into actionable direction for internal teams.
  • Build and manage brand-specific go-to-market calendars, including line development milestones, approval deadlines, sales meeting dates, sample timing, retailer presentation windows, and launch requirements.
  • Lead all brand marketing – go to market social strategy, retail marketing, and influencer campaigns/photoshoot strategy and execution.
  • Ensure that all workstreams stay aligned to critical market dates and customer-facing milestones.

Brand Partner Management

  • Act as a key day-to-day contact for assigned brand partners, building strong relationships and maintaining clear communication around priorities, timelines, product direction, approvals, and business needs.
  • Partner with brand owners/licensors to understand brand strategy, seasonal priorities, consumer insights, creative direction, product guardrails, marketing expectations, and approval requirements.
  • Prepare and lead brand partner meetings, recaps, follow-ups, and internal action plans.
  • Proactively identify risks, misalignments, or delays and drive solutions before they impact market readiness.
  • Ensure Mad Engine shows up as an organized, strategic, and commercially capable partner.

Line Direction & Product Commercialization

  • Partner with Design, Merchandising, Product Development, Sales, and Planning to establish seasonal line direction for assigned brands.
  • Help define product opportunities by channel, account, consumer segment, price point, fabrication, category, and retail strategy.
  • Ensure product assortments reflect the brand’s DNA while also meeting retailer needs, margin targets, speed-to-market requirements, and commercial expectations.
  • Review line plans, product concepts, graphics, samples, and presentation materials to ensure alignment with brand strategy and market opportunity.
  • Partner with Sales to incorporate customer feedback and marketplace insights into seasonal product direction.
  • Help identify whitespace opportunities, product extensions, category expansion, and account-specific growth strategies.

Licensing, Brand Approvals & Compliance

  • Manage the approval process for assigned brands in partnership with Licensing, Design, Product Development, and external brand teams.
  • Ensure all submissions are accurate, timely, complete, and aligned with brand guidelines.
  • Track approval status, revisions, outstanding issues, and deadlines to maintain speed and accountability.
  • Resolve approval-related challenges by facilitating clear communication between internal teams and brand partners.
  • Maintain knowledge of brand standards, usage guidelines, rights, restrictions, product categories, territories, and customer-specific requirements.

Sales Calendar & Market Readiness

  • Own the brand-specific sales calendar and ensure internal teams are prepared for key customer meetings, line reviews, trade shows, and market appointments.
  • Partner with Sales to develop retailer-facing brand narratives, product stories, assortment strategies, pitch materials, and selling tools.
  • Coordinate the creation of seasonal decks, line sheets, sample assortments, product information, brand overviews, and other sales support materials.
  • Ensure Sales has the information, assets, samples, approvals, and product context needed to effectively sell the brand.
  • Support major customer presentations and meetings as needed.

Cross-Functional Project Management

  • Lead recurring cross-functional meetings for assigned brands, ensuring clear ownership, accountability, timing, and follow-through.
  • Coordinate activity across Sales, Design, Merchandising, Product Development, Licensing, Creative, Sourcing, Planning, Operations, E-commerce, and Executive Leadership.
  • Maintain organized tracking tools for key milestones, deliverables, approvals, risks, and decisions.
  • Create visibility for leadership into brand status, launch readiness, opportunities, challenges, and resource needs.
  • Drive internal alignment and decision-making when priorities, timelines, or commercial objectives shift.

Brand Strategy & Business Growth

  • Support the development of brand strategies that connect partner objectives with Mad Engine’s commercial capabilities.
  • Monitor market trends, consumer behavior, competitor activity, retail needs, and account feedback to inform brand growth plans.
  • Identify opportunities to expand distribution, categories, channels, and consumer relevance for assigned brands.
  • Partner with leadership and Sales to evaluate business performance and recommend actions to improve sell-in, sell-through, and long-term brand value.
  • Help build scalable processes for onboarding, launching, and managing brand partnerships across the organization.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Marketing, Merchandising, Fashion, Communications, or a related field.
  • 6–10 years of experience in brand management, licensing, merchandising, go-to-market, product marketing, wholesale sales support, or related consumer products roles.
  • Experience working with licensed brands, consumer products, apparel, accessories, retail, wholesale, or brand partnerships.
  • Strong understanding of the product development and commercialization process, including line planning, approvals, sales tools, samples, and market calendars.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple brands, projects, timelines, and stakeholders in a fast-paced environment.
  • Excellent communication, presentation, relationship management, and follow-up skills.
  • Strong commercial instincts and ability to balance brand integrity with retailer and business needs.
  • Highly organized, detail-oriented, and comfortable driving accountability across teams.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office, especially PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working directly with licensors, brand owners, entertainment, sports, lifestyle, fashion, or character brands.
  • Experience supporting major retail accounts and wholesale selling processes.
  • Knowledge of licensing approval systems, brand guideline management, and seasonal submission processes.
  • Experience in apparel graphics, product merchandising, or consumer product line development.
  • Ability to build executive-level presentations and retailer-facing brand decks.
  • Familiarity with digital asset management, PLM systems, or project management tools.

title: Adjunct- Medical Physiology Instructor
description:
Physician Associate Program

College of Health Sciences

Alvernia University


Alvernia University invites applications for an Adjunct Faculty position to teach Medical Physiology within the Master of Medical Science Physician Associate (PA) Program in the College of Health Sciences.

The successful candidate will provide high-quality instruction in graduate-level medical physiology, emphasizing the integration of physiological principles with clinical application to support physician associate student development. The course content will focus on the normal function of human body systems and the application of physiological concepts to understanding disease processes, clinical assessment, and patient care. The instructor will foster an engaging, collaborative, and student-centered learning environment that supports student success within the PA curriculum.

Essential Responsibilities

· Teach Medical Physiology within the Physician Associate Program in accordance with approved curriculum objectives and course learning outcomes.

· Deliver graduate-level instruction through evidence-based teaching strategies, including lectures, case-based learning, active learning activities, and other instructional methodologies.

· Integrate foundational physiology concepts with clinical applications relevant to physician associate practice.

· Develop, administer, and evaluate assessments that measure student achievement of course objectives and learning outcomes.

· Provide timely feedback and academic support to students.

· Maintain accurate course records, including attendance and grades, in accordance with University policies.

· Collaborate with PA Program faculty to ensure curricular integration, appropriate sequencing of content, and continuous quality improvement.

· Participate in course evaluation and revision processes as needed.

· Maintain compliance with University policies and applicable accreditation standards.

Required Qualifications

· Master's degree or higher in Physiology, Biomedical Sciences, Anatomy and Physiology, Medicine, Physician Associate Studies, or a closely related health sciences discipline.

· Experience teaching medical physiology at the graduate and/or professional level is required.

· Demonstrated expertise in human physiology and its clinical application.

· Strong communication, interpersonal, and organizational skills.

· Commitment to excellence in graduate health professions education and student success.

title: Cultural Resources Specialist/Archaeologist - NRCS ACES Program
description:
CWI Works is recruiting for a Cultural Resources Specialist / Archaeologist position within the NRCS Agriculture Conservation Experienced Services (ACES) Program which provides support to the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA). Successful candidates must meet the age criteria of being 55 years of age or older and eligible to work in the United States. Selected candidates will also be required to undergo a federal security background check.

Role and Responsibilities:

The Cultural Resources Specialist/Archaeologist will provide support to the NRCS with cultural resources activities, identification, management, and consultation related to compliance with cultural resource protection regulations. The position will perform these activities on an as-needed basis by request from NRCS.

Duties include:

  • Archival Research: Conduct archival research in repositories available in Puerto Rico, including the State Historic Preservation Office and the Institute of Puerto Rican Culture, to verify previous cultural resources surveys conducted within and adjacent to the Area of Potential Effects (APE), identify reported cultural resources within and adjacent to the APE, and determine the probability of encountering previously unknown cultural resources.
  • Cultural Resources Surveys and Fieldwork: Conduct cultural resources surface reconnaissance surveys within the APE to determine the need for systematic or random subsurface testing based on data collected regarding the proposed undertaking, potential cultural resources, interviews, and other relevant data. Implement appropriate subsurface testing strategies on the APE to corroborate the presence or absence of cultural resources.
  • Section 106 Consultation and Documentation: Use information gathered through archival research and field activities to prepare Section 106 consultations in accordance with professional standards and/or National Register of Historic Places, when delegated, prepare eligibility determinations.
  • Compliance and Technical Guidance: Collaborate with NRCS to support compliance with current local and federal laws, regulations, and policies before NRCS-sponsored undertakings are implemented. Provide guidance to field personnel and farmers regarding the identification and avoidance of cultural resources.

Qualifications and Education Requirements:

Successful candidates must meet the age criteria of being 55 years of age or older and eligible to work in the United States; able to pass a Federal Background check; MA/MS degree; Minimum of 10 years of relevant experience in a related field may be used as the acceptable work experience requirement. Experience in archaeological research, cultural resources surveys, fieldwork, and cultural resources compliance. Knowledge and experience with cultural resources identification, management, and consultation. Must possess a valid Puerto Rico Driver's License. Experience with Microsoft Office, Government applications: WebSoil Survey, Conservation Desktop, PROTRACT, SharePoint and ARCVIEW (GIS) is preferred. Training will be provided as needed/on the job. The position is based primarily with the USDA-NRCS Ecological Sciences Division Office in Mayagüez, Puerto Rico, with work also associated with the NRCS State Office in San Juan. This position requires travel throughout Puerto Rico for site visits, fieldwork, and inspections. Overnight travel may be required when conducting field activities.

Hours & Compensation:

Part-Time position working 16 hours per week $40.00 per hour, vacation and sick leave.

Physical Requirements:

The position includes both office and field work. Some work is performed in the office setting where normal safety precautions are exercised. However, the field work involves exposure to moderate risks and discomforts such as high levels of dust, low or high temperatures, animals, poisonous insects, plants, adverse weather conditions, and regular and recurring exposure to operating equipment such as 4x4 vehicles and ATVs. Enrollee is required to wear proper personal protective equipment.

title: Assistant Director of Advancement Services
description:
Job Title: Assistant Director of Advancement Services
Report To: Vice President for Advancement

Status: Full-Time, Exempt

Summary/objective

Reporting directly to the Vice President for Advancement, the Assistant Director of Advancement Services plays a key role in supporting the College’s fundraising and alumni engagement efforts. This position manages gift processing, acknowledgments, reporting, and database oversight, while also serving as a critical liaison with Finance and other campus departments. The Assistant Director exercises independent judgment in overseeing advancement operations, determining appropriate processes, ensuring compliance, and advising leadership on data integrity, reporting strategy, and donor stewardship practices.

Essential functions

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions.

Gift Processing & Donor Stewardship

  • Independently oversee and administer all gift and pledge processing functions, determining appropriate handling procedures, resolving discrepancies, and ensuring compliance with institutional and regulatory requirements.
  • Manage donor acknowledgments, ensuring timely, personalized, and appropriate recognition for every gift.
  • Oversee pledge reminders and outstanding pledge reporting.
  • Secure signatures for gift agreements and distribute final copies to donors and campus stakeholders.
  • Handwrite thank-you notes for high-level donors as part of stewardship efforts.

Data & Reporting

  • Analyze advancement data trends and independently recommend process improvements, reporting strategies, and operational efficiencies to leadership.
  • Maintain the Advancement database, including entry of gifts, donor records, attributes, and event attendance.
  • Lead ongoing data cleanup efforts, eliminating duplicate records and improving data integrity.
  • Design, generate, and interpret weekly, monthly, and annual advancement reports and provide analysis to inform leadership decision-making.
  • Provide prospect research and prepare donor profiles for VP and leadership meetings.
  • Coordinate reporting needs for the Donor Impact Report and other advancement publications.

Finance & Compliance

  • Evaluate reconciliation discrepancies, determine corrective actions, and implement process adjustments to ensure financial accuracy and compliance.
  • Manage weekly, monthly, and year-end reconciliation of all gifts with Finance.
  • Support Advancement’s role in audits as needed.
  • Maintain knowledge of gift acceptance policies and ensure compliance in processing and documentation.

Events & Campaigns

  • Support Advancement events such as the Gala and Golf & Tennis Tournament, including registration oversight, check-in, seating, and reporting.
  • Collaborate with colleagues to set up and manage GiveSmart and other third-party vendor platforms for fundraising events and campaigns.
  • Assist with planning and logistics for donor and scholarship recognition events.

Cross-Departmental Support

  • Manage online registrations and payments for Athletics summer camps, Student Engagement events, Bishop Dunn Memorial School programs, and other non-Advancement activities hosted in GiveSmart.
  • Serve as liaison for database requests from IT, Registrar, HR, Marketing, and Security to ensure records are updated accurately.
  • Provide training and support to new Advancement staff on systems and reporting.

Supervisory responsibilities

This position does not have any direct reports.

Work environment

  • Sitting: Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk or workstation.
  • Typing/Computer Use: Frequent use of a computer keyboard and mouse.
  • Vision Requirements: Ability to read and view screens for extended periods.
  • Speaking/Hearing: Regular communication with coworkers and clients in person, over the phone, or via video calls.
  • Lifting/Carrying: Occasionally lifting or moving items up to 10-15 pounds, such as office supplies, laptops, or documents.
  • Reaching/Bending: Periodic reaching for or bending to access files, supplies, or equipment.
  • Mobility: Walking short distances within the office or to meeting rooms.

Travel required

  • Local travel required to attend meetings, events, and perform job-related duties within the region.

Required education and experience

  • Bachelor’s degree required.
  • 3–5 years of relevant professional experience in advancement services, development, or a related field.
  • Demonstrated success in higher education fundraising, advancement operations, or business development preferred.
  • Strong organizational and time management skills with proven ability to prioritize effectively.
  • Excellent communication skills across multiple platforms.
  • Ability to work both independently and collaboratively to achieve institutional goals.
  • Entrepreneurial mindset with creativity, initiative, accountability, and attention to detail.

Must be authorized to work in the United States. MSMC does not sponsor employment visas at this time.

title: Senior Graphic Artist - Disney Parks & Resorts/The Disney Store
description:

title: Senior Lease and Title Analyst
description:
Role and Responsibilities

Our Senior Lease & Title Analysts (Senior LTAs) are responsible for reviewing, analyzing, and maintaining lease and title documentation to support accurate ownership records and lease obligations across our oil and gas operations. Senior LTAs work closely with the Land Administration team, internal departments, and clients to ensure data accuracy, compliance, and timely action on lease obligations.

They provide support by interpreting legal documentation such as leases, mineral deeds, assignments, title opinions, and ownership reports. Senior LTAs are expected to work independently with minimal guidance, handle more complex lease and title matters, and serve as a resource to other Lease & Title Analysts and Technicians. This position plays a critical role in managing client-owned assets and maintaining accurate records within PetroLedger's land systems.

JOB DUTIES

Lease & Title Review

  • Read, analyze, interpret, and summarize complex oil and gas leases, deeds, assignments, title opinions, and JOAs.
  • Determine and maintain mineral, royalty, working interest, NRI, and leasehold ownership records.
  • Identify title defects and coordinate curative efforts with attorneys, landmen, and stakeholders.
  • Serve as an escalation resource for complex ownership and title issues.

Land System Management & Lease Records Conversions

  • Setup and maintain lease and title data in PetroLedger’s land system; maintain accurate ownership records, acreage and tracking systems.
  • Maintain physical and digital lease files; deactivate and archive expired or released leases and contract files.
  • Support lease records conversion projects, including scoping, data migration, validation, and quality control when transitioning client data onto new land management systems.
  • Generate acreage, expiration, and obligation calendars or reports from PetroLedger’s land management system for internal and/or client use.

Ownership, Compliance & Reporting

  • Monitor expiration calendars, delay rentals, minimum royalties, and shut-in royalty payments; ensure timely compliance with all lease obligations.
  • Maintain and update leasehold ownership data as determined by title opinions and other ownership reports.
  • Prepare acreage inventory for developed and undeveloped leases as needed.
  • Assist with due diligence efforts as may be required from time to time as related to asset sales or acquisitions.

Client & Team Support

  • Maintain direct client relationships with minimal oversight; communicate effectively with clients, brokers, title attorneys and state and federal agencies on lease and title matters.
  • Collaborate with client and internal PetroLedger teams to resolve ownership or lease-related issues; respond to inquiries with professionalism and high attention to detail.
  • Provide guidance, mentorship, and technical review support to Lease & Title Analysts and Technicians.
  • Serve as subject matter resource on complex title and lease matters.

Process Improvement & General Support

  • Identify and lead opportunities for data cleanup and process improvements within client records and Lease Records procedures.
  • Participate in process improvement initiatives related to lease records, land systems, and Lease Records and Land Administration procedures.
  • Ensure compliance with PetroLedger policies and regulatory requirements.
  • Perform additional tasks or responsibilities as may be assigned by management team.

SKILLS

  • Strong understanding of oil & gas leases, contractual obligations, and state-specific regulatory considerations.
  • Familiarity with mineral and working interest ownership structures; strong understanding of legal land descriptions, royalty provisions and title concepts.
  • Demonstrated ability to exercise independent judgment on complex or ambiguous title matters.
  • Excellent analytical and organizational skills with high attention to detail.
  • Ability to manage multiple clients, assignments and competing deadlines simultaneously.
  • Experience supporting or leading lease records conversion or data migration projects preferred.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills; customer service orientation and professionalism in all interactions.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office (especially Excel) and land/accounting software platforms; Quorum or PakEnergy preferred.
  • Comfortable handling confidential ownership and financial data
  • Adaptable to in-office and remote work environments.

QUALIFICATIONS AND EDUCATION

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and experience preferred.
  • 5-8 years of land administration, lease records, or title analysis experience in oil and gas industry.
  • Experience with land systems and lease management tools is highly preferred.

Additional Notes

This job description outlines the core responsibilities of the role but is not exhaustive. Additional goals may be assigned in alignment with PetroLedger’s values and evolving needs.

The Senior Lease & Title Analyst designation reflects a higher level of experience, independent judgment, client responsibility, and technical expertise in lease records and title analysis. Senior LTAs are expected to handle more complex lease and title matters, work independently with minimal guidance, maintain direct client relationships, provide guidance to other team members, and serve as a key resource to the Lease Records Manager.

Why Join PetroLedger?

At PetroLedger, we’re more than an outsourced accounting and land services provider; we’re a collaborative partner to our clients and a growth-focused environment for our people.

What you can expect:

  • Meaningful work supporting complex oil & gas operations and client-owned assets
  • Collaborative, team-oriented culture with direct access to leadership
  • Career growth opportunities, including progression to Senior Lease & Title Analyst roles
  • Exposure to diverse clients and systems to expand your expertise
  • Flexible, hybrid work environment supporting work-life balance

Benefits

PetroLedger offers a competitive and comprehensive benefits package, including:

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Short-term and long-term disability coverage (STD & LTD)
  • Life insurance
  • Paid time off (PTO) and company holidays
  • Professional development and growth opportunities

title: Senior Wealth Advisor
description:
Senior Wealth Advisor - Greater Cleveland Area, OH (Base salary + Incentive Compensation, Remote/Hybrid option)

Position Summary

The Senior Wealth Advisor is an advanced client-facing professional responsible for leading larger, more complex, and strategically important relationships within Croghan Colonial Bank’s Wealth Management and Trust Department. The role is designed for a planning-oriented senior advisor who can integrate financial planning, tax-aware wealth strategy, estate planning coordination, investment discussions, fiduciary judgment, relationship management, business development, mentoring, and governance contribution. The position is similar in many respects to a senior or lead advisor in a planning-centric RIA, but it operates within a bank trust environment using Croghan’s fiduciary and trust capabilities. This is not a broker-dealer producer role, and securities licensing is not required for the core position unless Croghan separately assigns licensed activities through approved channels.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Lead larger, more complex, higher-risk, multi-generational, business-owner, executive, concentrated-asset, charitable, sensitive, or strategically important relationships.
  • Serve as the senior relationship presence when complexity, retention risk, fiduciary sensitivity, family dynamics, planning complexity, tax sensitivity, or reputational exposure requires advanced judgment.
  • Develop relationship strategies across family members, entities, trusts, investment accounts, fiduciary structures, banking relationships, business interests, outside advisors, and next-generation stakeholders.
  • Lead sophisticated client and professional-advisor conversations involving estate planning, wealth transfer, fiduciary obligations, liquidity needs, portfolio strategy, tax-aware coordination, retirement income, business succession, charitable planning, incapacity, family governance, and sensitive beneficiary matters.
  • Apply advanced fiduciary judgment to governing documents, discretionary decisions, conflicts, beneficiary issues, complex distributions, unusual assets, account acceptance, account reviews, policy exceptions, and documentation requirements.
  • Recognize when legal, tax, compliance, committee, executive, investment, or fiduciary specialist review is required and coordinate that review effectively.
  • Provide senior-level planning and investment judgment where authorized, including portfolio construction review, risk assessment, cash-flow needs, concentrated positions, liquidity issues, tax considerations, and implementation tradeoffs.
  • Exercise higher delegated authority where approved by bank policy and applicable governance processes.
  • Originate, lead, and convert significant new relationships consistent with Croghan’s fiduciary capabilities, client-service capacity, planning strengths, and target market.
  • Develop durable referral relationships with attorneys, CPAs, business advisors, commercial bankers, community leaders, and other centers of influence.
  • Represent Croghan through professional, community, educational, and client-facing activities that build credibility and create new relationship opportunities.
  • Mentor Wealth Advisors, Associate Wealth Advisors, and other client-facing or support professionals through case consultation, meeting preparation, debriefing, technical coaching, documentation standards, and client communication guidance.
  • Contribute to standards for client reviews, planning quality, relationship segmentation, documentation, fiduciary escalation, client communication, business development, and professional development.
  • Participate in or support fiduciary, investment, account-acceptance, risk, audit, regulatory, policy, or governance work as assigned.
  • Identify process weaknesses, client-experience gaps, training needs, technology limitations, risk trends, and growth opportunities and recommend practical improvements.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in finance, business, accounting, economics, financial planning, law, taxation, or a related discipline preferred, or equivalent relevant experience.
  • Eight to ten or more years of progressive experience in wealth management, RIA advisory work, financial planning, tax planning, estate planning, trust administration, fiduciary services, investment management, private banking, law, accounting, or a related discipline.
  • Demonstrated success independently managing complex client relationships and making high-quality decisions under fiduciary, planning, investment, service, documentation, regulatory, and reputational constraints.
  • Advanced technical competence across multiple wealth-management disciplines and the judgment to recognize when specialist, legal, tax, compliance, committee, or executive involvement is required.
  • CFP and/or CPA strongly preferred for senior candidates. JD, CTFA, CPWA, CIMA, CFA, AEP, or comparable role-relevant credentials are also highly valued depending on the candidate’s experience and assigned responsibilities.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop business, cultivate referral sources, lead major prospect opportunities, mentor others, influence without relying solely on title, and raise the quality of team decision-making.
  • Securities licensing is not required for the core Senior Wealth Advisor role unless Croghan separately assigns licensed activity through approved channels.

Desired Skills, Knowledge, Abilities and Backgrounds

  • Advanced planning-oriented professional with strong client relationship instincts and credible technical judgment.
  • Particularly attractive backgrounds include CFP, CPA, JD, CTFA, CPWA, CIMA, CFA, advanced planning, tax, estate planning, RIA lead advisor, family office, private wealth, or senior fiduciary advisory experience.
  • Able to lead business development in a relationship-based, fiduciary, planning-oriented manner rather than through transactional sales tactics.
  • Credible with attorneys, CPAs, business owners, executives, multi-generational families, bankers, and community leaders.
  • Willing to mentor others, share expertise, build team standards, and help institutionalize client relationships.
  • Ability to travel to Main Office located in Fremont, OH or other physical Croghan locations as needed

What We Offer -

  • Fair, competitive salaries evaluated against benchmarked data on a normal basis
  • Annual incentive compensation program
  • Comprehensive benefits package including Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance
  • 401(k) with a company match and additional annual contributions
  • Bank provided Group Life Insurance, Short-Term and Long-Term Disability Programs
  • Vacation, paid federal holidays, and additional PTO
  • A community-based, hometown culture
  • A collaborative environment supportive to continual growth and development

How you will make an impact:

Be The One Who Shows Up!

Children in crisis need quick action from strong, compassionate individuals dedicated to ensuring their safety. This demanding and challenging career could be your opportunity to speak for those with no voice and fight to help ensure the safety of those who cannot protect themselves. We are looking for people who are detailed-oriented, possess good decision-making skills, and can thrive in a high-pressure, fast-paced environment. When seconds count, your career decision may be the critical difference in the life of a child.

What you will do:

  • Conduct investigations of abuse, neglect, abandonment and/or special conditions for children;

  • Collect information through observation and interviews with the children, parents, relatives, and neighbors;

  • Assess danger threats, child vulnerabilities and caregiver protective capacities in order to determine whether a child is safe;

  • Arrange emergency placement for any child that cannot safely remain in their home;

  • Notify state attorney, law enforcement and child protection teams;

  • Provide families with service linkages to agency and community resources;

  • Conduct initial/ongoing child present and impending danger assessments;

  • Report indication of abuse, neglect and/or abandonment to the Florida Abuse Hotline.

title: Carrier Voice Engineer
description:
We are seeking an experienced Carrier Voice Engineer to secure, support, and optimize carrier-grade voice services across wireline, wireless, wholesale, enterprise, and interconnect environments. This role requires deep expertise in VoIP, SIP, TDM, SBC platforms, voice security, fraud mitigation, AI-enabled analytics, software systems, databases, and Tier III operational support.

The ideal candidate has hands-on experience with large-scale telecom voice platforms, SIP trunking, SS7/SIGTRAN, DDoS protection, security monitoring, data analysis, and automation within a highly available carrier network.

Key Responsibilities


  • Design, implement, and maintain security controls for carrier-grade voice platforms, including SIP infrastructure, SBCs, softswitches, media gateways, and interconnect gateways.
  • Configure, harden, and troubleshoot Session Border Controllers supporting carrier interconnects, SIP trunks, wholesale, enterprise, and customer-facing voice services.
  • Protect voice infrastructure against SIP-based attacks, toll fraud, robocalling abuse, traffic pumping, caller ID spoofing, DDoS events, and abnormal call routing behavior.
  • Monitor voice networks for security events, service-impacting issues, fraud indicators, and anomalous traffic patterns using logs, telemetry, SIEM tools, and operational dashboards.
  • Apply AI, machine learning, automation, and advanced analytics to improve fraud detection, threat identification, incident response, and operational efficiency.
  • Analyze telecom data from CDRs, SIP logs, SBC telemetry, routing systems, firewalls, DNS, SIEM platforms, fraud systems, and operational databases.
  • Support and troubleshoot software applications used for voice provisioning, fraud management, CDR processing, reporting, monitoring, service assurance, and network operations.
  • Query and analyze relational or analytics databases to support troubleshooting, reporting, fraud investigations, and security analysis.
  • Provide Tier III support for voice security incidents, SIP/SBC issues, fraud events, DDoS attacks, and complex service-impacting problems.
  • Support secure migration and ongoing protection of legacy and hybrid voice environments, including TDM, SS7, SIGTRAN, PSTN gateways, and IP-based voice platforms.
  • Maintain high availability and resiliency through secure design, geographic redundancy, failover validation, disaster recovery planning, and capacity management.
  • Maintain documentation, standards, diagrams, playbooks, and procedures; support audits, risk reviews, regulatory requirements, and security governance activities.


Required Qualifications


  • 7+ years of experience in telecom network engineering, voice engineering, network security, or carrier operations.
  • 5+ years of hands-on experience with carrier-grade VoIP, SIP, SBC, softswitch, or voice platform environments.
  • Strong knowledge of telecom voice technologies and protocols, including SIP, RTP/SRTP, TLS, SDP, DNS, SS7, SIGTRAN, ISUP, and SIP trunking.
  • Experience with carrier voice platforms such as Cisco, Metaswitch, Genband/Ribbon, NetSapiens, or comparable SBC/softswitch platforms.
  • Experience securing SIP trunks, carrier interconnects, wholesale voice, enterprise voice, and customer-facing voice services.
  • Knowledge of voice fraud patterns, telecom abuse scenarios, and mitigation techniques.
  • Experience with AI/ML, automation, scripting, or analytics used for fraud detection, anomaly detection, reporting, or network/security operations.
  • Experience working with software applications and databases used in telecom, security, fraud, provisioning, reporting, or operations environments.
  • Familiarity with tools such as SIEM platforms, firewalls, DDoS platforms, packet capture tools, CDR repositories, fraud systems, dashboards, and log analysis platforms.
  • Strong troubleshooting skills using Wireshark, tcpdump, SIP traces, SBC logs, CDR analysis, SQL queries, and platform diagnostic tools.


Preferred Qualifications


  • Experience supporting Tier 1, Tier 2, or large regional carrier voice networks.
  • Experience with STIR/SHAKEN, robocall mitigation, call authentication, or voice reputation platforms.
  • Experience with scripting, automation, data analysis, or reporting tools such as Python, SQL, Bash, PowerShell, REST APIs, Power BI, or Grafana.
  • Experience with relational or analytics databases such as Oracle, SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL, Snowflake, Databricks, Elasticsearch, or OpenSearch.
  • Familiarity with OSS/BSS, provisioning systems, service assurance platforms, fraud management systems, network inventory systems, SIEM/SOAR, or ticketing platforms.
  • Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CISM, or CCNP Security

description:

Our diverse product portfolio proudly bears the Del Monte® brand and also includes prepared fruits and vegetables, juices, beverages, snacks, and desserts - available in over 80 countries worldwide. With operations spanning more than 35 countries, we’ve proudly been nourishing families for over 135 years.


Purpose of Position:


Del Monte Foods is the Foods Division of Fresh Del Monte, a global grower, producer and marketer of fresh, value-added, and shelf-stable produce. Del Monte Foods has a powerful portfolio of brands, including the iconic Del Monte®, Contadina® and S&W®. We are currently seeking Seasonal General Production Workers. Del Monte Foods in Plover, Wisconsin is hiring Seasonal General Production Workers – Grade 2 to support our annual pack season operations. Employees in these positions may support production equipment operation, cookroom processes, sanitation, material flow, maintenance support, waste handling, warehouse coordination, quality checks, and other operational support functions throughout the facility. Positions may require overtime, weekends, flexible schedules, and extended shifts during peak production periods.


Del Monte Foods en Plover, Wisconsin está contratando Trabajadores Generales de Producción Temporales – Grado 2 para apoyar nuestras operaciones de temporada de empaque. Los empleados pueden apoyar operaciones de producción, procesos de cocimiento, saneamiento, flujo de materiales, apoyo mecánico, manejo de desperdicios, coordinación de almacén, controles de calidad y otras funciones operativas dentro de la planta. Schedules may include day or night shift assignments, overtime, weekends, and shifts up to 12 hours per day during peak production periods. Seasonal employment typically begins in June and may continue through October with opportunities for extended work through late November/early December based on operational needs and employee performance.


Accountabilities:


  • Seasonal General Production Worker – Grade 2 employees perform semi-skilled production, operational, sanitation, inspection, cookroom, mechanical support, material handling, and process support activities in a food manufacturing environment. Employees may operate equipment, monitor production processes, complete required documentation, support product flow, perform sanitation activities, assist with minor maintenance activities, and support production efficiency and food safety initiatives throughout the facility.


Employees may be assigned to various operational areas based on business needs, training, qualifications, and production demands.


Seasonal work areas may include, Cookroom operations, Retort operations, Tagging and cookroom, Capper operations, Flow control and receiving, Waste pit operations, Grounds and sanitation support, Janitorial services, Scalehouse operations, Slicer or snipper maintenance support, Plant greasing and lubrication, Product sampling and quality support.


Key Responsibilities for General Production Grade 2 Roles

Employees may perform duties in one or more operational areas, including:

  • Operate or assist with production and processing equipment
  • Monitor product flow, quality, and equipment performance
  • Complete required production, cookroom, quality, or operational documentation
  • Inspect product and packaging for defects or contamination
  • Assist with sanitation, cleanup, and waste handling operations
  • Perform minor equipment adjustments, greasing, lubrication, or mechanical support activities
  • Support material movement and operational flow throughout the facility
  • Maintain clean and organized work areas
  • Communicate operational concerns, safety hazards, or equipment issues to leadership
  • Follow GMP, food safety, quality, and workplace safety requirements

title: Project Control Analyst
description:
Geodesicx has an exciting opportunity for a Senior Project Controller (PC) to join our Project Management Office (PMO). As a PC within the project management office (PMO), you will hold a pivotal role that extends across budgeting, financial monitoring, analysis, recommendations, and training within the context of the company's projects. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in financial management, experience with budgeting, and the ability to work closely with key stakeholders (i.e., company executives, project customers, and internal teammates).

Scope of Responsibilities:

  • Develop and manage comprehensive project budgets, incorporating all costs and expected expenditures.
  • Work with project managers and other stakeholders to ensure budgets align with project scopes and objectives.
  • Implement budgeting controls and procedures to ensure adherence to financial plans.
  • Regularly monitor project expenses and compare them against the budget, identifying variances and potential issues.
  • Prepare detailed financial reports for internal stakeholders, highlighting the current financial status of projects.
  • Conduct financial analysis to identify trends, risks, and opportunities within project finances.
  • Provide actionable recommendations to improve financial performance, efficiency, and cost control on projects.
  • Assist in the financial evaluation of project proposals, forecasting future financial needs and potential returns.
  • Gain a comprehensive understanding of all functions within the PMO, including project management, procurement, risk management, and quality assurance.
  • Work collaboratively with other PMO members to ensure a holistic approach to project management and financial oversight.
  • Participate in cross-functional meetings and initiatives to contribute financial insights and perspectives.
  • Develop training materials and programs tailored to enhancing the financial management skills of junior PCs and other PMO members.
  • Mentor junior PCs, providing guidance on best practices in budgeting, financial monitoring, and analysis.
  • Facilitate knowledge sharing sessions to disseminate financial management techniques and insights across the PMO.

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in business or technical field AND Ten (10) years of experience in engineering/science management, operations research analysis or financial/cost analysis. Experience shall include collection, review, and analysis of information in order to make recommendations to stakeholders. Analyze relevant data, which may include annual revenues, employment, or expenditures. Interview managers and employees while observing their operations. Develop solutions to problems. In the course of preparing recommendations, understand the nature of the organization, the relationship it has with others in the Government, and its internal organization and culture. Prepare and solve mathematical models.
  • Strong Microsoft Excel skills. Proficiency in other financials applications is a plus.
  • Excellent analytical, strategic thinking, and problem-solving skills.
  • Effective communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to articulate financial strategies and risks to non-financial stakeholders.

Desired Qualifications:

  • Active DoD SECRET clearance or ability to obtain one.
  • A minimum of 10 years of experience in financial management, with at least 2-4 years working with various government appropriations for the Department of Defense.
  • Experience working with Business Intelligence tools to design dashboards, reporting solutions, and data integration.
  • Experience with the JAMIS accounting system.
  • Experience supporting procurement for contracts.

title: Beverage Supervisor
description:
Position Summary:

The F&B Supervisor is responsible for assisting the F&B Manager in all aspects of leading and directing the front-of-the-house team to deliver AAA Four Diamond level service. The ideal candidate will have an understanding of various cuisines while showcasing a thorough understanding of Four Diamond steps of service. Responsibilities include assisting in overseeing the performance and coordination of all work performed by the Team Members. This role requires effective leadership skills, creativity, attention to detail, and a passion for delivering an exceptional dining experience.

About Us:


At Gun Lake Casino Resort, every Team Member is an ambassador, essential to the success of our company and our culture. We expect that all Team Members take personal ownership in ensuring that everything they do is in the best interest of Gun Lake Casino Resort and embody the core values of the Seven Grandfather Teachings:

Love: Love your brothers and sisters and share with them.

Truth: Be true in everything you do. Be true to yourself and to your fellow Humans.

Respect: You must give respect if you expect respect. Respect everyone, all persons, and all the things created.

Bravery: To do what is right, even in the most difficult of times.

Honesty: Be honest in every action and provide good feelings in your heart.

Wisdom: We cherish knowledge; wisdom is used for the good of the people.

Humility: Know that you are equal to everyone else, no better, no less.

In this Role:


  • Assist the F&B Manager in setting clear expectations and provide ongoing training to ensure Team Members deliver exceptional experiences.
  • Teach and train the proper steps of service ensuring consistency in delivery. Foster a positive work environment that encourages teamwork and professional growth.
  • Evaluate, oversee, and provide coaching opportunities regarding job performance of Team Members.
  • Ensure that all Team Members are knowledgeable of and adhere to all Gun Lake Casino’s Standards, policies, and procedure for the department.
  • Assist the F&B Manager in overseeing all aspects of daily restaurant operations, including opening and closing procedures, staff scheduling, and inventory management.
  • Assist in implementing and enforcing health and safety standards to maintain a clean and safe environment for guests and staff.
  • Monitor food quality, presentation, and portion control to ensure consistency and guest satisfaction.
  • Responsible for practicing, supporting, and promoting Gun Lake Casino Resort’s “Unsurpassed Service” and AAA Four Diamond service standards at all times.
  • Maintain a strong knowledge of the menu offerings, including ingredients and preparation methods, to assist guests with menu selections and accommodate special requests.
  • Interact with guests to ensure an outstanding dining experience and promptly address any concerns or feedback
  • Assist the F&B Manager in monitoring and managing restaurant expenses, including food, beverage, supplies, and labor costs, to maximize profitability while maintaining high-quality standards.
  • Ensure compliance with ServSafe food safety and sanitation regulations, maintaining a clean and organized kitchen environment.
  • Collaborate with the culinary team to understand guest preferences, receive feedback, and adjust to enhance the overall dining experience.
  • Responsible for handling any Team Member or Guest opportunities.
  • All other duties as assigned.

Essential Qualifications:

  • Must be 21+ years of age.
  • High School Diploma or GED required.
  • At least two (2) years of food and beverage service experience in a fast-paced, specialty retail restaurant required. Casual and Fine Dining service styles preferred.
  • At least one (1) year as a supervisor having full P&L responsibility preferred.
  • Ability to speak, write, and communicate in English required.
  • Good understanding of various food, wine, spirits, and beverage knowledge with some culinary background or experience preferred.
  • Comprehensive administrative knowledge, which includes profit and loss statements, cost control, menu planning, budgeting, training, inventory control, and sanitation required.
  • Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively with Guests, Team Members, and Management in both written and verbal form.
  • Ability to help control operational costs and improve financial results.
  • Demonstrates proficiency in written business communications to effectively present data and analyses for operational improvements.
  • Must demonstrate sound judgment and maturity in his or her decision-making ability, even when dealing with difficult situations.
  • Must possess and demonstrate leadership skills and ability that will enhance and exemplify Gun Lake Casino Resort’s “Unsurpassed” Service Standards.
  • Must hold/maintain certification with handling (ServSafe) and Alcohol Awareness (TIPS) and the ability to gain/maintain training requirements from both programs.
  • Availability and willingness to work extended hours including nights, weekends, and holidays as business requires.
  • Must be able to obtain a gaming license with the Gun Lake Tribal Gaming Commission.
  • Ability to work independently with minimal direction.
  • Ability to conduct group and individual training regarding policies and procedures on an ongoing basis. Set daily, weekly, and monthly goals and opportunities and lead the unit to achieve the desired result.
  • Communicate consistently with all managers, keeping them abreast of all department activities.
  • Ensure that all Team Members adhere to all policies and procedures set forth by the department.
  • Responsible for maintaining cleanliness and sanitation standards in accordance with department policies and the Department of Health.
  • Ensure that the restaurant and equipment are in good working order to ensure a clean and hazard-free work area that complies with the Department of Health, OSHA, and Gun Lake Casino’s guidelines. Monitor, work with facilities, and document if any area is below standards or not functioning properly.


Physical Requirements:

  • Requires normal, corrective vision range, the ability to see color, and the ability to distinguish letters, numbers, and symbols.
  • Ability to read, write, and input data into the computer.
  • Ability to climb, bend, reach, walk, and stand for the duration of the shift.
  • Manual dexterity to operate job-related equipment.
  • Must be capable of lifting 50 lbs with or without assistance.
  • Requires normal sense of smell, taste, touch, and hearing.
  • Ability to sit and work on a computer for long periods of time.


Work Conditions:

Work is typically in an area which may be unusually hot, cold, and/or noisy and may contain second-hand smoke. Work may be performed in a small area with a 3 ft. wide access. Tasks performed from a sitting or non-sitting position. Performance of job duties will require standing, walking, lifting, reaching, pushing, pulling, and grasping. These tasks include the maintenance and care of assigned areas. Work may entail trained chemical usage. Constant contact with fellow Team Members and guests.

Disclaimer and Conditions of Employment:

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by persons assigned to this job. These statements are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required.

All applicants must be able to demonstrate their US work authorization during the employment verification process. The pre-employment process also requires the ability to pass a criminal background investigation, and drug test.

Indian Preference:

The Match-E-Be-Nash-She-Wish Band of Pottawatomi Indians abides by Native American preference in its hiring and employment policies.

title: Installer
description:

Insidesource keeps inventory of power and specialty tools for employee use. Management actively reviews inventory for purchase of additional tools as necessary.

Please direct any questions regarding this policy to HR.

Physical Requirements:

  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds unassisted.

description:

title: Department Lead- Hunting
description:

Assist in the sales process and ensure the customer has the best possible experience. This role is a developmental opportunity in preparation for a management position. Provide leadership to develop employee career growth within the organization. Maintain a focus on customer service to ensure sales goals are met.

  • Take charge in creating the best possible customer experience.
  • Ability to maintain overall function of the store by ensuring higher standards of compliance than is required by law.
  • Delegate tasks as needed.
  • Teach and reinforce behaviors that result in associates delivering exceptional sales and service.

  • Ability to communicate effectively, coach and train staff for growth and developing company strength.
  • Provide guidance and participate in maintaining of store appearance.
  • Facilitate change and new program implementation by effectively communicating new direction from corporate level by explanation, clarification, and implementation of new programs to gain efficiencies, increase sales and grow profits.

Assess resources to include human capital and monitor progress and communicate adjustments as needed to management. Maintain Human Resource partnerships by setting expectations for staff development; effectively manage performance and provide coaching, direction, and leadership.

  • High school diploma or GED required.
  • At least 6 months experience in retail, or other service industry.

DIRECT REPORTS


Not Applicable.

WE ARE AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER
