title: Senior Financial Reporting Analyst
description:
At Frontline Insurance, we are on a mission to Make Thing Better, and our Senior Financial Reporting Analyst plays a pivotal role in achieving this vision. We strive to provide high quality service and proactive solutions to all our customers to ensure that we are making things better for each one.


What makes us different? At Frontline Insurance, our core values – Integrity, Patriotism, Family, and Creativity – are at the heart of everything we do. We’re committed to making a difference and achieving remarkable things together. If you’re looking for a role, as a Senior Financial Reporting Analyst where you can make a meaningful impact and grow your career, your next adventure starts here!


Our Senior Financial Reporting Analyst enjoys robust benefits:

· Hybrid work schedule!

· Health & Wellness: Company-sponsored Medical, Dental, Vision, Life, and Disability Insurance (Short-Term and Long-Term).

· Financial Security: 401k Retirement Plan with a generous 9% match

· Work-Life Balance: Four weeks of PTO and Pet Insurance for your furry family members.


What you can expect as a Senior Financial Reporting Analyst:

  • Prepare accurate and timely regulatory filings, financial data calls, and related submissions required by the NAIC and state departments of insurance.
  • Coordinate reporting requirements, source data, supporting schedules, and submission deadlines for assigned regulatory deliverables.
  • Research filing instructions, definitions, and reporting changes; document conclusions and communicate reporting impacts to stakeholders.
  • Prepare consolidated GAAP financial statements, including applicable topside tax-to-GAAP, statutory-to-GAAP, intercompany, elimination, and consolidating adjustments.
  • Prepare routine and ad hoc financial and operational reporting deliverables for Executive Management and departments.
  • Lead assigned reporting deliverables from planning through completion, manage competing priorities, communicate status and risks, and escalate issues requiring management attention.
  • Train and provide technical guidance to Financial Reporting staff, serve as the first level of review for assigned work products, and provide timely feedback to support accuracy, consistency, and adherence to established reporting procedures.
  • Maintain the Financial Reporting team’s standard operating procedures, reporting calendars, checklists, templates, data dictionaries, and related process documentation.
  • Identify and implement process improvements that strengthen accuracy, timeliness, standardization, data traceability, and internal controls.
  • Analyze business process, product, accounting, regulatory, and system changes to determine reporting impacts and ensure affected reports and procedures are updated and tested.
  • Partner with Financial Systems & Reporting Assurance and other stakeholders on report development, data validation, user acceptance testing, and remediation of reporting issues.
  • Complete special projects, ad hoc reporting and analysis requests, and other day-to-day responsibilities as assigned.


What we are looking for as a Senior Financial Reporting Analyst:

  • BS or MS in Accounting or Finance
  • 3 - 5 years of prior related experience.
  • Enterprise and accounting information systems experience preferred
  • Some insurance industry experience preferred
  • Strong analytical skills and a self-starter attitude necessary.
  • Solid written and verbal communication skills.
  • Attention to detail
  • Ability to multi-task and manage time effectively on tasks with competing priority.
  • Experience working in dynamic and team environment
  • Fast learner with Interpersonal skills to develop relationship between the business and the system to enhance the appropriate flow of information.


Why work for Frontline Insurance?

At Frontline Insurance, we’re more than just a workplace – we’re a community of innovators, problem solvers, and dedicated professionals committed to our core values: Integrity, Patriotism, Family, and Creativity. We provide a collaborative, inclusive, and growth-oriented work environment where every team member can thrive.


Frontline Insurance is an equal-opportunity employer that is committed to diversity and inclusion in the workplace. We prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind based on race, color, sex, religion, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws.

description:

The Beverage Porter is responsible for providing AAA 4-Diamond customer service while assisting the team in serving food and beverages to guests and the service team. title: Junior Cloud & DevOps Engineer_Categoria protetta
description:
Vuoi far parte di un team che ogni giorno porta l'innovazione digitale nelle imprese, collabora con player di mercato italiani e stranieri e individua soluzioni 'agili' ai problemi delle aziende?

Sta pensando di candidarsi? Non aspetti, scorra verso il basso e invii la sua candidatura il prima possibile per non perdere l'opportunità.
Abbiamo l’ambizioso obiettivo di diventare il #1 in Italia nel mondo Open Source e per questo motivo siamo costantemente alla ricerca di nuovi talenti con una spiccata propensione all’innovazione, alla crescita professionale e al lavoro in team.
Metti in campo le tue skills per raggiungere insieme questo traguardo e unisciti al nostro team che lavora con i più importanti vendor tecnologici a livello mondiale, sarà per te un’opportunità unica di crescita professionale e umana.

Per EXTRAORDY- La formazione ufficiale Red Hat in Italia, consociata del Gruppo WeAreProject , ricerchiamo un/una Cloud Native Engineer.

***Partendo dai requisiti dei clienti, stesura di specifiche di progettazione conseguenti all'analisi dei requisiti, disegno ed implementazione\deployment di soluzioni ed infrastrutture basate su Kubernetes ( Red Hat Openshift ) piattaforme managed Kubernetes services offerte da hyperscaler cloud providers)
Supportare soluzioni DevOps basate sia su infrastrutture locali sia su cloud pubblici
Definire il quadro di riferimento per i PoC e relativi criteri di successo condivisi col cliente
Riportare ai team commerciale e tecnico le esigenze dei clienti ed eventuali feedback sui prodotti gestiti
Dare il proprio contributo nello sviluppo del portafoglio di soluzioni tecnologiche attinenti al proprio team
troubleshooting e risoluzione di problematiche tecniche sull’infrastruttura IT, inclusa l’analisi degli alert, l’identificazione delle cause e l’eventuale intervento per il ripristino della piena operatività dei servizi.

***Esperienze e conoscenze richieste***
Esperienza operativa e gestionale relativa ad ambienti Linux
Familiarità con concetti quali le “pipelines” CI\CD, SCM ( Software Configuration Management ) e relative piattaforme d’automazione (ad esempio Bitbucket, ArgoCD, Git Enterprise,GitLab e pipelines)
Conoscenza piattaforme container runtime (Docker, CoreOS od altro…) e relative piattaforme d’orchestrazione basate su Kubernetes/OCP
Conoscenza modelli di gestione delle risorse storage e networking in ambito Kubernetes (SDS\SDN)

***Buona\ottima conoscenza piattaforma Red Hat Openshift e relativi tools di deployment

title: Senior Software Engineer, Security and Privacy, Detection AI, Core
description:
Google's software engineers develop the next-generation technologies that change how billions of users connect, explore, and interact with information and one another. Our products need to handle information at massive scale, and extend well beyond web search. We're looking for engineers who bring fresh ideas from all areas, including information retrieval, distributed computing, large-scale system design, networking and data storage, security, artificial intelligence, natural language processing, UI design and mobile; the list goes on and is growing every day. As a software engineer, you will work on a specific project critical to Google’s needs with opportunities to switch teams and projects as you and our fast-paced business grow and evolve. We need our engineers to be versatile, display leadership qualities and be enthusiastic to take on new problems across the full-stack as we continue to push technology forward.

As a Senior Software Engineer (L5) on the detection and response AI team, you will take end-to-end ownership of different workstreams across the Detection AI space. You will operate with high autonomy, translating ambiguous organizational goals into clear technical roadmaps. You will research, identify, and lead critical problems for the team to solve. Partnering alongside a peer Tech Lead, you will carve out multi-quarter technical initiatives, establish architectural direction, and multiply the output of a talented pool of L3 and L4 engineers.

This team build multi-agent systems to autonomously triage, investigate, and remediate security events, and architect governance frameworks, evaluation pipelines, and observability dashboards for security AI. We operate key enterprise platforms (Brief, Incident Communications) orchestrating critical communications during major Alphabet incidents.

The Core team builds the technical foundation behind Google’s flagship products. We are owners and advocates for the underlying design elements, developer platforms, product components, and infrastructure at Google. These are the essential building blocks for excellent, safe, and coherent experiences for our users and drive the pace of innovation for every developer. We look across Google’s products to build central solutions, break down technical barriers and strengthen existing systems. As the Core team, we have a mandate and a unique opportunity to impact important technical decisions across the company.

  • Scope out problems in detection and response space and enable the organizational strategy to move left in the detection pipeline.
  • Set technical direction, author comprehensive design documents, and lead design reviews for complex, multi-quarter features within the team.
  • Partner closely with cross-functional peers and sister SWE teams to resolve architectural dependencies and align project timelines.
  • Guide, mentor, and delegate tasks to adjacent junior and mid-level engineers, fostering a collaborative engineering culture.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.
  • 5 years of experience with software development in one or more programming languages.
  • 3 years of experience building software for data privacy or security (e.g., identity and access management).
  • 3 years of experience testing, maintaining, or launching software products.
  • 1 year of experience with software design and architecture.

Preferred qualifications:

  • 5 years of experience with data structures and algorithms.
  • 1 year of experience in a technical leadership role.
  • Experience in security systems, artificial intelligence, and machine learning.
  • Experience as a technical lead with a proven track record of leading teams.
  • Experienced in navigating high-ambiguity environments and defining technical strategy for engineering teams.

title: Information Systems Security Officer (ISSO)
description:
Geodesicx is looking for an Information Systems Security Officer to join our team in the Charleston, SC area.

Summary

The Information Systems Security Officer (ISSO) Contractor will serve as a primary cybersecurity technical advisor and Risk Management Framework (RMF) executor in support of the Program Manager Advanced Amphibious Assault (PM AAA) Information Systems Security Manager (ISSM). This role is critical to ensuring the cybersecurity posture and successful accreditation of all systems and sub-systems on current and future United States Marine Corps (USMC) Amphibious Combat Vehicle (ACV) variants, with a specific focus on deployed Command, Control, Communications, and Computers (C4) systems.

This is an Assessment and Authorization (A&A) focused role. The candidate will steer accreditation efforts, develop comprehensive RMF documentation, and drive Authority to Operate (ATO) packages through the Department of Defense (DoD) lifecycle in accordance with the Risk Management Framework (DoDI 8510.01). The ISSO will act as the ISSM’s right hand, managing the tactical execution of the cybersecurity program, ensuring operational systems and networks remain compliant, secure, and fully accredited.

Responsibilities

  • Lead the planning, coordination, and execution of A&A events, including RMF ATO efforts for current and future PM AAA Vehicle Variants and support software.
  • Develop, review, endorse, and maintain A&A documentation System Security Plans (SSPs), Security Assessment Reports (SARs), Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms) in accordance with DoD, Department of Navy (DoN), and Marine Corps policies.
  • Upload all artifacts and maintain system information repositories within Enterprise Mission Assurance Support Service (eMASS).
  • Support periodic security events including the Annual Security Review (ASR), Independent Verification and Validation (IV&V), and Annual Federal Information Security Modernization Act (FISMA) Reviews.
  • Advise the ISSM in ensuring information ownership responsibilities and baselines are established for ACV C4 systems (including accountability, access approvals, and special handling).
  • Perform required compliance assessments for C4 systems deployed on PM AAA Family of Vehicles (FoVs); review, document, and maintain all results.
  • Assess, mitigate, track, and document vulnerabilities on the Information Technology (IT) Security POA&M.
  • Initiate protective or corrective measures required to maintain the accredited security posture of deployed C4 systems, enforcing DoD, DON, and local Privacy Act policies.

Required Skills

  • Clearance: Active U.S. Government Security Clearance (Secret or higher)
  • Citizenship: Must be a U.S. Citizen.
  • RMF Expertise: Proven, hands-on experience preparing and walking DoD RMF accreditation packages (ATOs) through the complete lifecycle in accordance with DoDI 8510.01, NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5, CNSSI 1253, and ICD 503.
  • A&A Tooling: Direct experience utilizing eMASS and/or Marine Corps Compliance and Authorization Support Tool (MCCAST) to build, track, and submit system artifacts and ATO packages.
  • Vulnerability Scanning & Compliance: Demonstrated capability implementing, verifying, and operating mandatory DoD compliance tools, specifically:
    • Assured Compliance Assessment Solution (ACAS) / Nessus
    • Security Content Automation Protocol (SCAP) Compliance Checker (SCC)
    • Host Based Security System (HBSS) / Endpoint Security Solutions (ESS)
  • STIG & IAVM: Extensive experience applying, documenting, and mitigating Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs) and Information Assurance Vulnerability Management (IAVM) notices.

Desired Skills

  • Prior experience supporting USMC System Commands (MARCORSYSCOM) or specifically Portfolio Acquisition Executive-Marine Corps (PAE-MC) / PM AAA.
  • Familiarity with the ACV platform, tactical C4 systems, or ground combat vehicle architectures.
  • Experience securing and accrediting embedded systems, tactical edge networks, and standalone tactical variants.
  • Familiarity with Marine Corps specific cybersecurity workflows (e.g., MCSC SEAL CYB Branch interactions).
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills to effectively translate complex technical vulnerabilities into executive-level risk assessments for the ISSM and Program Manager.

title: Director of Finance
description:
Position Summary:

The Director of Finance serves as a strategic, analytical, and operationally disciplined leader responsible for supporting the financial integrity, reporting accuracy, compliance, and fiscal stewardship of Gun Lake Casino Resort. This role provides leadership over key finance and accounting functions, including General Ledger Accounting, Revenue Audit, and Accounts Payable.

The Director of Finance is responsible for leading day-to-day Finance Department operations, supporting the annual operating and capital budget process, ensuring timely and accurate financial reporting, maintaining strong internal controls, and providing meaningful financial analysis that supports informed business decisions. This position partners closely with property leaders to monitor financial performance, evaluate operational results, manage expenditures within approved guidelines, and support the long-term financial and reputational success of the property.

As a senior leader within the Finance Department, this position is expected to lead with integrity, accountability, adaptability, sound judgment, and a commitment to continuous improvement. The Director of Finance promotes Gun Lake Casino Resort's "Unsurpassed Service" standards, supports Four Diamond expectations, and models the values of the Seven Grandfather Teachings while developing high-performing teams and maintaining the highest standards of confidentiality, compliance, and professional conduct.


About Us:

At Gun Lake Casino Resort, every Team Member is an ambassador, essential to the success of our company and our culture. We expect that all Team Members take personal ownership in ensuring that everything they do is in the best interest of Gun Lake Casino Resort and embody the core values of the Seven Grandfather Teachings:

Love: Love your brothers and sisters and share with them.

Truth: Be true in everything you do. Be true to yourself and to your fellow Humans.

Respect: You must give respect if you expect respect. Respect everyone, all persons, and all the things created.

Bravery: To do what is right, even in the most difficult of times.

Honesty: Be honest in every action and provide good feelings in your heart.

Wisdom: We cherish knowledge; wisdom is used for the good of the people.

Humility: Know that you are equal to everyone else, no better, no less.



In this Role:


Leadership & Strategic Partnership

  • Consistently practice, support, and promote Gun Lake Casino Resort's Four Diamond Standards and organizational values.
  • Serve as a strategic partner to the Vice President of Finance & Administration and Executive Leadership Team in developing and executing financial strategies, operational priorities, and tactical plans that support organizational objectives, sustainable growth, guest satisfaction, and long-term success.
  • Lead the day-to-day operations of the Finance Department, ensuring effective execution of departmental priorities and achievement of established goals.
  • Direct, coach, mentor, and develop the Finance leadership team, fostering a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, operational excellence, collaboration, and professional growth.
  • Demonstrate organizational agility by adapting priorities, resources, and communication to meet changing business needs, regulatory requirements, and operational demands.


Financial Planning, Analysis & Reporting

  • Lead the development, administration, and monitoring of the annual operating and capital budgets in partnership with department leaders and executive leadership.
  • Monitor departmental financial performance, analyze operating results, and partner with leaders across the organization to ensure fiscal accountability, sound decision-making, and achievement of budget objectives.
  • Develop, analyze, interpret, and communicate financial information, key performance indicators, trends, benchmarks, risks, and opportunities to support operational and strategic decision-making.
  • Ensure timely, accurate completion of month-end closing activities and all required financial reporting.
  • Provide executive leadership with accurate, timely, and meaningful financial reports, analyses, and recommendations.


Financial Operations & Compliance

  • Ensure compliance with all applicable Tribal, Federal, State, and Gaming regulatory requirements, including Minimum Internal Control Standards (MICS), internal controls, accounting standards, and organizational policies and procedures.
  • Maintain effective systems of internal controls to safeguard company assets and ensure the integrity of financial reporting.
  • Develop and maintain strong working relationships with the Gaming Commission, regulatory agencies, external auditors, financial institutions, vendors, and other external partners.
  • Coordinate and support internal and external audits while ensuring timely resolution of audit findings.


Financial Administration

  • Oversee banking relationships and treasury activities.
  • Oversee the organization's fixed asset accounting and inventory processes.
  • Support the design, implementation, and administration of compensation programs, including wages, incentive plans, commissions, and salary calculations, ensuring accuracy and compliance with approved practices.
  • Oversee business insurance administration and other financial administrative functions as assigned.


Leadership Expectations

  • Maintain the highest level of integrity, ethics, professionalism, and confidentiality regarding all financial, operational, guest, Team Member, and organizational information.
  • Build collaborative partnerships across departments to support organizational performance and achieve enterprise-wide objectives.
  • Communicate effectively with Team Members, leaders, guests, regulatory agencies, and external business partners through both written and verbal communication.
  • Maintain professional appearance and grooming standards in accordance with company policy.
  • Interact with guests in a professional, courteous manner and appropriately resolve guest concerns.
  • Foster a positive, inclusive, and team-oriented work environment that reflects the organization's culture and values.

Other Duties

title: Violence Prevention Instructor_FT
description:
Reports to: Violence Prevention Supervisor

Schedule: Monday- Friday; 37.5 hours per week; with flexibility to respond to programmatic needs Grant timeline (2 years)

FLSA Status: Non-Exempt

Salary Rate: $26

The YWCA of Western MA is dedicated to eliminating racism and empowering women. The YW provides a safe place for survivors of domestic violence and/or sexual assault. Our programs and services include crisis shelter and transitional housing for survivors and their families, counseling, SAFEPLAN court advocacy, community education, supervised visitation, and vocational training for youth. The YWCA provides services at several sites, including Holyoke, Northampton, Westfield, and our primary Springfield campus.

Expectations of all Employees

In the performance of essential and general job responsibilities, all YWCA employees are expected to:

  • Demonstrate commitment to the YWCA’s social justice mission and principles of trauma-informed work.
  • Represent the YWCA in a professional and competent manner to participants, community members, organizational partners, and others.
  • Perform quality work within program guidelines and deadlines.
  • Work effectively as a team contributor and foster a positive working environment.
  • Work independently while understanding the need for communication and coordinating work efforts with other employees and organizations.
  • Maintain professional boundaries, ethics, and strict confidentiality.

Summary

The Violence Prevention Instructor will deliver evidence-based violence prevention curricula to youth ages 12-18, who live in Hampden County. The Prevention Instructor will leverage existing YWCA partnerships with area schools and youth serving organizations while forging new partnerships to deliver the evidence-based curriculum. The Prevention Instructor will forge new partnerships through networking and relationship building with public schools, private schools, youth serving organizations and charter schools in Hampden County. By partnering with community programs the Violence Prevention Instructor will be able to engage youth in critical prevention services, equipping them with the skills and knowledge necessary to prevent exploitation in their lives.

The Violence Prevention Instructor will also organize trainings for the YWCA agency and staff in its various programs, including its emergency shelter, supportive housing program, young parent living programs, rape crisis center, community based domestic violence counseling and hotline. These staff trainings will cover how these programs, especially those that interact with youth, can embed violence prevention into their policies and procedures and their day-to-day interactions with clients.


Duties & Responsibilities

  • Deliver year-round training to youth across cities and towns located in Hampden County as instructed by Program Supervisor.
  • Plan, design, facilitate, evaluate learning, youth development, and outreach activities;
  • Assess youth participants’ healthy relationships knowledge and behaviors at the start and end of the group experience;
  • Follow quantitative and qualitative data collection procedures;
  • Adopt, adapt, facilitate, and deliver the One Love, violence prevention curriculum that educates young people about healthy and unhealthy relationships, empowering them to identify and avoid abuse and to practice healthy love;
  • Adopt, adapt, facilitate, and deliver “Bout That Life” a bystander intervention workshop designed for students of color. The program’s objective is to bring an anti-oppression perspective into sexual violence work;
  • During workshops, help participants identify key terms: victim/survivor, sexual violence, IPV, stalking, consent, bystander, oppression, privilege, intersectionality, barriers in communities of color for intervention;
  • Initiate, strengthen, and sustain collaborative working relationships with public school, community, youth serving organizations and grant partners;
  • Attend and participate in required external meetings as well as relevant school and community events;
  • Engage in Youth Advisory Board, a peer-education based leadership group for youth across Hampden County and engage youth in the H.E.R.E. Project with community organizations.
  • Plan and facilitate a large-scale annual event for youth in the community to interactively engage in violence prevention work, involving the YWCA’s Youth Advisory Board;
  • Participate in regular supervision and project meetings with the Program Supervisor and Director of Youth, Violence Prevention, and Court Support Programs as well as required agency meetings and trainings; and
  • Perform other duties as necessary.

Qualifications:

  • Must be committed to the YWCA agency mission and be able to support its vision actively and responsibly in a positive manner within the agency as well as the community;
  • Bachelor’s degree required;
  • Experience in collaborating with nonprofit organizations, public schools, and colleges;
  • Experience in working with youth in urban school settings
  • Experience in working with at risk youth
  • Understanding of both interpersonal and structural racism and bias;
  • Experience in public speaking and/or group facilitation;
  • English / Spanish language proficiency preferred;
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills; and
  • Excellent organizational and team collaboration skills
  • Crisis Management & Conflict Resolution - Ability to manage challenging situations, mediate conflicts, and provide appropriate support to youth in crisis.
  • Technological Skills Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and virtual collaboration tools (Zoom, Google Workspace). Familiarity with databases for tracking program participation and outcomes.
  • Leadership & Mentoring - Demonstrated leadership skills and ability to mentor and guide youth and/or junior staff.
  • Flexibility & Adaptability -Ability to adapt to changing priorities, work schedules, and program needs in a fast-paced environment.
  • Must have access to reliable transportation and valid driver’s license required. Must be able to cover the agency's insurance policy.


EEO STATEMENT

It is the policy of YWCA of Western Massachusetts to provide equal employment opportunity (EEO) to all persons regardless of age, color, national origin, citizenship status, physical or mental disability, race, religion, creed, gender, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, genetic information, marital status, pregnancy or maternity, status with regard to public assistance, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local law. In addition, the YWCA will provide reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities.

DISCLAIMER

The above statements are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties and skills required of employees assigned to this position.

AT-WILL EMPLOYMENT

The YWCA is an “at-will” equal opportunity employer. While the YWCA will continue to operate with care regarding employment decisions, the YWCA and its employees may terminate the employment relationship at any time and for any reason, with or without cause, and without advance notice. Exceptions include select; non-exempt positions covered under the Collective Bargaining Agreement. This position is covered under the CBA (union) and is subject to union dues.

CRIMINAL BACKGROUND CHECKS

The YWCA, in our effort to provide safety to those we serve, and to protect our agency, performs criminal offender record information (CORI) checks on all prospective employees. Final offers of employment are contingent upon receipt of an acceptable CORI report as solely determined by the YWCA.

INTRODUCTORY PERIOD

All employment at the YWCA begins with a 150-day introductory period.

title: Entry-Level Screen Printer
description:
Entry-Level Screen Printer

Location: Oklahoma City, Oklahoma
Job Type: Full-time, 40 hours per week
Classification: Hourly, non-exempt
Schedule: Monday - Thursday 6:00 am to 4:30 pm
Pay: Starting Pay Range: $15.00 - Starting pay rate will be based on demonstrable skills and experience

Build a Career in Screen Printing

Century Martial Arts is seeking a dependable, hands-on individual to join our production team as an Entry-Level Screen Printer / Screen Print Trainee.

This is a full-time training opportunity for someone interested in learning commercial screen printing and developing a specialized production skill. You will work alongside experienced screen printers while learning how to prepare screens and materials, mix inks, set up equipment, monitor print quality, and maintain an organized and safe work area.

Previous professional screen-printing experience is not required. However, successful candidates should have some relevant hands-on experience, education, training, or transferable skills that would help them succeed in a detailed production environment.

We are looking for someone with a demonstrated record of dependable attendance, punctuality, and follow-through who is interested in learning a specialized production skill and growing with the company.

Benefits and Perks

Available Immediately

  • $0-copay medical clinic for eligible non-emergency medical needs
  • Free onsite martial arts classes
  • Access to onsite workout facilities
  • Employee product discounts

Available After 90 Days

  • Affordable medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Paid time off accrual
  • Paid holidays
  • 401(k) retirement savings plan with company match
  • Company-paid life insurance
  • Company-paid short-term disability insurance
  • Elective long-term disability insurance
  • Tuition reimbursement

Eligibility requirements and plan terms may apply.

What You’ll Learn and Do

  • Assist with setting up and operating commercial screen-printing equipment.
  • Prepare screens, inks, garments, and other materials for production.
  • Measure and mix inks according to formulas and job specifications.
  • Load and position products correctly for printing.
  • Monitor print runs for color, clarity, alignment, and consistency.
  • Inspect finished products and identify smudging, misprints, or other defects.
  • Clean screens, tools, equipment, and work areas.
  • Learn basic equipment maintenance, troubleshooting, safety procedures, and quality standards.

Experience That May Help You Succeed

Relevant experience may come from professional work, school, training programs, personal projects, or hobbies, including:

  • Screen printing, printmaking, graphic arts, or visual arts
  • Commercial printing, sign production, vinyl application, embroidery, or apparel decoration
  • Manufacturing, assembly, machine operation, or production work
  • Painting, auto body work, woodworking, or other detail-oriented trades
  • Mixing colors or materials using formulas and measurements
  • Quality inspection or work involving alignment, accuracy, and color consistency
  • Using hand tools, measuring tools, or mechanical equipment

You may be a strong candidate even if you have never held the title of Screen Printer.

What We’re Looking For

  • A work history that demonstrates reliability, commitment, and consistent attendance
  • Interest in learning screen printing and developing hands-on production skills
  • Attention to detail and pride in producing accurate, high-quality work
  • Ability to listen, follow instructions, and accept coaching and learn from more experienced printers
  • Good hand-eye coordination and manual dexterity
  • Ability to recognize differences in print alignment, color, clarity, and quality
  • Basic math skills, including measuring and working with proportions
  • Basic mechanical aptitude and willingness to learn equipment setup and maintenance
  • Ability to stay organized and complete tasks within production timeframes
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team
  • Commitment to following safety procedures and maintaining a clean work area

Preferred Qualifications

One or more of the following is helpful but not required:

  • Previous screen-printing, printmaking, graphic arts, or commercial printing experience
  • Coursework, certification, or training in printing, art, design, manufacturing, or a skilled trade
  • Manufacturing, machine operation, assembly, warehouse, or production experience
  • Experience using hand tools, measuring tools, mechanical equipment, or production machinery
  • Quality control or product inspection experience
  • Personal, school, freelance, or hobby screen-printing experience

Education and Experience

  • High school diploma or GED
  • Previous screen-printing experience is helpful but not required
  • Previous manufacturing, production, machine operation, assembly, or warehouse experience is preferred
  • Equivalent combinations of education, training, hands-on projects, and relevant work experience will be considered

Physical Requirements

The employee must be able to perform the essential functions of the position, with or without reasonable accommodation. Requirements include:

  • Standing and walking for most of the workday
  • Frequent use of the hands for grasping, handling materials, and fine manipulation
  • Reaching, bending, squatting, pushing, and pulling
  • Moving or lifting materials weighing up to 45 pounds, using assistance or material-handling equipment when appropriate
  • Visual ability sufficient to inspect print alignment, clarity, color consistency, and product quality, with or without corrective lenses
  • Ability to distinguish colors when required for ink preparation and quality inspection

Work Environment

This position works in an air-conditioned production and warehouse environment. Employees may work around moving machinery and may experience light dust, printing-related odors or fumes, and occasional changes in temperature or humidity. Required personal protective equipment and job-specific safety training will be provided.

Why Join Century Martial Arts?

Century Martial Arts has supported martial artists, schools, instructors, retailers, and athletes for more than 50 years. We are owned and operated by martial artists, but our team includes people from many professional and personal backgrounds. Our employees share a commitment to quality, teamwork, customer service, and helping our customers succeed.

When you join Century, you become part of a stable, established company where you can learn new skills, grow professionally, and build a long-term career.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Century Martial Arts is an equal opportunity employer. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, skills, experience, abilities, and business needs without regard to any legally protected characteristic.


Monday - Thursday 6:00 am to 4:30 pm
40 hours per week / 80 hours per pay period

title: SVN 0152 2026 - NATIONAL LEGAL OFFICER, BOGOTA, NO-A
description:
Introducción

Established in 1951, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) is the leading intergovernmental organization in the field of migration and works closely with governmental, intergovernmental, and non-governmental partners. IOM is dedicated to promoting humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It does so by providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a workplace where all employees can thrive professionally. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture on the IOM Workplace Culture webpage.

Applications are welcome from both internal and external candidates. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those from qualified and eligible second-tier candidates during the selection process. For additional information, please refer to the internal guidance and the IOM Candidate Tier System and Internal-Equivalent Candidates.

Organizational Context and Scope

The Legal Unit provides legal advice and support to the Mission on a wide range of matters, including donor agreements, procurement and contractual arrangements, implementing partner assessments, institutional compliance, private sector partnerships, and relations with national authorities. The Unit ensures that the Mission’s activities are carried out in accordance with IOM policies, regulations, instructions and applicable legal frameworks.

Under the direct supervision of the Chief of Mission, the National Legal Officer will provide legal coordination and support services to the Mission, ensuring that requests for legal review are properly documented, processed and referred to the Office of Legal Affairs (LEG), as required

  1. Support the coordination and administrative processing of contribution agreements and related documentation, ensuring completeness and compliance with IOM procedures and facilitating review by LEG and the Regional Office, as required. Provide day-to-day guidance and task allocation to the Legal Unit Assistant, as applicable.

  2. Coordinate the submission, tracking and follow-up of legal templates and agreements requiring review and clearance by LEG in accordance with IN/099 Rev. 2 and other applicable instructions.

  3. Review supporting documentation related to procurement and implementing partner processes to ensure completeness and compliance with established IOM requirements and refer matters requiring legal determination to LEG.

  4. Prepare and coordinate legal correspondence, diplomatic communications and Note Verbales, ensuring consistency with guidance provided by LEG and relevant institutional requirements.

  5. Coordinate the review and processing of individual contractor documentation, ensuring the use of approved templates and facilitating the relevant clearance and signature processes.

  6. Compile, organize and present relevant background information and support documentation for legal matters referred to LEG.

  7. Support the coordination and administrative processing of legal matters related to partnerships, construction projects and records management, ensuring timely referral to LEG where legal review or guidance is required.

  8. Perform such other duties as may be assigned by the supervisor.

Required Qualifications and Experience

EDUCATION

  • Bachelor’s degree in law or a related field from an accredited academic institution with two years of relevant professional experience; or,
  • Master’s degree in the above-mentioned fields

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

EXPERIENCE

  • Experience supporting legal and contractual processes, including the review and administration of agreements, legal documentation and compliance with organizational procedures

  • ​​Proficient in Microsoft Office applications e.g. Word, Excel, PowerPoint, E-mail, Outlook;

  • ​Attention to detail, ability to organise paperwork in a methodical way;

  • ​Discreet, details and clients-oriented, patient and willingness to learn new things; and,

  • ​Prior work experience with international humanitarian organisations, non-government or government institutions/organisation in a multi-cultural setting is an advantage.

SKILLS

  • Excellent interpersonal skills and ability to collaborate effectively in a team-oriented environment.

  • In-depth knowledge of the broad range of migration-related subject areas addressed by the Organization.

  • Knowledge of United Nations and bilateral donor programming frameworks and requirements.

  • Teamwork and collaboration skills.

  • Flexibility and willingness to undertake new responsibilities and challenges.

  • Commitment to continuous learning and professional development.

  • Ability to review legal documentation, identify issues requiring escalation and ensure compliance with established procedures

  • Good drafting and communication skills

Languages

All IOM staff members, regardless of category, are required to be proficient in at least one of IOM’s official languages: English, French, or Spanish.

For this position:

Required

  • For this position, fluency in English and Spanish is required (oral and written).

Desirable

  • Working knowledge in French.

Proficiency in the required language(s) will be specifically assessed during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral evaluations.

Required Competencies

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

  • Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.

  • Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.

  • Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.

  • Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.

  • Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

Core Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 1

  • Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.

  • Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.

  • Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.

  • Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.

  • Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

MANAGERIAL COMPETENCIES - Behavioural indicators – ​Choose a level.​

  • Leadership: Provides a clear sense of direction, leads by example and demonstrates the ability to carry out the Organization’s vision. Assists others to realize and develop their leadership and professional potential.

  • Empowering others: Creates an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential.

  • Building Trust: Promotes shared values and creates an atmosphere of trust and honesty.

  • Strategic thinking and vision: Works strategically to realize the Organization’s goals and communicates a clear strategic direction.

  • Humility: Leads with humility and shows openness to acknowledging own shortcomings

Notes

Please refer to this link for guidance on IOM employment categories

Any offer made to the selected candidate in relation to this vacancy is subject to funding confirmation.

This selection process may be used to fill similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible for appointment to a similar position for a period of 24 months.

Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, verification of residency or visa requirements, accreditation, and security clearances.

IOM maintains a zero-tolerance policy regarding conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority, and discrimination on the grounds of gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religion, ethnic origin, or disability.

IOM does not charge any fees at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training, or any other fee). IOM does not request any information related to applicants’ bank accounts.

IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM e-Recruitment System: Apply through IOM e-Recruitment. For internal candidates, please refer to the relevant internal application procedures. This online recruitment platform also allows candidates to track the status of their application.

Late applications will not be accepted. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

For further information on career opportunities and other vacancies, please visit: IOM Careers and Job Vacancies.

description:
Job Purpose

The Senior Design Delivery Director is an executive leadership role responsible for directing and governing the end-to-end design delivery function across Retal Urban Development Company's portfolio of residential, mixed-use, hospitality, commercial, and master-planned development projects. The role ensures the successful planning, coordination, management, and delivery of all design activities from project inception through construction completion.

The Senior Design Delivery Director leads multidisciplinary design teams, manages external consultants, establishes design governance frameworks, drives value optimization, ensures compliance with regulatory requirements, and aligns design outcomes with Retal's strategic, financial, operational, and market objectives. The position serves as the key interface between executive management, development, project delivery, consultants, and key stakeholders to ensure projects are delivered efficiently, cost-effectively, and to the highest standards of quality, innovation, sustainability, and customer value.

Identify innovative solutions that improve project feasibility and financial performance.
8. Design Risk Management
Identify, assess, and mitigate design-related risks affecting cost, schedule, quality, approvals, and constructability.
Ensure proactive resolution of design conflicts and project delivery challenges.
9. Regulatory & Code Compliance
Ensure full compliance with Saudi Building Code, municipal regulations, zoning requirements, planning guidelines, and relevant industry standards.

Collaborate closely with Development, Project Delivery, Construction, Commercial, Procurement, Sales, Marketing, and Asset Management teams.

Lead the integration of sustainability, smart technologies, ESG objectives, and innovative design practices across all developments.
Promote environmentally responsible and future-ready development solutions.

Build, lead, mentor, and develop high-performing design delivery teams.
Establish talent development programs, succession planning initiatives, and performance management frameworks.
Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, excellence, and continuous improvement.

Prepare and deliver executive-level presentations, strategic reports, and project updates to senior leadership, board members, investors, and stakeholders.
Communicate portfolio performance, key risks, opportunities, and strategic recommendations.

title: Commercial Trucking Insurance Associate
description:
ABOUT SAVVITAL
At Savvital, we provide offshore staffing solutions and high-performing Virtual Professionals (VPs) designed to help modern businesses scale efficiently. Our clients don't partner with us simply to cut costs — they work with us to build capacity, eliminate operational bottlenecks, and reclaim their most valuable resource: time.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Commercial Trucking Insurance Associate at Savvital, you will support a U.S.-based commercial insurance agency with a strong focus on trucking and transportation insurance.

This is a specialized position requiring hands-on experience with commercial trucking insurance, including new business quoting, renewals, policy servicing, and carrier coordination. The ideal candidate understands the unique requirements of trucking accounts and is comfortable managing insurance applications, policy documentation, endorsements, certificates, renewals, and day-to-day account requests.

You should have a solid understanding of the U.S. commercial insurance landscape, strong attention to detail, and experience working with insurance management systems, rating platforms, and carrier portals.

New Business & Quoting

  • Obtain and compare quotes from multiple carriers.
  • Handle quoting, requoting, and follow-ups throughout the submission process.
  • Work with underwriters and carriers to obtain additional information, clarify requirements, and move submissions toward binding.
  • Ensure all applications and submissions are complete, accurate, and presented professionally.

Renewals

  • Manage the renewal process for trucking insurance accounts from initial preparation through completion.
  • Review expiring policies and identify changes in vehicles, drivers, operations, locations, coverage, or other exposures.
  • Prepare renewal submissions and obtain updated quotes when required.
  • Follow up with carriers and underwriters regarding renewal terms and requirements.
  • Communicate renewal updates and outstanding requirements to the agency team.
  • Track renewal deadlines and ensure accounts are processed on time.

Policy Servicing

  • Process day-to-day servicing requests for commercial trucking accounts.
  • Handle endorsements, policy changes, vehicle additions and removals, driver updates, and other policy transactions.
  • Issue and update Certificates of Insurance (COIs).
  • Assist with policy changes, cancellations, reinstatements, and other servicing needs.
  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date policy and client information.
  • Follow up with carriers to resolve outstanding policy and servicing requests.

Trucking Insurance Operations

  • Assist with gathering and reviewing information required for trucking submissions and renewals.
  • Ensure policy information accurately reflects the insured's current operations and exposures.
  • Identify missing or inconsistent information and follow up proactively.

Carrier & System Management

  • Submit applications, endorsements, and servicing requests through carrier portals.
  • Maintain accurate client and policy records within agency management systems.
  • Conduct regular reviews of account information to ensure records remain complete and accurate.
  • Coordinate with carriers, underwriters, and internal agency team members to resolve issues and keep accounts moving.
  • Maintain organized documentation and follow-up records for all active accounts.

Commercial Trucking Experience

  • 1+ years of hands-on experience in commercial lines insurance, with direct experience handling trucking or transportation insurance.

  • Understanding of commercial trucking insurance workflows, documentation, and underwriting requirements.

Quoting & Policy Servicing

  • Experience preparing commercial insurance submissions and obtaining quotes.
  • Experience processing endorsements, policy changes, cancellations, and renewals.
  • Experience issuing Certificates of Insurance (COIs).
  • Strong understanding of commercial policy documentation and account servicing.

Systems & Technology

  • Proactive approach to follow-ups and outstanding requirements.

title: Team Lead Retail- FT St. John's Bluff
description:
11160 Beach Blvd. Jacksonville, FL 32246

Our Philosophy: Work is the Cornerstone of Life
At Goodwill, we believe that the opportunity to work can - and does - change a person’s life. A job offers the independence that comes with a paycheck, increases self-esteem, and breaks the cycle of poverty. It’s a philosophy that we have been following in North Florida since 1940, when our local organization was founded as one of a growing number of independent non-profit affiliates of what is now Goodwill Industries International. Today, Goodwill Industries is the nation’s largest private provider of training and employment services for people with disabilities and special needs. And our local organization has grown into one of Goodwill’s top performers in placing people into employment.


Goodwill Industries of North Florida is currently seeking a Team Lead for our retail stores. The Retail Team Lead is responsible for assisting the Store Manager and Assistant Store Manager in the store’s daily operation and achievement of sales results. Under the direction of the Store and Assistant Manager helps with managing the processing of donated goods and ensure the staff is trained and that good customer/donor relations are demonstrated by example and maintained by setting high standards of customer service.

  • Greets donors and receives merchandise, providing donor with an itemized receipt, if desired.

  • Processes donated goods as outlined according to standard operation procedures.
  • Examines shoes, electrical, and mechanical merchandise and other non-clothing items to determine, appropriateness for sales floor, in accordance with established standards.
  • Must be able to handle customer or donor complaints in the absence of the Assistant or Store Manager
  • Will bring all policy violations are employee relations issues to the attention of the Assistant Manager and/or Store Manager to handle.


Education / Experience

  • Minimum of 2 years prior retail experience preferred
  • High School or Equivalent


Required Skills

  • Excellent communication and customer service skills
  • Must have by able to promote and ultimately be responsible for workplace safety
  • Proficiency with POS reporting procedures.
  • Must have reliable transportation and a valid driver’s license.
  • Energy and enthusiasm to help others.

title: Fiber I&R Technician - Ohio
description:
Fiber I&R Technician – Cortland, OH

Role Summary

The Fiber I&R Technician installs, maintains, and repairs fiber optic internet services for residential and commercial customers in Ohio. This is a full-time, W-2 position with CS Contract Solutions — you'll be employed directly by CS and deployed to work on behalf of our telecom carrier clients across your assigned region. As a field technician, you must be flexible with work locations as client project needs shift, and you'll be expected to deliver world-class quality installations along with clear product education for every customer.

Location & Travel

Primary service area(s): Cortland, OH

Training: This role requires a paid one-week training program in Bedford, NH, including travel and overnight lodging, shortly after hire.

Compensation & Pay Structure

This is a production-based pay position (per completed job), not a fixed hourly or salary rate.

Estimated annual earnings range: $104,000 – $208,000, reflecting typical to top-performing technicians once fully ramped. Specific pay details will be shared upon resume submission.

Paid training is available for all skill levels.

Why Work for CS Contract Solutions and its Family of Companies?

  • Highly competitive, production-based pay, with health, vision, and dental insurance, PTO, and 401(k).
  • CS is growing rapidly and believes in promoting from within, with many growth opportunities available.
  • Greenhorn and remedial paid training for all skill levels — we keep our axes sharp.
  • A culture that supports technicians in the field, because a supported technician is a productive technician, and a productive technician is a happy technician.
  • Incentivized competitions that reward safety and quality — a bonus for doing what's already required.

What We Are Looking For...

Someone who takes pride in doing their best every day to deliver a quality product. Individuals who anticipate customers' needs to offer them solutions for today and tomorrow. A person who listens to understand, not to respond. At CS we have a set of core values that we operate under — to work here, you will need to align with them.

  • Honesty and Integrity
  • Attitude Over Skills
  • Courage in Communications
  • The 3 E's. Effort, Energy, and Execution
  • Keep Your Axe Sharp

Role and Responsibilities

  • Install, maintain, and repair fiber optic systems — including placing aerial or buried drops and interior/exterior wiring — for residential and commercial customers.
  • Complete pre-install work orders and post-install service verification, confirming internet, phone, and (if applicable) TV service performance before leaving the job site.
  • Provide clear product education to customers to ensure satisfaction and reduce repeat visits.
  • Observe all safety rules and OSHA regulations, including safe work at heights and in confined spaces.
  • Keep scheduled customer appointments, and log work orders and time accurately using internal systems.
  • Maintain minimum acceptable metrics for Repeats, Productivity, and Completions.
  • Assist other technicians and adapt to new processes and information as the job requires.

Qualifications and Educational Requirements

  • Fiber optic internet and home phone service experience preferred; paid training provided for all skill levels.
  • Must have your own truck, van, or SUV with a ladder rack, plus your own tools and safety equipment per the company's required checklist.
  • Smartphone, laptop, and Microsoft Excel required.
  • Ability to lift up to 80 lbs unassisted.
  • Effective communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to multi-task and work as part of a team.
  • Must pass background check, MVR screen, and drug test.
  • Ability to work overtime and weekends depending on customer and client needs.

title: Senior Account Clerk – Health and Human Services
description:
This position is grant funded and employment will only be renewed based upon grant award notification.


DESCRIPTION: Under direction, performs a variety of responsible and difficult clerical tasks which involve computing, classifying, verifying, and recording numerical data and the reconciliation of accounts, records, and documents to keep sets of financial records complete and/or takes the lead over other employees in the maintenance of accounting records; does other related duties as required.
NOTE: The definition and examples of work for this title are for illustrative purposes only. A particular position using this title may not perform all duties listed in this job specification. Conversely, all duties performed on the job may not be listed.
 
EXAMPLES OF WORK:
  • Posts and processes revenue, expense, cash receipt, accounts payable, accounts receivable, and other financial transactions; assigns appropriate accounting codes and classifications and ensures transactions are recorded accurately and within the appropriate accounting period.
  • Reviews, verifies, reconciles, and processes financial documents, vouchers, reports, applications, and records for completeness, mathematical accuracy, proper accounting classification, and compliance with applicable requirements; researches and resolves discrepancies, errors, and irregularities.
  • Prepares requisitions, vouchers, adjustment vouchers, balance statements, listings of charges and payments, and other financial documents; processes changes to financial data and liquidates outstanding obligations and receivables.
  • Investigates irregular charges, billings, refunds, and delinquent accounts; maintains communication with operating units and other parties to obtain missing information, resolve discrepancies, and ensure deadlines are met.
  • Performs financial calculations, including interest charges, refunds, averages, percentages, and other data according to established formulas.
  • Maintains accounting, financial, statistical, inventory, allotment, and control records, including records of merchandise, materials, equipment, stock, quarterly and annual allotments, and outstanding obligations.
  • Establishes and maintains controls to prevent over-obligation of funds and prepares documents for computerized processing, including assigning transaction codes and verifying proper data entry.
  • Prepares routine and special reports and compiles data for budgets, financial statements, audits, and other required reporting; provides information and assistance during audits.
  • Communicates with County departments, vendors, the Superior Court of New Jersey, Administrative Office of the Courts, Office of the Attorney General, other County Prosecutors’ offices, and outside agencies regarding funding, transactions, reporting requirements, and compliance.
  • Obtains product quotes in accordance with public contracting laws and regulations; manages vendor registration and authorization, processes product orders, and receives and distributes vendor orders.
  • Prepares routine correspondence, requests missing information or documentation, responds to inquiries, and provides information by telephone and in person; reviews and adjusts routine complaints and transactions as appropriate.
  • Provides assignments, instructions, advice, and guidance to employees; may serve as a lead worker, train new employees, and occasionally supervise a designated phase of clerical activities.


EXPERIENCE: One (1) year of experience in the preparation, maintenance, and/or review and verification of financial records.


LICENSE: Appointees will be required to possess a driver's license valid in New Jersey only if the operation of a vehicle, rather than employee mobility, is necessary to perform essential duties of the position.


KNOWLEDGE AND ABILITIES:

  • Knowledge of accounting clerical methods, procedures, forms, terminology, codes, classifications, office practices, and financial recordkeeping.
  • Knowledge of basic accounting principles and arithmetic functions.
  • Ability to understand and apply accounting codes and classifications and the relationships among accounting records, documents, and transactions.
  • Ability to perform routine clerical work requiring close attention to numerical and verbal detail; review, compare, and verify data and identify discrepancies or errors.
  • Ability to perform basic arithmetic calculations, including addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, averages, and percentages, and correct computation errors.
  • Ability to understand and follow oral and written instructions and communicate effectively with employees, vendors, agencies, and the public.
  • Ability to maintain accurate records, compile financial and statistical data, and learn and utilize electronic and manual accounting and information systems.
  • Ability to lift up to 25 pounds.


RATE: $23.71 per hour, 35 hours per week

Benefits: Health, Pharmacy, and Dental Insurance, State Pension and Life Insurance, Paid Holidays, and Paid Time Off (Vacation, Sick, Personal)

Additional Voluntary Benefits: Vision Insurance, Health and Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts, Life Insurance, 457(b) Accounts, Credit Union Membership, and Tuition Reimbursement


EEOC

This title is classified and competitive through Civil Service


Must be a resident of New Jersey. Preference given to Salem County Residents.

title: Volunteer Relations Specialist I
description:
Volunteer Relations Specialist I
Job Description

Applicants must be authorized to work lawfully in the United States for NCCPA as NCCPA will not sponsor or take over sponsorship of employment visas.


As the Volunteer Relations Specialist I, you will be responsible for gathering meeting requirements, developing volunteer rosters, and collecting volunteer documentation for approximately 25-30 multi-day meetings per year. Additionally, the Specialist will provide onsite support in advance of, during, and following the close of content development in-person meetings as assigned.


Reports To: Manager of Volunteer Relations

Who We Are

National Commission on Certification of Physician Assistants (NCCPA) is the only certifying organization for physician assistants in the United States. Established as a not-for-profit organization in 1974, we are dedicated to assuring the public that board certified PAs meet established standards of clinical knowledge and cognitive skills upon entry into practice and throughout their careers. All U.S. states, the District of Columbia and the U.S. territories have decided to rely on NCCPA certification as one of the criteria for licensure or regulation of PAs.

Location: NCCPA is a hybrid work environment with our headquarters located in Johns Creek, Georgia. NCCPA has determined that the telecommuting status of this position is hybrid, which means that employees in hybrid positions are allowed to split their work hours between working remotely and working onsite at the NCCPA headquarters. The duties of this position require that the candidate report on-site to the Johns Creek headquarters, at minimum, on a weekly basis and live within the commutable distance. NCCPA has defined commutable distance as within the State of Georgia and within 85 miles of ground transportation, one-way between an employee’s primary residence and the NCCPA headquarters in Johns Creek, Georgia.


Why Work at NCCPA

We get to do meaningful work every day, and we enjoy working and having fun together! No wonder we’ve been ranked #5 out of 62 small businesses in the metro Atlanta area by the Atlanta Journal Constitution's 2025 Top Workplaces in the Region.

How Will You Make a Difference? You will…

  • Support NCCPA’s exam-related initiatives by coordinating volunteer recruitment and meeting logistics for approximately 25–30 multi-day meetings annually.
  • Establish and maintain positive, professional relationships with NCCPA’s volunteer pool to ensure a high-quality participant experience.
  • Recruit, evaluate, and propose volunteer rosters in alignment with meeting specifications and operational requirements for manager approval.
  • Facilitate clear, timely communication across internal teams to ensure volunteer needs and meeting tasking are met on schedule.
  • Utilize project tracking tools to manage recruitment activities, meeting preparation, and onsite support tasks.
  • Draft and distribute professional communications and provide phone and video conference support to volunteers.
  • Collect, review, and maintain complete volunteer participation documentation in accordance with NCCPA standards.
  • Coordinate logistical support requests including travel, catering, honoraria, and IT service needs.
  • Prepare and manage meeting materials such as welcome bags, participant folders, name tags, and tent cards.
  • Provide onsite meeting support before, during, and after content development sessions, including room setup, resets, and material collection.
  • Assist with travel logistics and provide prescheduled weekend or day-of-meeting support as needed.
  • Maintain an organized electronic library of current and recent volunteer records.
  • Collaborate with the Volunteer Relations team on Volunteer Appreciation Week and ongoing recognition efforts.
  • Support Program Educators Workshops and assist with additional departmental administrative or reporting needs as assigned.


Hard Skills You Will Have...

  • An associate’s degree.
  • A minimum of two years of professional experience in an administrative, office support, or coordination role.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Outlook, Word, and Excel.
  • Experience using project tracking or project management tools to manage tasks and deadlines.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including drafting professional correspondence.

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, and work effectively in a fast-paced environment.

  • Demonstrated ability to handle confidential and sensitive information with discretion.


Soft Skills You Will Have...

  • Excellent organizational and time-management skills with strong attention to detail.
  • A proactive, solution-oriented mindset with the ability to anticipate needs and address concerns efficiently.
  • Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills that foster collaboration and trust.
  • A positive, achievement-oriented work ethic with a commitment to professionalism.
  • Flexibility and adaptability when supporting meetings, travel logistics, and shifting priorities.
  • A collaborative approach and willingness to support team-wide initiatives.


Extra Skills You Can Bring Along

  • A bachelor’s degree.

  • Experience working with Wrike or similar project management software.

  • Familiarity with customer relationship management (CRM) tools.

  • Experience supporting meetings, events, or volunteers within a testing organization, nonprofit, or professional association environment.

  • Experience providing onsite meeting or conference support

title: Engineering Manager, Site Reliability Engineering
description:
Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) combines software and systems engineering to build and run large-scale, massively distributed, fault-tolerant systems. SRE ensures that Google Cloud's services—both our internally critical and our externally-visible systems—have reliability, uptime appropriate to customer's needs and a fast rate of improvement. Additionally SRE’s will keep an ever-watchful eye on our systems capacity and performance.

Much of our software development focuses on optimizing existing systems, building infrastructure and eliminating work through automation. On the SRE team, you’ll have the opportunity to manage the complex challenges of scale which are unique to Google Cloud, while using your expertise in coding, algorithms, complexity analysis and large-scale system design. SRE's culture of intellectual curiosity, problem solving and openness is key to its success. Our organization brings together people with a wide variety of backgrounds, experiences and perspectives. We encourage them to collaborate, think big and take risks in a blame-free environment. We promote self-direction to work on meaningful projects, while we also strive to create an environment that provides the support and mentorship needed to learn and grow.

Google’s software engineers develop the next-generation technologies that change how billions of users connect, explore, and interact with information and one another. Our Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) team combines software engineering and systems administration to build and operate some of the world's most complex distributed systems. As an SRE Manager, you will lead a team of engineers tasked with ensuring our services are fast, reliable, and available. You will balance the development of new features with the long-term health and stability of the production environment.

Behind everything our users see online is the architecture built by the Technical Infrastructure team to keep it running. From developing and maintaining our data centers to building the next generation of Google platforms, we make Google's product portfolio possible. We're proud to be our engineers' engineers and love voiding warranties by taking things apart so we can rebuild them. We keep our networks up and running, ensuring our users have the best and fastest experience possible.

  • Lead and grow a team of SREs, providing technical guidance, career development, and performance management.
  • Partner with Software Development teams to design, build, and maintain scalable and reliable services.
  • Drive the evolution of monitoring, alerting, and incident response frameworks to ensure rapid detection and resolution of production issues.
  • Implement software solutions and automation to eliminate manual tasks and improve the efficiency of systems operations. Manage Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and error budgets to balance innovation with system stability.
  • Participate in on-call rotations as a manager-escalation point and lead incident command during critical outages. Advocate a culture of engineering excellence, technical curiosity, and continuous improvement within the Sydney office.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 8 years of experience with software development in one or more programming languages.
  • 3 years of experience managing people or teams.
  • 3 years of experience leading projects.
  • 3 years of experience designing, analyzing, and troubleshooting distributed systems.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Master’s degree or PhD in Computer Science or a technical field.
  • Experience managing high-performing teams responsible for large-scale, 24/7 production systems.
  • Deep understanding of SRE principles, including error budgets, toil reduction, and capacity planning.
  • Proven track record of driving cross-functional projects and influencing architectural decisions.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to translate complex technical concepts for non-technical audiences.

title: Forge Utility  Worker - Manufacturing
description:
2nd Shift: Monday - Friday, 3:40 PM - 2:30 AM + 10% shift premium

Employee-Owned Company - Build Your Career - Premier Company

Scot Forge is a 100% employee-owned company that manufactures custom open die and rolled ring forgings. We've worked hard to develop a culture of mutual trust, respect, and accountability. Known as a great place to work for generations, many employees have spent their entire careers at Scot Forge.

We are looking for "Entry Level" candidates to join our Forge Team. Successful candidates will receive a comprehensive training program with opportunities to advance, develop skills and experience in forging. This is hot, heavy, dirty work that will challenge you - but will also reward you with great pay, benefits, and stability.

Forge Utility Responsibilities:

  • Locate material according to shop order information, verify material identify, visually examine material for defects, and transport material, scrap, and forgings throughout production area.
  • Fuel press equipment, long reaches and fork trucks as needed.
  • Verify and ensure material identity before loading furnace.
  • Fill in as forge crew member as needed.
  • Coordinate pre-forging load with Blacksmith or appropriate forge personnel.
  • Load, unload and operate furnace to maintain production schedule for forging cycles and cooling cycles in accordance with forge practice manual.
  • Grind material defects with hand grinder or overhead grinder, load and secure material.
